ChenQiu is canon

Some skill info you’ll need :

Chen Ran

Ego Extreme Realm / Extreme Realm: Chen Ran's power is described as an extreme raw-stat system rather than a complicated mechanism. His mental strength overwhelms ordinary Five-Star players; his Extreme Realm reacts extremely quickly, can reason from the knowledge/common sense available to him, and can manifest weapons (such as a sniper rifle) and enormous attacks within No-Distance. Its reasoning cannot solve a problem when his prior knowledge supplies no usable clue.

Common Sense: Chen Ran's emotions and feelings have become normalized/common sense. This makes some Superego-style mental manipulation ineffective against him. 

Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm: Chen Ran's True Self system. It is associated with normalizing emotions/feelings and a recultivation method after the usual mental-state process has been disrupted. The other True Self Players can infer its broad logic from his behaviour but cannot reconstruct the actual recultivation method merely by observing him.

Eternal Kingdom : Chen Ran's True Self skill, associated with “One” and eternity. Its demonstrated effects include dispelling skills and prohibiting skill use within its effective range. At the point shown in this arc, it can neutralize a trap/skill attack before impact and seal a Secret Chamber so that other skills cannot be used there. Future/fully sublimated use can impose a more focused Eternal Prohibition on a target or item. At Seven-Star it can break through an instance boundary; at the lower level in the current chamber it cannot simply affect a separate instance or wild space beyond those boundaries.

Eternal Kingdom sub-commands : Spacetime Prohibition isolates/prohibits spacetime effects; Shrinking Earth to an Inch applies a localized prohibition to the Secret Chamber; Wheel of Time is used in the River-of-Time struggle to manipulate the temporal/weapon state. The text shows these as different applications, not three unrelated core skills.
Chen Yang

Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique : A True Self-level mind-cultivation system. One observed function is rapid recovery/stabilization of mental energy by drawing on an external resource; the investigation links Points to quantified spirit.

Chen Yang's Soldier: An externalized mental entity/personality under Chen Yang's control. It can act or speak separately, serve as a mouthpiece, conceal what the main personality is doing, and complicate rules that count speakers/participants. Do not confuse this Soldier with Ling Chi's Ghost Path Soldier system.
Six Paths of Reincarnation Emperor Seal: Chen Yang's seal-based ability. If he is judged for a lie, the consequence falls on his
next life

, not the current body; a later judgment falls on the life after that, and so on. The skill can edit/borrow effects associated with a future incarnation and is used with Limit Imprint to copy skill effects.

Six Paths Reincarnation Ghost Seal: A distinct command in the same family. When applied to Zhang Fan, it gives a special status described as nine lives, with death affecting the next life instead of immediately killing the current self. Chen Yang fires it at Chen Ran too, but that attempt is deflected by Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom.

Celestial Sage Emperor Seal of the Great Emperor of Mount Tai: Presented as the perfected/ultimate form related to Jiang Zhe's Samsara Emperor Seal. Its name suggests authority over life/death, the Netherworld, and fortune/misfortune, but the initial activation produces no visible result.

Samsara Emperor Seal: Jiang Zhe's seal skill, described as a simplified/branch version of Chen Yang's higher-level seal system. 

Limit/Exreme Imprint: Lets Chen Yang imprint/copy skill effects, including skills Zhang Fan has devoured. Combined with the Emperor Seal and copying, it lets many Chen Yang copies carry imprinted skills. It can itself be countered/disabled by another application of Return to Simplicity; it is not an unconditionally superior True Self effect.

Reverse Future: A temporal/causal skill used to act upon or crack effects through the future. Its exact mechanics vary by combination and are not exhaustively explained here; it can be used as a countermeasure against a Secret Chamber, but fails against some effects protected by causality-severing status.

Return to Simplicity: A skill-disabling/counter effect. It can crack or suppress active skill effects, and one composite use turns Zhang Fan's skill panel grey for thirty minutes. It can also be applied back to its user, so a user may lose access to it until the skill state is reset.

Radiant Three-Kills: Chen Yang's three-move sword sequence used against Chen Ran's different mental-state manifestations. Its named moves here are Heaven and Earth One Sword, Heavenly Emperor One Sword, and Heaven's Will One Sword. The swords penetrate into No-Distance and destroy the mental constructs there; the sequence leaves Chen Ran's consciousness vulnerable to the Black Lotus possession.
Zhang Fan

Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation: Zhang Fan's dangerous True Self-level system, associated with devouring other players' skills. Skill acquisition allows him to expand an enormous library of techniques and is the basis of his potential to keep growing.

Dao Heart Demonic Seed: A parasitic mind-cultivation system. It sends strands/hairs into a target's mental energy, drains it, and grows a Black Lotus in the target's consciousness. If allowed to grow, it can consume emotional components and progressively take over the target's consciousness/system, enabling possession rather than merely controlling the body. Its spread across timelines would make it particularly dangerous.

Black Lotus: The manifestation planted by the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. It drains mental energy and can possess a host, gradually transforming the host's consciousness into the possessor's. It can be destroyed or crushed by sufficiently powerful external intervention.

Mind Follows Will: A command-type skill Zhang Fan devoured. Its key stated benefit is that he can activate/use other skill effects by thought alone without speaking the full commands. It is later described as having a passive aspect. In combination with a Straw Man, it helps him fake or survive an apparent death.

Straw Man: A decoy/substitute that can take the apparent lethal result (shown with a bullet-pierced head) while Zhang Fan survives. Its demonstrated use depends on Zhang Fan's Mind Follows Will; it is not evidence that he is literally immortal without conditions.

All Rivers Run into the Sea: Zhang Fan's skill framework for a large library of acquired effects. It appears in composite commands with Karma/Causality, Time Stop, Empathy, Holographic Perspective, Night Rain Slows Down, Return to Simplicity, and other effects.
Ling Chi

Ghost Path Soldier: A True Self system/mind-cultivation method that allows the user to externalize a controlled Soldier. A Soldier can act or speak separately and may be treated as a separate participant by a Secret Chamber's rules depending on when it came into existence. This lets Ling Chi manipulate turn order and judgments as well as fight. Maintaining an external Soldier costs spirit.

Supreme Goodness is Like Water: Ling Chi's state-of-mind/mental-attack system used with Ghost Path Soldier. The ten realms of the mind-cultivation system can yield different mental-rule attacks. Named manifestations shown in this span include:
Joy : assimilates mental attacks directed at Ling Chi.
Anger : can transform/redirect assimilated attacks into attacks against another target; in the initial test, attacks aimed at Ling Chi are redirected toward Chen Ran and strengthened.
Pleasure : a rule-based mental attack; the text says a target can break it by understanding/cracking its rule.
Sorrow: a mental-state manifestation inside No-Distance that can be targeted by a Black Lotus.
Music : a mental-rule attack manifested as soldiers singing the Songs of Chu and surrounding the target; Chen Ran reasons his way through its direction/imagery and shoots his way out.

Heavenly Punishment and Earthly Destruction (also associated with Ling Chi's Jie Mie system): Skill destruction. The demonstrated condition matters: Zhang Fan first establishes a causal bridge between Death Rewind and Ling Chi's skill. Ling Chi can then destroy Death Rewind, remove it from hundreds of An Sheng's avatars, and even break Spring and Autumn Brushwork's ability to create new teammates carrying that skill. This is not shown as a free, unconditional “erase anything at any time” ability.
Andersen Fairy Tale Squad and the Secret Chamber

Death Rewind : It is a rollback/rescue mechanism tied to a death condition; An Sheng can have teammates carry/retract it, making permanent kills difficult. In the four-way mental test it does not trigger, leading the characters to infer that ordinary mental attacks do not satisfy its trigger. Ling Chi eventually destroys it after the causal link is established.

Spring and Autumn Brushwork : An Sheng's skill for creating teammates/avatars from written “Article” content. It can create many avatars with skill loadouts, and an avatar can be removed by crossing out its article. After Ling Chi destroys the Death Rewind effect, Spring and Autumn Brushwork can still create teammates but can no longer give them Death Rewind.

Mutual Aid / Mutual Support : It is discussed alongside Spring and Autumn Brushwork as part of what sustains/constructs the Andersen Squad's Secret Chamber. Its standalone mechanics are not fully explained here.

Possession / emotion, common-sense and feeling manipulation: The Andersen Squad's broader plan includes attempts to exploit players' emotions/common sense/feelings. The arc shows these methods becoming ineffective or unreliable against Chen Ran's normalized state and the four True Self Players' counters.
Copying, causality, cards, and information-gathering skills

Causality / Karma : These are used to connect a skill's effect to a target, track causes across spaces/timelines, and make an effect reach corresponding avatars. Zhang Fan's causal link is what allows Ling Chi's skill destruction to reach Death Rewind and its copies.

Empathy : After identities are swapped, the user can receive the other person's memories. Chen Yang uses/imprints it as part of attempts to obtain Zhang Fan's cultivation information and later to steal the Ghost Path Soldier system from its moment of enlightenment.
Night Rain Slows Down : Slows the flow of time in the Secret Chamber by about ten times, as shown by the characters' watches.
Holographic Vision : Shows a remote scene (for example, the basement cell) to the user.

Holographic Perspective : Lets the user observe the Eighteenth Floor remotely. Error of Karma can corrupt/redirect what the user sees, so the apparent scene may be a decoy rather than the real target.
Supreme Card : A status/card skill associated with Du Hongnian. Different cards have different effects; the text suggests a 54-card set. Examples shown:
Two of Hearts : increases spirit tenfold.
Eight of Spades : reverses cause and effect.

Heart 8 : used to graft a cause-and-effect relationship onto Chen Yang so effects from the other Floor Masters can reach him.
The card suite also interacts with severing cause and effect, so a generic “Reverse Future” attempt does not necessarily bypass it.

Error of Karma : A causality-command skill with a passive protection: other people's skills do not directly affect its user; the effects are redirected to other people instead. It brands affected people with a lollipop mark and can redirect the consequences through slaves/other targets, disrupting Zhang Fan's remote observation/attack plan.
Guest Returns to Hometown : It has a bounce/relative-return effect that can redirect causal-linked skills to their origin. It cannot bounce a Dispel after the skill has already been dispelled.
Flowers in the Mirror, Moon in the Water : A duplication-type skill; in the demonstrated combo, mirrors appear and copies emerge from them.

Life is a Long Regret, Like Water Flowing East : Combined with Flowers in the Mirror, Moon in the Water, it yields Infinite Replication, producing countless copies rather than a limited set of duplicates.

Infinite Replication: The combination skill that allows numerous copies to exist at once. Chen Yang uses the copies with imprinted Six Paths Emperor Seal effects; in the time-travel contest, copies also go to earlier points in time to intercept Zhang Fan.

Yīn Chā Yáng Cuò: Chen Yang imprints this to mark Han Fei, then combines the mark with Du Hongnian's Two of Hearts effect so that No-Distance can act upon Han Fei. The skill's complete standalone mechanics are not expanded in this passage.
Against All Odds : Mentioned as having a causal command effect that can be cracked by Return to Simplicity. Its complete effect is not established in this range.
Temporal manipulation and River-of-Time battle skills
Wheel of Time: Du Hongnian uses it to freeze Chen Yang temporarily and also to see a foresight-like effect showing multiple Du Hongnians/future outcomes in parallel Secret Chambers.

Sui Han · Gui Yuan : In the River-of-Time battle, this causes the scene to rewind to the state before Eternal Kingdom was used and restores the Pure White Liar Killer to the Cold-Faced Youth's waist, effectively enforcing an order of events/rules.

Dao Extreme · Space-Time Reincarnation · Wheel of Time · Wheel of Space : This composite is used around time paradoxes and attempts to steal Ghost Path Soldier. It pulls participants into other spaces/temporal positions and is part of the correction/reset mechanism that prevents paradoxical events from remaining on the timeline. 
Radiant Three-Kills · Heavenly Emperor's Sword : In the River-of-Time fight, the mental attack manifests a crowd of players as a single enormous treasure sword whose particles/force are composed of their mental attacks. The attack is intercepted by Chains of Rules and then neutralized by Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Chains of Rules : Wraps/locks the manifested sword light so the attack can be contained.
Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss : Alters the No-Distance space and makes the sword light and Chains of Rules disappear/return to tranquillity.

Moonlight · Bo Luan · Return to the End : Named as one of the strongest strikes in the eleven-way River-of-Time clash.
Dao Heart Demonic Seed · Azure Dog Devouring Heaven : Also named among the eleven strongest strikes; its separate mechanics are not explained here beyond its association with the Dao Heart Demonic Seed.
General abilities and mechanics that affect how the skills work
Second Realm : A perception/analysis method that can reveal spirit bodies invisible to ordinary sight and track their movement/identity. It is repeatedly activated to identify externalized Soldiers.

Spirit Vision / Unity of Heaven and Man Mind Cultivation : A higher-order perspective. At high cultivation it frees thought from the limits of one time, space, instance, life/death state, or reincarnation, allowing the user to reason across the full River of Time. This is a cultivation/perception advantage, not simply remote eyesight.

No-Distance : A mental battlefield/space. At the True Self level it can appear as layered “worlds of the heart”; attacks can strike the opponent's internal mental-state manifestations rather than only their physical body.

Future-lie / timeline rules : These are not standalone attacks but constraints created by statements/actions and the River of Time. They determine whether a player can retract a skill, lend a Liar Killer across time, or change a future without creating a contradiction.

Soldier versus Black Lotus : Do not conflate the two. A Soldier is a controllable externalized mental persona associated with Ghost Path Soldier or Chen Yang's Three Corpses technique; a Black Lotus is a parasitic possession structure created by Dao Heart Demonic Seed.
TRUE SELF INFIGHTING

Chen Ran was the first to leave the basement. The moment he stepped through the exit, the passage behind him disappeared, confirming that the basement had only been an entrance into another secret chamber. The chamber itself was extremely simple. A chandelier hung in the center of the ceiling, illuminating only a square table and four chairs beneath it while the surrounding walls remained in darkness. Chen Ran stood against the eastern wall, while three other figures stood against the remaining walls. None of them could see the others' faces clearly, but all four could immediately sense that the situation was abnormal.

The mental fluctuations coming from the other three were stronger than anything Chen Ran had encountered from ordinary Five-Star Players. They were not merely comparable to Yue Guanshan. They were on another level entirely. The other three also sensed the same thing from Chen Ran, which was why none of them immediately moved. There was no reason to rush into an unknown confrontation when every person present possessed enough mental strength to make the first exchange dangerous.

The four then simultaneously took out cigarettes and lit them. Even this seemingly ordinary action carried a purpose. None of them used their Second Realm abilities to force a clearer perception of the others' faces. Instead, they remained in the darkness and observed only the four small points of fire moving in front of the walls. When the cigarettes burned down, the four men flicked their cigarette butts at almost exactly the same moment. All four butts collided above the table and landed in the center.
The moment they landed, their mental energies collided.

The collision immediately confirmed that the four systems were fundamentally different. One person's mental strength was immovable and heavy, like a mountain that could not be shaken. Another felt like countless blades pressing against the body. Another spread outward like silk, aggressive and parasitic. The last was like an enormous flood, continuously surging forward without any sign of exhaustion. Yet although all four had enough mental power to produce such pressure, none of them actually pulled the others into No Distance. They were probing one another without committing to a real attack.

Chen Ran then discovered another problem. His Ego Extreme Realm could normally provide him with information from the knowledge and common sense he already possessed, but in this case it gave him nothing useful. The other three seemed to have encountered the same limitation. Their mental fluctuations clearly differed from one another, so at least they could rule out the possibility that they were simply clones of the same person, but that did not answer the more important question of why four people with such similar levels of power had appeared in the same Five-Star dungeon.

After another cigarette, the person in the eastern position, Chen Ran, asked the first question: what Star level were they? All four answered that they were in a Five-Star dungeon and therefore were currently Five-Star Players. That answer immediately made the situation even stranger. A normal Five-Star Player should have possessed an overwhelming advantage against other players of the same level, especially in terms of mental strength. Yet all four people here had encountered others whose mental strength was powerful enough to rival their own.
The implication was that the dungeon had deliberately gathered people who normally should not have existed together.

The next question concerned whether they could confirm that they themselves were real people. Again, all four answered that they could. This created another contradiction. From Chen Ran's perspective, he was almost certain that he was the only genuine player among the four and that the remaining three were products of the dungeon. But there was no reason the other three would not have reached the same conclusion from their own perspectives. Each person had come from a different dungeon and therefore had their own reason for believing that they were the real one.

The Liar Killers at their waists could have been used to test this, but none of them actually used them. There was too much inconsistency in the situation. The three people facing Chen Ran possessed mental strength comparable to his own, and if they had deliberately lied, there would have to be another explanation for why the lie was possible. The safest assumption was therefore that all four answers were truthful from the perspective of the person giving them.

After another period of smoking, another question was asked. All four came from Five-Star dungeons, and in each of those dungeons, their opponents had apparently reached the point where ordinary methods could no longer kill them. Their enemies had therefore attempted to eliminate them through internal conflict, which was why each had entered this secret chamber. The others confirmed that their own circumstances were essentially identical.

That allowed them to establish the first real piece of the structure. They probably came from different points along the River of Time, but Omniscient and Omnipotent were launching precision attacks against them simultaneously from different times. Their individual perspectives made each of them appear to be the real person, because each existed normally within his own timeline. Yet from a God's-eye perspective, only one of the four could belong to the true timeline, but that still did not prove that Chen Ran was the one.

The secret chamber itself could have been constructed to kill Chen Ran, but there was another possibility: the chamber could have been constructed to kill Future Chen Ran, thereby causing Chen Ran to die indirectly. In either case, Chen Ran could be connected to the intended death without necessarily being the true-timeline player. This meant none of the four could simply identify himself as the target and work from there. They needed another method.

Chen Ran had already begun reconstructing An Sheng's strategy in his mind. An Sheng had previously tested Chen Ran's emotions and feelings and discovered that they had effectively become common sense. If ordinary deception could no longer kill Chen Ran, then the next method would have to rely on internal conflict and strategic manipulation. To construct a secret chamber capable of defeating Chen Ran in that way, An Sheng would need opponents whose abilities and reasoning could actually challenge him.
There were not many people in Hell who fit that description.

The final cigarette was flicked into the center of the table. The player in the northern position then identified himself as Chen Yang, the Fifth True Self Player, and asked the others to state their identities.

Chen Ran immediately recognized that this was the Five-Star Chen Yang, not an earlier or weakened version. He identified himself as the Tenth True Self Player. The other two followed as Zhang Fan, the Sixth True Self Player, and Ling Chi, the Seventh True Self Player.

This revelation changed the significance of everything that had happened before it. The four strongest mental fluctuations in the chamber belonged to four True Self Players whose systems had been developed independently. Their appearances were different, but their systems could be partially reconstructed simply from the qualities of their mental energy.

The first target of this reconstruction was Chen Ran. His mental strength was so powerful that the others immediately recognized a fundamental difference between his system and theirs. Chen Ran was essentially a pure stat monster. He did not appear to depend on some complicated offensive mechanism that transformed into his current strength. His underlying system itself produced an overwhelming numerical advantage.

The others therefore understood why Chen Ran was so difficult to deal with. Their own systems were more like complicated techniques: they relied on mechanisms, transformations, or special rules to produce particular effects. Chen Ran's system instead raised the fundamental parameters on which those techniques depended. Even if another player possessed a more sophisticated technique, there was little meaning to that sophistication if the difference in basic attributes became large enough.

That immediately made the others consider a more serious possibility. If Chen Ran, with his current system, were allowed to cultivate another complete system on top of those stats, the resulting combination could become even more dangerous. The three therefore instinctively regarded Chen Ran as someone who needed to be suppressed before he had the opportunity to accumulate too much additional power.

Zhang Fan was the next person they examined. His spirit did not have the heavy quality of Chen Ran's. Instead, it felt like strands of silk, aggressive and parasitic. The three could not completely identify the system, but they could already associate it with the Dao Heart Demonic Seed.

This created a temporal contradiction. Everyone had enough information to know that Zhang Fan would eventually be sealed. If his future karma had been sealed together with him, then why was Zhang Fan standing here now? The simplest explanation was that the Zhang Fan in this secret chamber came from a point in time before the sealing occurred.
That possibility was enough to make Zhang Fan suspicious that the others already understood something about his future.

Chen Yang's mental fluctuations created a different impression. His spirit was like an endless ocean, continuously surging and seemingly incapable of being exhausted. The other three initially interpreted this as another type of stat-based system, but they quickly noticed a difference between Chen Yang and Chen Ran. Chen Yang's strength seemed to depend on conversion rather than simply possessing enormous raw reserves. The question was therefore not only how much mental energy he possessed, but how that energy was obtained, how efficiently it was converted, and what process allowed him to sustain himself.

That made Chen Yang particularly dangerous in a prolonged mental battle. If the four continued fighting without interruption, he appeared to be the one most likely to survive because he could continue recovering while the others gradually exhausted themselves.
The three naturally developed the same thought: Chen Yang should be killed first.
Chen Yang, noticing the killing intent directed toward him, was already calculating the same problem from the opposite side.

Ling Chi was the fourth. His mental attack was the purest of the four and produced a sharp sensation even without an actual attack being launched. The others could not immediately determine how his system worked. What they could determine was that nearly everything about Ling Chi's system was oriented toward combat. His killing intent was also the heaviest among them, which meant that if a fight broke out, he was unlikely to hesitate simply because the other three were True Self Players.

At that point, all four had independently reached the same basic conclusion: none of the others could be allowed to grow unchecked, and the safest choice in a real infighting situation would be to remove the others before they could reveal their full systems.
They simultaneously reached for their Liar Killers.

The other three immediately stopped when Chen Ran moved. They all possessed information about the Tenth True Self Player being the "One" and therefore the embodiment of eternity. His skill should naturally be capable of suppressing or becoming the nemesis of other skills. But before anyone actually fired, the three suddenly threw their lighters toward Chen Ran.
Chen Ran caught all three without difficulty and placed them into his pocket.

This small action caused the other three to reassess him. He had not reacted with the emotional hesitation one would expect from a normal person. His response was purely conditioned by his Self State of Mind. From this, they quickly realized that Chen Ran's current state did not simply represent an ordinary Ego. His emotions and feelings had been normalized to the point that he remained permanently within the Self State of Mind.
That deduction led directly to the underlying logic of the Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm.

The other three realized that if emotions and feelings had been normalized, then Chen Ran could no longer simply return to the normal process through which ordinary players cultivated the Self, Superego, and other states. The existence of the Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm therefore implied a method of recultivation. The three could identify the general logic of the system, but they could not reproduce the actual method because the recultivation process itself was something they had never experienced.

Chen Ran noticed that they had deduced this much after only a brief encounter. He also understood why they had reached the conclusion so quickly. The evidence was already visible in the way he behaved; they simply needed to connect the behavior to the structure of his state of mind.
The four then resumed their mutual probing, this time turning toward Chen Yang. They attacked his mental energy simultaneously, observing exactly what happened when his spirit was damaged.
Chen Yang's spirit initially declined rapidly. After approximately a minute, however, the rate of decrease stopped. His mental strength stabilized even though the three continued attacking him.

This established that Chen Yang was indeed absorbing some form of energy. But the energy being absorbed was not the spirit of the three people attacking him. They could feel that their own spirit was continuing to be expended while Chen Yang's reserve recovered through another source.
The three began considering Points.

If a living player could be regarded as a spiritual existence, and if death followed by the creation of a dungeon eventually turned the player's remaining existence into Points, then Points could essentially represent a quantified form of spirit. That would explain why Chen Yang could use Points as a resource for his system. Yet when the three examined their own Liar Killers, they found no method of directly extracting the Points stored inside them.
Chen Yang, meanwhile, recognized what they were trying to do. The others were approaching the underlying logic of his Three Corpses Transformation Technique after observing it only once.
The next experiment focused on Ling Chi.

The four recovered their spirits and then launched another round of mental probing. This time, Ling Chi's system immediately produced a contradiction. Chen Ran found himself being attacked by Skeleton Soldiers whose strength was far greater than the mental attacks Ling Chi was directing toward Zhang Fan and Chen Yang. The discrepancy was too large to be accidental.

When Chen Yang and Zhang Fan withdrew their mental energy, the number of Skeleton Soldiers attacking Chen Ran immediately decreased. This allowed them to reconstruct the interaction. Ling Chi's [Joy] was capable of assimilating the mental attacks directed toward him. Those assimilated attacks could then be affected by [Anger], transforming the original attack into a stronger attack against someone else.

This was no longer a matter of strengthening an ordinary mental attack, as Ling Chi's system could use different states of mind as different forms of mental-rule attacks. The three types of Heart Cultivation contained multiple realms, and each realm could therefore correspond to a different effect. [Pleasure], for example, had already demonstrated a rule-based quality when Yue Guanshan previously encountered it. Ling Chi's system could similarly include techniques that strengthened attacks, redirected an opponent's power, or imposed direct rules on the mental battlefield.
That explained why Ling Chi's system was difficult to predict. It was not centered around one fixed offensive mechanism. Its output changed depending on the state of mind being used.

The others attempted to reproduce the same process by enchanting their own mental attacks, but they could not immediately do so. Ling Chi, however, had also learned something from the experiment: Chen Ran's mental energy was not being assimilated in the same way as the others. Chen Ran's pure stat-based system created a fundamental difference in the underlying logic of his mental energy, making it difficult for Ling Chi's [Joy] to treat it as an ordinary mental attack.
The probing then turned toward Zhang Fan.

Zhang Fan released several strands of mental energy that attached themselves to the other three like hairs. At first, the effect was so weak that it was almost impossible to notice. The strands slowly burrowed into their mental energy and began draining it.

The three watched carefully and discovered that the hairs eventually converged into tiny Black Lotuses within their minds. The lotuses did not attack immediately. They simply remained planted there, quietly absorbing mental energy.

Zhang Fan then withdrew his mental attack and observed the result. When he released his spirit again, the Black Lotuses responded to the renewed connection and began absorbing energy at a much faster rate.

Inside Chen Ran's No Distance, the Black Lotus then changed targets. It attached itself to the version of Chen Ran representing [Sorrow]. The moment this happened, the version of Chen Ran began to fade, while his appearance gradually transformed into Zhang Fan's.

Chen Ran immediately understood that allowing the process to continue would be dangerous. Within the Self Extreme State he created a sniper rifle and destroyed the Black Lotus, turning it into mental energy. He then forced the remaining energy out of No Distance and repeatedly checked himself before confirming that Zhang Fan's influence had been completely expelled.
Chen Yang and Ling Chi went through the same process.

The experiment was enough to reveal the basic danger of the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. Zhang Fan's ability was not simply draining mental energy. It could gradually replace the target's own consciousness.

If the Black Lotus were allowed to continue developing, it could progressively consume the target's Joy, Anger, Sorrow, Pleasure, and other emotional components, then continue moving through the Unity of Heaven and Man, the Self, Ego, Superego, and ultimately the True Self. The target's No Distance could also be consumed as part of the same process.

At that point, there would no longer be a question of simply controlling someone's body, because Zhang Fan could effectively control the entire system of another player and turn that person into his puppet.

The implications were far beyond the three people standing in the chamber. Zhang Fan also possessed the ability to devour skills. If he eventually obtained a space-time type ability and could spread the Dao Heart Demonic Seed across different timelines, then nobody could be certain which allies were still acting under their own will. The possibility extended to people like Qiu Yinong, Lin Xuan, Jiang Zhe, Loss of Self triggers, opponents, and even the Floor Masters of the two major alliances.

This was why his future sealing could no longer be interpreted as an ordinary defeat. If Zhang Fan were allowed to reach the Half-Step True Self Heart Realm while fully mastering the Dao Heart Demonic Seed, players below that realm would have almost no means of resisting the possession. At the same time, his ability to devour skills would allow him to expand the problem from individual consciousnesses to entire systems.

Once the four understood this, there was little reason to continue hiding their systems from one another. They had already reached the limit of what could be deduced from observation alone. Without actual information exchange, they could not reconstruct the remaining mechanisms.
Chen Yang then looked directly at Chen Ran.

The interaction between the two revealed another problem. Chen Yang explained that before his death, he had already deduced that a place such as Hell should exist. He had therefore created nine personalities and arranged for them to kill one another. The surviving personality had ultimately been influenced by Chen Yang and chosen to end itself, meaning that his consciousness could theoretically be recovered in Hell.

Chen Ran immediately noticed a discrepancy in the number. Chen Yang had created nine personalities, but the information currently available to him suggested that someone might have tampered with that structure. Chen Yang did not seem particularly concerned. His priority was elsewhere: he believed that the personalities he had left behind should be able to recover Chen Ran from Hell.

When Chen Ran asked whether Chen Yang had really been sent back several hundred years, Chen Yang confirmed it. From his personal perspective, however, he had only been in Hell for five days. That made his Five-Star cultivation speed abnormal, especially because he claimed that if there had not been complications involving his Superego Loss of Self triggers, he might already have reached the Superego State of Mind.

The condition he described for that advancement was particularly revealing. Chen Yang needed to kill a law-abiding good citizen in order to satisfy the requirements of his Loss of Self. He immediately clarified that he was not planning to kill Zhang Fan or Ling Chi. His intention was to rank up first and ideally return to the world of the living afterward.
Then Chen Ran asked what he intended to do if he returned.
Chen Yang answered that he wanted to kill Chen Ran.

His reasoning was based on what he called established fate. According to his deductions, Chen Ran was destined to die through an accident involving a truck. Chen Yang considered it preferable to kill Chen Ran himself because he would then be killing someone who was already destined to die rather than deliberately changing the fate of an innocent person.
He even took out a Party notebook and asked Chen Ran to explain exactly how he had been killed so that he could reconstruct the situation when he returned to the living world.

Chen Ran tried to point out the obvious problem. If Chen Yang chose not to kill him, then perhaps the original accident would not happen and Chen Ran would survive. Chen Yang responded by reframing the issue around karma. If he did not kill Chen Ran, then another cause would eventually take Chen Ran's place.

Chen Yang had investigated the original truck driver and discovered that the man had not even left his home on the day the accident supposedly occurred. Someone had interfered with the karmic line and replaced him.
That someone was Chen Yang himself.

The game was called [Lie]. Four people would take turns speaking, and they could say anything. If everyone told the truth, everyone would be obliterated. The rules looked simple, but they were extremely difficult precisely because the four participants were not ordinary players. The game had originally been designed as a Five-Star dungeon because ordinary players could be killed through conventional means. These four could not. The only realistic method of eliminating them was to make them kill one another. Therefore, the stronger the participants were, the harder the game became. Chen Yang possessed the fastest growth in Hell. Chen Ran was the "One" among the ten True Self Players and possessed the ability to restart Hell. Zhang Fan had once been a beggar with almost no conventional knowledge, yet he had survived long enough that even the True Self Players feared him. Ling Ling Chi possessed so little recorded history that his existence was difficult to trace, but he had launched a war under Omniscient and Omnipotent's rule and subsequently survived by hiding among the Death Row Inmates. The scarcity of records surrounding him was therefore not evidence that he was weaker than the Ninth True Self Player. The Ninth had failed in her attempt to achieve her objective and had resorted to hiding within other timelines, whereas Ling Chi had remained among the Death Row Inmates without the Omniscient and Omnipotent being able to eliminate him. From this comparison, Chen Yang concluded that Ling Chi was stronger than the Ninth, at least in the relevant contest against the Omniscient and Omnipotent; his position among the Death Row Inmates represented an achievement that his limited historical record concealed rather than a sign of inferiority.

Zhang Fan's behavior during the previous sequence then became suspicious: he possessed [Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation] and understood skill combinations and devouring better than almost anyone.
