That was irrational if his objective had simply been to win the battle. Therefore, the more likely explanation was that Zhang Fan had deliberately allowed Chen Yang to see enough of his abilities to determine who belonged to the true timeline. The benefit of doing so was not the identity itself. If Zhang Fan or Ling Chi were the true-timeline player, Chen Yang would target them anyway, so revealing their identity would change little. But if Chen Ran were the true-timeline player, Chen Yang would have a reason to protect him because Chen Ran's death could cause the Chen Yang on the true timeline to suffer as well. Chen Yang might appear to target everyone equally while secretly refusing to kill Chen Ran. That weakness could then be exploited.

Zhang Fan's structure therefore gave each person a different objective , as Zhang Fan and Ling Chi needed to target Chen Ran, while Chen Yang and Chen Ran would consequently be forced into cooperation. But there was an obvious contradiction: if Chen Ran really belonged to the true timeline, then his objective would also be to kill all three of them, including Chen Yang. The remaining uncertainty was whether Chen Ran himself knew that he was the true-timeline player. If he did, Chen Yang would be the natural first target. Zhang Fan therefore stated that extremely confident people often died because of their own confidence. Chen Yang had seen through the general direction of Zhang Fan's plan, but he had still chosen to imprint Zhang Fan's skills because he believed his five winning moves would allow him to remain on the true timeline. His confidence in the plan had caused him to accept the risk.

Chen Yang did not become shaken by this interpretation. Instead, he explained that he had never truly lost before. He had been at the top in almost everything during his previous life and had therefore developed a "Heart of Certain Victory." This created a peculiar psychological effect. Someone who had won repeatedly accumulated enough momentum that others became reluctant to believe they were holding a bad hand. Even if such a person possessed a terrible hand in a gambling game, the opponent might still assume that the repeated winner possessed something better. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi therefore instinctively suspected that Chen Yang must still possess another solution. This itself became part of the infighting. Once they believed Chen Yang might have another hidden card, every subsequent action he made became difficult to interpret.

Chen Yang then deliberately proposed another possibility. If Chen Ran really were the player from the true timeline, perhaps Chen Ran's death would not necessarily be harmful to him. Perhaps the Ninth would simply allow Chen Yang to replace Chen Ran, creating a new Absolute Defense together with two Chen Yangs. Zhang Fan did not answer and smiled. This was a familiar tactic: by deliberately introducing multiple possible explanations, a player could prevent the opponent from determining which explanation was the actual objective. Chen Ran, meanwhile, watched the two brothers quietly. In a game of internal strife, influencing the opponent's thoughts was often more important than directly attacking them. Ling Chi therefore used his spirit to lock onto Chen Ran and Chen Yang, while Zhang Fan also locked onto them to prevent either brother from establishing the dangerous Future Lie that they would only tell the truth later. If either brother successfully established that Future Lie, Zhang Fan and Ling Chi could be forced into a situation where neither could safely judge him.

The first round of the Lie game therefore had to be analyzed from the rules rather than from ordinary assumptions. At least one person had to tell a Lie in every round, because if all four people told the truth, the chamber would immediately obliterate everyone. However, this did not mean that the liar would necessarily be the one who died. The first speaker had to judge the other three after the round ended, and a wrong judgment could itself become dangerous.

Suppose the speaking order was Chen Ran, Chen Yang, Ling Chi, and Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi was the only person who lied. Chen Ran would not know which of the other three had lied, so he would have to choose a judgment that preserved his own survival. He could accuse Chen Yang while declaring Ling Chi and Zhang Fan truthful. Ling Chi would know that the judgment was wrong, but he still could not safely judge Chen Ran in return, because doing so would reveal that Ling Chi himself had lied. Chen Yang was in a similar position. Even if he had told the truth and Chen Ran had wrongly judged him as lying, killing Chen Ran would leave Chen Yang facing Zhang Fan and Ling Chi alone, which was an extremely dangerous outcome. The result was that both the liar and the person who made the wrong judgment could survive, depending on what they knew about the future sequence.

This was why the Future Lie of "I will only speak the truth later" was so dangerous. A player who established it could potentially survive until only two people remained, because the other players could no longer safely judge him. The relationship between Chen Ran and Chen Yang made this even more dangerous. They were brothers and were capable of protecting one another, while Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had no such relationship. If either brother established the Future Lie, the other could potentially cooperate with him and force the other two into a losing sequence.

Chen Yang's ability to sacrifice himself made the situation even worse. If Chen Yang established the Future Lie, Chen Ran could safely continue telling the truth, leaving Zhang Fan or Ling Chi as the only possible liar. Chen Yang could then make a judgment against one of them. If that judgment failed, it would identify the other as the liar, allowing Chen Ran to judge that person afterward. Chen Yang could therefore sacrifice himself while ensuring that one of Zhang Fan or Ling Chi died with him. The result could leave Zhang Fan and Chen Ran as the final two, after which the rules would force Zhang Fan to make a judgment against Chen Ran. Because Chen Ran had not lied, that judgment would fail and Chen Ran would eventually become the survivor.

Zhang Fan and Ling Chi therefore did not need to believe that Chen Yang would actually choose to sacrifice himself. The possibility alone was enough to make the Future Lie unacceptable. Before the preparation period ended, the four therefore established several restrictions. Chen Ran and Chen Yang could not use shared memories, common experiences, codes, or secret languages from before death. The Future Lie promising to tell the truth or Lie later was forbidden. No-Distance was forbidden, suggestive movements were forbidden, and nobody was allowed to directly state whether a previous statement had been true or false. These restrictions did not solve the game, they just prevented the players from deciding the entire outcome through a single loophole before the actual speaking sequence began.

When the preparation ended, the four received name tags. Zhang Fan became Li Chengqian, Chen Yang became Li Chengze, Ling Chi became Li Chengqing, and Chen Ran became Li Chengman. According to the setting, Li Chengqian was the Crown Prince, and Zhang Fan was the first person to speak. He began by telling two stories from Feng Menglong's [Stories to Warn the World], one involving Wang Meiniang and Qin Zhong and the other involving Du Shiniang and Li Jia. He explained why the two women reached different endings despite both involving men spending their savings to redeem them. His conclusion was that Wang Meiniang and Qin Zhong succeeded because Wang Meiniang also contributed and did not force Qin Zhong to act independently, while Du Shiniang's tragedy occurred because she forced Li Jia to choose between her and his future. Zhang Fan then ended his speech.

The other three immediately began analyzing the hidden meaning. On the surface, Zhang Fan's statements about the stories were not lies. But his opening sentence created an unusual problem. He had said that he would analyze stories from "his era" and assumed that the others had heard of them. [Stories to Warn the World] was completed in 1624, while the Ming Dynasty fell in 1644. Ling Chi had been a general near the end of the Ming Dynasty, meaning he was likely born around or before the completion of the book. Zhang Fan was the Sixth True Self Player while Ling Chi was the Seventh, so Zhang Fan should have been born before Ling Chi. If Zhang Fan and Ling Chi were separated by the normal decades or centuries between True Self Players, then Zhang Fan's statement was suspicious. Yet the two stories themselves had backgrounds from different historical periods. [Du Shiniang Sinks Her Jewel Box in Anger] was set during the Wanli era of the Ming Dynasty, while [The Oil Seller Wins the Courtesan] was set during the Jingkang Incident of the Northern Song. If Zhang Fan had been born during one of those periods, his claim that the stories were from his era could actually be true. Thus, the wording contained a deliberate ambiguity that appeared false on the surface while potentially becoming true under another interpretation.

The hidden meaning of Zhang Fan's speech was therefore not simply the historical accuracy of the two stories. Wang Meiniang and Qin Zhong represented a relationship in which the man followed the woman's wishes instead of independently forcing his own decision. Zhang Fan was using that structure as a message to Ling Chi: the two of them were cooperating, so neither should plot against the other. If they both told the truth, the game would remain manageable. Ling Chi then had to respond to that hidden message. His own story described his childhood with Ling Jū and Ling Runsheng. His father insisted that a general needed ferocity and that this ferocity came from the heart, but he deliberately kept Ling Chi away from the battlefield. Ling Chi argued that he possessed superior horsemanship, spear skills, and military strategy, but his father refused to acknowledge him as part of the family genealogy.

The story continued by explaining Ling Jū's concept of "Animality." A veteran soldier possessed a certain ferocity developed through experience, but Ling Jū considered this ferocity to be man's primitive Animality controlled by Reason. He demonstrated the concept through a cat that reacted violently to his presence. Ling Chi then analyzed the idea rather than simply accepting his father's explanation. A cat had no Reason, so its Animality was instinctive. Humans possessed Reason, which could control Animality. Ling Chi remembered that when he and his family had encountered danger on the road, the hair on his body had stood up before the bandits appeared. He therefore reasoned that Animality was connected to environmental danger and might be triggered by controlling the environment. His father immediately became angry and struck him, ordering him to kneel in the ancestral hall.

Inside the ancestral hall, Ling Jū finally revealed why he had treated Ling Chi differently. The Ming Dynasty's situation was already beyond recovery, and Ling Jū believed that the historical torrent could not be stopped. Ling Runsheng was his eldest son, so he was expected to die on the battlefield alongside his father. Ling Chi was different. Ling Jū had deliberately kept him out of the genealogy and raised him among the guards because he wanted Ling Chi to survive the fall of the dynasty. If the country collapsed, Ling Chi could change his name, take the family members away, and continue living. Ling Chi's desire to die alongside his father and brother was therefore not an act of filial piety from his father's perspective. It was a selfish choice that would also drag the soldiers' families and other dependents into the same death. Ling Jū forced Ling Chi to promise that if he and Ling Runsheng went to war, Ling Chi would instead escort the military families to safety.

The historical information complicated the story. Ling Jū and Ling Runsheng corresponded to actual historical records, including Ling Jū's service under the Southern Ming and his eventual refusal to surrender. Ling Runsheng also died with him. What remained uncertain was whether a son named Ling Chi had actually existed and been excluded from the genealogy. The theory of Animality also appeared to fit Jie Mie's mental attack methods. More importantly, Ling Chi's story suggested that he had never fought on a battlefield or killed anyone, which was compatible with the previous-life conditions of a True Self Player. However, Chen Yang had received information that Ling Chi had been a general at the end of the Ming Dynasty, while Ling Chi's own story suggested that he had been deliberately kept away from military combat. One possible explanation was that Ling Chi later returned to the battlefield after escorting the military families to safety. But if he had done so, he would have killed people, which would conflict with the conditions associated with becoming a True Self Player. Another possibility was that "general" had merely been an honorary title arranged by Ling Jū so that Ling Chi could move among the military families without attracting suspicion. Therefore, Ling Chi's story could appear truthful while still containing a hidden lie.

This placed pressure on Chen Ran. Zhang Fan's story had conveyed that he would tell the truth, and Ling Chi's story had conveyed the same thing. If Chen Ran also declared that he would tell the truth, then all four could potentially be obliterated. Yet Ling Chi also understood that Chen Ran could use deterrence. If the other three dared to tell the truth, Chen Ran could simply tell the truth as well, making their survival depend on whether one of them was willing to lie. Thus, Zhang Fan and Chen Yang's apparent commitment to telling the truth placed Chen Ran under pressure, while Chen Ran's own threat of mutual destruction placed pressure back on them.

The deeper problem was the identity of the liar. Ling Chi reasoned that Zhang Fan would be the next person to make the judgment and therefore had to choose his words carefully. If Zhang Fan declared that Chen Yang was truthful, Ling Chi was truthful, and Chen Ran was truthful, then if Chen Yang had lied, Chen Yang would kill Zhang Fan, Ling Chi would kill Chen Yang, and only Ling Chi and Chen Ran would remain. Because of the speaking order, Ling Chi would then obtain the first judgment and could still be trapped by Chen Ran. Therefore, Zhang Fan could not safely make that judgment. The safer statement was that Chen Yang was lying while Ling Chi and Chen Ran were telling the truth. Ling Chi then simulated the three possible actual combinations behind that statement. One possibility was that Chen Yang lied and the other two told the truth. Another was that Chen Yang and Ling Chi told the truth while Chen Ran lied. The third was that Chen Yang and Chen Ran told the truth while Ling Chi lied. Under the second and third possibilities, the subsequent judgment order could allow Ling Chi to survive. Therefore, from Ling Chi's own perspective, he was forced to tell the truth. Since Zhang Fan could reach the same conclusion, Zhang Fan was also effectively forced into telling the truth. The remaining liar would therefore have to be Chen Yang or Chen Ran.

Chen Ran then appeared in his own mental simulation as a school student being bullied. He woke in a classroom after being beaten by three classmates led by Xue Qiang. The circumstances were constructed around a typical bullying situation. Xue Qiang demanded protection money, Chen Ran had reported the matter to a teacher, and the teacher apparently leaked the information back to the bullies. The next day, the three dragged Chen Ran into the bathroom and beat him. They threatened to demand one hundred yuan, a significant amount for a student in the early 2000s. After reconstructing the situation, Chen Ran returned to class, where the other students either sympathized with him or enjoyed watching him suffer. His desk had been thrown into the trash, and the teacher who should have protected him ignored him.

The bullying escalated. Xue Qiang poured ink over Chen Ran's head and eventually attempted to humiliate him in front of the class. Chen Ran then went home, found an old Walkman, and became visibly excited. The Walkman was connected to the later solution because Chen Ran had begun constructing a record of the events. The next morning he returned to the teacher and pretended to cry while asking for help. The teacher blamed him for being bullied, and the other teachers avoided involvement because the class teacher had a relationship with the principal. Chen Ran responded with an unusually cheerful smile, then waited until class began. He locked the front door from outside, entered through the back door, locked that door from inside, and threw the key out of the sixth-floor window. He had deliberately created a closed environment in which nobody could leave.

Chen Ran then attacked Xue Qiang. He punched him, dragged him across the classroom, smashed his head into the wall, and continued beating him. When Xue Qiang's two lackeys attempted to intervene, Chen Ran allowed them to attack him before disabling them one by one. He then turned his attention to the teacher, mocked her previous question about why he was bullied while pointing out that she had failed to protect him, and repeatedly smashed her head against the door. He then forced other students to approach him and attacked them as well. Eventually, more than a dozen students were lying injured throughout the classroom. Chen Ran even struck the class monitor, despite remembering that the monitor had never bullied him. The reason was not personal revenge against the monitor. The monitor represented someone who had watched everything happen and done nothing.

Chen Ran then used the remaining students as tools. He broke Xue Qiang's leg and told Xue Qiang's two lackeys that if they wanted to leave, they had to break Xue Qiang's hands and feet. When the principal finally arrived and broke down the classroom door, Xue Qiang's limbs were broken, the lackeys were injured, and the teacher's mouth had been beaten badly. Chen Ran then struck the principal and the teachers who entered with him. Yet when the police later questioned him, he became a frightened, sobbing child. The Walkman contained recordings of him asking the teacher, grade director, and principal for help, along with their dismissive responses. To the police, the evidence therefore showed a bullied child who had repeatedly sought assistance and received none, followed by a violent incident after he had been abandoned by the adults responsible for protecting him.

The other three immediately recognized the apparent contradiction. If Chen Ran had really experienced such an incident during his life, Chen Yang should know about it because they were brothers. Chen Yang's silence therefore strongly suggested that the event had never happened. Yet Zhang Fan noticed something else. Chen Ran's description repeatedly used the language of someone waking from sleep, organizing memories, and reconstructing a sequence of events. That sounded less like a real memory and more like the process of solving a dungeon decryption. The school environment, the indifferent teachers, the principal, the absent parents, and the grandparents living elsewhere all created the exact kind of isolated environment commonly used by a decryption. Therefore, Chen Ran's story was likely not a literal account of his previous life at all. It was probably a simulated plot he had encountered during a dungeon decryption or a story he had constructed as part of solving one.

Zhang Fan then realized that the surface facts were not necessarily the most important part. The four people had established Future Lies preventing them from directly announcing whether they were telling the truth, so their narratives had to communicate their positions through metaphor. Otherwise, all four could simply tell the truth and die. Zhang Fan's two stories therefore had a second meaning. Wang Meiniang and Qin Zhong represented a relationship in which the woman did not force the man to act according to his own independent judgment. Du Shiniang, by contrast, forced Li Jia into a decision. Zhang Fan's metaphor was therefore directed at Ling Chi: I will not plot against you, and you should not plot against me. We should both tell the truth.

Ling Chi's story contained the corresponding metaphor. His subjective desire was to go to the battlefield and die with his father and brother. Yet his father prevented him from doing so and forced him to protect the military families instead. In other words, Ling Chi did not act entirely according to his own subjective desire. He followed the decision imposed by his father. This matched Zhang Fan's metaphor of Qin Zhong following Wang Meiniang rather than acting independently. Therefore, Ling Chi's story communicated that he would also tell the truth. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi were consequently both signaling the same intention without directly violating the Future Lie restriction.

Chen Ran's metaphor was simpler. In his story, anyone who bullied him was eventually beaten by him. The corresponding message in the internal struggle was: if the other three continued to pressure Chen Ran, he would simply flip the table and drag everyone down with him. If necessary, he would accept his own death as long as the others died as well. The class monitor who had done nothing and was still slapped by Chen Ran represented Chen Yang. Chen Ran was therefore criticizing Chen Yang for standing aside or failing to act. That left Chen Yang. His story was superficially much simpler than the other three, because he did not seem to be presenting a complicated metaphor at all. He described his own experience inside the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber, where eighteen people were gathered in a queue before the Judge, with Ox-Head and Horse-Face maintaining order. The central object was the Judge's Liar Killer. The chamber itself was designed around the same contradiction the four True Self Players were currently facing: people could be led into making Lies, while the person holding the gun possessed the ability to kill those who had already been determined to be Liars.

Chen Yang's behavior inside that chamber showed why he was so dangerous. The moment the Judge questioned him, Chen Yang answered that he had never committed an evil deed. The Judge immediately determined that he had lied, but the gun jammed and fell from his hand. Chen Yang understood the significance of this immediately. Because the Judge had failed the judgment, the gun no longer belonged to him. Chen Yang took advantage of the opening, picked up the weapon, and killed the Judge with his own command of the Liar Killer.

The rest of the chamber then became a test of whether Chen Yang could control people rather than just kill them. An old man quickly noticed that the words on the desk identified the location as the Ghost Gate Pass while everyone in the queue had been repeating that it was the Yellow Springs Road. He therefore correctly inferred that the chamber was constructed to make people Lie. Chen Yang recognized that this old man was different from the others, because he understood the rules instead of blindly following them. Rather than immediately killing him, Chen Yang used him as part of the structure of the game.

Chen Yang first demonstrated that he did not need to personally kill everyone. He threatened the remaining people, ordering them to kill Ox-Head, Horse-Face, and the old man if they wanted to survive. When one of the stronger men tried to resist and even attempted to seize the gun, Chen Yang simply relied on the chamber's repulsion mechanism instead of wasting a bullet. He then deliberately protected the Little Girl from witnessing the violence. This created the appearance that Chen Yang possessed a degree of kindness and restraint. The others interpreted his behavior emotionally rather than strategically, and that misunderstanding became the basis for his next move.

The old man eventually tried to save himself by revealing the apparent loophole. He pointed out that the crowd had already been manipulated into Lying, while he and Chen Yang were the only two people who had not lied. From the old man's perspective, this should have made him safe. But Chen Yang had already anticipated the reaction. By standing in front of the Little Girl and appearing to shield her, he allowed the others to believe that he was merciful. The strong man therefore decided to kill the old man rather than risk waiting for Chen Yang to act. Once the old man was dead, Chen Yang no longer needed anyone else.

He simply raised the Liar Killer and began judging the remaining people one by one. Since the others had already been made to Lie, the gun worked exactly as expected. In less than ten minutes, the entire secret chamber had been cleared, leaving only Chen Yang before finally killing the Little Girl as well. The important point was therefore not that Chen Yang possessed the strongest ability. It was that once the gun was in his hands, he no longer needed to participate in the normal cycle of mental deception. He could allow the other people to deceive one another, use their own assumptions to produce the necessary actions, and then clean up the result with the Liar Killer.

However, Chen Yang's story contained an obvious contradiction. The old man had been present in the chamber before the registration began, meaning that he should also have been questioned by the Judge. If he was truly a hidden member of the Judge's group, then he should have needed some way to pass the Judge's questions without being exposed. Since Chen Yang had waited for him to reveal himself, his earlier answers must have been sufficiently convincing. The simplest explanation was that the old man's previous evil actions had genuinely been committed under coercion, allowing him to answer the Judge's questions without actually making a Lie. In other words, the old man's ability to remain hidden was itself consistent with the rules rather than evidence that Chen Yang had fabricated the story.

The far more important contradiction concerned the deaths of Ox-Head and Horse-Face. Chen Ran, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi had previously inferred that ordinary physical fighting was prohibited by the rules of the Eighteenth Layer. Yet Chen Yang had just described a crowd literally beating people to death. Taken at face value, that should have been an obvious Lie. Chen Yang was unlikely to make such a basic mistake, so the contradiction pointed toward a deeper distinction: the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber was not actually an ordinary dungeon secret chamber.

This connected directly to the greatest Gui Yu of the Eighteenth Layer. Once the Eighteenth Layer had been blockaded by the Unity of Heaven and Man, the normal connection between the Eighteenth Layer and the Eternal Land had been severed. The easiest way to understand this was to imagine a house whose interior rooms remained intact but whose entrance had been sealed. The house still existed, but the outside world could no longer enter it through the normal route.

The Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber therefore functioned as the entrance rather than as an ordinary room inside the Eighteenth Layer. Before the blockade existed, the Eternal Land and the Eighteenth Layer had belonged to the same larger structure. After the blockade, the entrance to that structure had effectively been sealed directly outside the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber. This explained why players did not proceed directly from the Tutorial Chamber into the Eighteenth Layer after completing the tutorial. They were instead redirected into a Novice Instance.

This also explained why the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber could obey rules that appeared impossible under the normal restrictions of Hell. It followed the rules and order associated with the entrance of the Eternal Land rather than simply inheriting the restrictions of the blockaded Eighteenth Layer. Therefore, the people inside Chen Yang's story really could be beaten to death. The apparent contradiction only existed because the four True Self Players were unconsciously treating the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber as though it were an ordinary dungeon.

The importance of this discovery was much larger than Chen Yang's story itself. Chen Ran had previously been able to infer the greatest Gui Yu of the Eighteenth Layer and use that understanding to identify a method of Deciphering it. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had reached the same general solution from a different direction. The Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber was therefore not an introductory dungeon. It was connected to the original entrance between the Eternal Land and the Eighteenth Layer, which was precisely why it remained capable of interacting with the blockade created by the Unity of Heaven and Man.

Chen Yang's story therefore contained a deliberate double layer. On the surface, he had described an outrageous massacre and seemed to be telling a story that should have been impossible under the rules of Hell. Underneath that surface, however, the story was logically consistent once the status of the Novice Tutorial Secret Chamber was understood. Chen Yang was effectively telling the other three: I am telling the truth, and the apparent contradiction comes from your understanding of the rules rather than from my statement.

This placed the other three under even greater pressure. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had already used their own stories to communicate that they intended to tell the truth. Chen Yang had now provided a second piece of evidence supporting the same position, while simultaneously demonstrating that he understood a structural secret about the Hell system that the others had not fully recognized. The question was therefore no longer simply whether Chen Yang was lying. The real problem was that his story had been constructed so that the people judging it had to distinguish between an apparent violation of the rules and a genuine contradiction in the rules themselves.

The resulting deduction was that Zhang Fan, Ling Chi, and Chen Yang all appeared to be telling the truth, while Chen Ran's statement appeared to be the only one being treated as a Lie. However, that conclusion was not enough to solve the problem, because Chen Ran had deliberately constructed his story so that the Lie-detection principle and the behavioral rules of the Secret Chamber did not possess exactly the same information.

The Lie-detection principle only needed to determine whether Chen Ran's statement could be established as a Lie. The problem was that Chen Ran's speech could be interpreted in more than one way. Under one interpretation, the statement was false. Under another, the same words could describe a true situation. The objective facts therefore did not give the system enough information to determine which interpretation Chen Ran had intended. His statement existed in a state that could not be cleanly classified as either truth or falsehood.

That ambiguity became dangerous when Chen Ran was asked to judge another player. His judgment would reveal which interpretation he himself was treating as valid. If Chen Ran judged Zhang Fan and that action established that his previous statement had been made under the truthful interpretation, then the chamber's rules could finally determine that all four players had effectively told the truth. The universal obliteration condition would then become active, killing the other three. Chen Ran therefore could not safely judge Zhang Fan.

This meant that refusing to judge was not simply a passive decision. It was the action that preserved the uncertainty surrounding Chen Ran's own statement. Zhang Fan faced the same problem from the opposite direction. If he judged Chen Ran and that judgment supplied the missing information needed to classify Chen Ran's statement, then Zhang Fan might accidentally resolve the ambiguity in Chen Ran's favor. Chen Ran had therefore transferred the danger of his own uncertain statement onto the person trying to judge him.

The important distinction was therefore between what the players themselves knew and what the rules of the Secret Chamber could establish. Chen Ran knew what he intended to say, but the rule system did not possess enough information to distinguish the possible meanings. His Extreme Realm had not merely produced a clever sentence. It had placed the rule system itself into a position where its own method of determining truth could no longer produce a stable answer.

That was why the obvious judgment was itself dangerous. Zhang Fan could theoretically declare Chen Yang truthful, Ling Chi truthful, and Chen Ran a liar. But doing so required him to provide the very information Chen Ran had designed the chamber to lack. The trap was therefore not simply that Zhang Fan might choose the wrong answer. The trap was that choosing any definite answer could itself resolve the ambiguity and activate the mechanism Chen Ran wanted to avoid.

Zhang Fan therefore judged Chen Yang to be telling the truth, Ling Chi to be telling the truth, and Chen Ran to be lying. Chen Yang showed no reaction to the first judgment, confirming that the judgment was correct. Zhang Fan then judged Ling Chi truthful, which was also consistent with their cooperative arrangement. Finally, he stated that Chen Ran was lying. Chen Yang and Ling Chi both placed their hands on their Liar Killers but did not immediately draw. If Zhang Fan were absolutely certain that Chen Ran was lying, then he should have drawn first. The fact that he had not done so indicated that he himself was not yet certain how Chen Ran's statement should be interpreted. Chen Ran remained relaxed, which further suggested that he had deliberately constructed a situation in which being judged was itself dangerous.

The three then activated their own systems to analyze Chen Ran's operation. Zhang Fan could use [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] to split his consciousness into countless simulations. Chen Yang could use [Three Corpses Transformation Art] to consume Points and increase his brain activity. Ling Chi could use [Ghostly Path Soldier] to eliminate incorrect thoughts and control the direction of his own reasoning. Yet all three methods were still external systems that temporarily boosted their ability to think. Chen Ran's Self Extreme State was fundamentally different. When Chen Ran used the Extreme Realm to think, his mental consumption was essentially zero. The other three had to spend enormous amounts of mental energy to simulate what Chen Ran had already constructed naturally.

The actual trick was that Chen Ran had been a web novel author before his death. Everything he had said in the school story except the final sentence was content from a story he had written. The protagonist of that story happened to be named Chen Ran and experienced school bullying. Chen Ran was therefore not claiming that these events had happened to him. He was reciting a story he had written. The final sentence, "The above is the content of what I said," was not part of the story. That distinction created the loophole. When someone recites an entire poem or book passage, the person is not lying just because the events in the poem did not happen to them. They are simply reproducing existing content. Likewise, Chen Ran was simply reciting the contents of his own story.

The final sentence could then be interpreted in two different ways. It could mean that everything above was the content that Chen Ran had personally said, in which case the statement was false because he had only recited the story. Or it could mean that everything above was the content of the speech Chen Ran had just delivered, in which case the statement was true. The rules for judging Lies could not determine which interpretation Chen Ran intended because the objective facts supported both readings. Therefore, Chen Ran's words existed in a superposition of truth and falsehood. The secret chamber could not directly classify them as one or the other. Since the rules could not determine whether Chen Ran had lied, the obliteration condition could not simply treat all four as truthful and activate.

This created the real mechanism behind Chen Ran's survival. If Chen Ran judged Zhang Fan, the judgment would establish through his behavior that Chen Ran had chosen the interpretation in which his statement was true. That would allow the rules to determine that all four had told the truth and obliterate the remaining three. Therefore, Chen Ran could not safely judge Zhang Fan. By refusing to judge, he kept his own statement in the unresolved state between truth and falsehood. Zhang Fan's judgment of Chen Ran was similarly trapped in the same uncertainty. Chen Ran had therefore transferred the risk that belonged to himself onto Zhang Fan. Zhang Fan could not kill Chen Ran because doing so would provide the very behavioral evidence required to resolve the ambiguity in Chen Ran's favor.

The broader principle was that rules could not be perfectly airtight. The Eighteenth Layer itself already contained numerous examples of players exploiting gaps between the written rule and the actual behavior required by the rule. A player could use a Whisperer secret chamber to bypass a restriction that technically applied to the player but not to the space they created. Similarly, the rules surrounding the Lie game could be exploited if the player discovered a situation where the rule system lacked sufficient information to classify an action. Chen Ran's Self Extreme State had therefore found a loophole in the rule system itself. The Extreme Realm was not simply a stronger form of mental calculation. It allowed Chen Ran to stand outside the normal assumptions used by the rules.

Zhang Fan and Ling Chi now faced a direct problem. Theoretically, they could violate the Future Lie restriction and use [No Distance] to wear Chen Ran down. But they could not trust Chen Yang. If Chen Yang agreed to help them weaken Chen Ran and then betrayed them at the correct moment, Chen Ran could judge all three to death. Chen Yang could transform what would normally be a one-for-one trade into a one-for-two trade. Therefore, Zhang Fan and Ling Chi could not simply cooperate with Chen Yang even when doing so appeared rational. Chen Yang's previous behavior had already demonstrated that he could construct multiple layers of deception, while Chen Ran's new loophole meant that the consequences of one incorrect judgment were catastrophic.

The four were therefore left in a situation where Chen Ran could not be safely selected, Zhang Fan and Ling Chi could not safely trust Chen Yang, and Chen Yang could not openly reveal everything he knew without changing the entire structure of the game. The apparent simplicity of the rules had disappeared because each statement now carried two separate questions: what did the speaker literally say, and what objective fact could the rules actually establish from that statement? Chen Ran had exploited the gap between those two questions. Zhang Fan, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi could understand the result, but understanding the loophole did not immediately give them a method to eliminate Chen Ran. This distinction mattered because the others might otherwise attribute Chen Yang's earlier behavior to the restrained personality they had initially encountered, when the underlying manipulation could already have been underway.

The structure of the third round made that prediction reasonable. By that point Ling Chi possessed a Soldier, Zhang Fan had begun to master the same system, and Chen Yang probably did as well. If Ling Chi's Soldier spoke first and Chen Ran then spoke as though Ling Chi's main personality had already taken its turn, Ling Chi could erase the Soldier and cause the rules to recognize it as a separate participant. Chen Ran would then have spoken before Ling Chi's main personality, violating the turn order and triggering his own erasure. Refusing to speak would create a different problem. Ling Chi could continue forcing the same uncertainty while Zhang Fan completed his own cultivation. Chen Ran would eventually face a situation in which there was no safe action. The only sensible conclusion was that Ling Chi's next speech contained a trap designed specifically to make Chen Ran choose incorrectly.

From Chen Ran's perspective, the best defense was therefore to predict the shape of the trap before Ling Chi revealed it. If Ling Chi wanted to kill him, he would emphasize that the main personality was speaking. If Chen Ran believed that claim and acted on it, Ling Chi could use the Soldier's independent status against him. If Chen Ran refused to believe it, Ling Chi could continue waiting until Zhang Fan and his Soldier were ready. Either direction ultimately forced Chen Ran into the position of reacting.

This was the point where the earlier distinction between Military Form and the Four Schools of Military Strategy became important. Chen Ran tended to wait until the opponent created a problem and then destroy the person who had created it. Ling Chi was the opposite. He had been preparing the pieces necessary to attack Chen Ran several moves in advance. The Ghost Path Soldier had been passed to Zhang Fan before Chen Yang had even finished constructing the human-nature rules, and the entire third-round arrangement had been built around the assumption that Chen Ran would react to the immediate situation instead of anticipating the complete sequence.

The timeline correction therefore had a second effect on the struggle. Chen Yang had not only obtained the Ghost Path Soldier. He had demonstrated that someone could use the past, future, and time itself as part of a pre-arranged strategy. Zhang Fan, who possessed a system similar to lesser omnipotence, had still been thinking primarily from the present. Ling Chi had begun thinking across time, but he still assumed that the skill he had cultivated was the highest weapon available in the current exchange. Chen Yang had already operated beyond those assumptions.
The implications became clear when Chen Yang's Soldier appeared beside the three.

Chen Yang had not needed to send his main personality. His Soldier was sufficient. It looked exactly like him, but spoke with complete confidence about the three opponents being half-baked. Ling Chi had chosen to place his moves in advance and therefore assumed that his opponent would only respond after seeing those moves. Chen Yang explained that the same premise was already obsolete because he also possessed the ability to plant pieces in advance. If Ling Chi had only learned one simple relation, he was assuming every later relation that he could not currently perceive was wrong. His problem was not insufficient intelligence in the ordinary sense. It was that his current range of cognition defined the limits of what he was willing to consider possible.

Chen Yang then turned toward Zhang Fan. His criticism was even more direct because Zhang Fan possessed a skill bordering on lesser omnipotence yet still remained confined to the present. During his search of the Eighteenth Floor, Chen Yang had looked across the entire range of space-time and had never found another version of Zhang Fan using the Dao Heart Demonic Seed to preserve the true timeline. Zhang Fan had been afraid of being sealed in advance and therefore never seriously attempted the maneuver. That fear itself showed that he had not yet understood what the True Self Players were actually competing over. They were not fighting only for strength. They were fighting over perspective.

A person whose thoughts remained within the present would naturally regard a sealed future or altered past as an impossible danger. A person whose Spirit Vision had broken free of those limitations could treat the same future and past as pieces on the board. Zhang Fan had the technical means to operate on a larger scale, but he had not yet developed the corresponding way of seeing. Chen Yang regarded that short-sightedness as Zhang Fan's greatest weakness.
Finally, Chen Yang's Soldier looked at Chen Ran.

Chen Ran's problem was different. He already understood the danger posed by Future Chen Ran. He knew that the future version of himself existed for a reason, and he knew that the relationship between the current Chen Ran and Future Chen Ran was abnormal. But precisely because he knew that danger, he had been hiding his own threat level. Chen Yang told him that this was the wrong direction. The existence of Future Chen Ran should not become a reason for him to reduce his own danger coefficient. It should make the opposite true.

A nuclear weapon had value precisely because everyone knew what it could do. If nobody knew about it, nobody had reason to restrain themselves around it. Once the danger was publicly recognized, opponents had to spend enormous effort discussing how to deal with it. Chen Ran's identity as the potential replacement for the future version of himself could function the same way. The more openly dangerous he appeared, the greater the cost of anyone trying to destroy him.

Chen Yang therefore argued that Future Chen Ran should not be treated as an unavoidable chain around the present Chen Ran. If the two were truly competing for the same position, then Chen Ran should treat the future self as an opponent rather than a superior version that had to be protected. The question was no longer whether the future Chen Ran would eventually influence his growth. The question was whether the current Chen Ran would have the courage to reject that predetermined path.

The speech then moved beyond the four players. Chen Yang pointed toward the sky and identified the Ninth True Self Player as the larger threat. The Omniscient and Omnipotent wanted to kill them, but his actions were restricted by the structure of the Eighteenth Floor. The Ninth True Self Player was different. She had created the Fate Layer and therefore possessed a direct ability to shape their future. Chen Yang argued that fighting one another inside the Secret Chamber was wasteful when the four of them had a common enemy capable of controlling their destiny.

The suggestion of cooperation sounded reasonable enough that even Chen Ran had difficulty rejecting it immediately. Ling Chi, Zhang Fan, and Chen Ran were already operating at a severe disadvantage. Joining forces with Chen Yang could preserve all four players rather than leaving three of them dead. Yet none of the three accepted the proposal on trust. Zhang Fan immediately suspected that Chen Yang still wanted the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. Ling Chi noticed that Chen Yang's spiritual reserves appeared to have recovered by more than half despite the tremendous expenditure of the previous exchanges. Chen Ran, meanwhile, was stuck on Chen Yang's statement that other scholars would naturally debate his status and could not help wondering what that actually meant for his own future.

The four therefore reached the same practical conclusion for different reasons: cooperation was the most rational option available, even if none of them trusted the person proposing it. The difference was that the three understood this cooperation only as a temporary arrangement, while Chen Yang already appeared to be thinking beyond the Secret Chamber.
That brought the entire cultivation system into focus.

There were ten mental states divided across three broad forms of cultivation: the Three Realms of the Spirit Platform, Supreme Goodness Is Like Water, and Unity of Heaven and Man. The Three Realms of the Spirit Platform were fundamentally about breaking mental shackles. The player first escaped the control of raw emotion, then the restrictions imposed by common sense, and finally the limitations created by subjective feeling.

Supreme Goodness Is Like Water moved in another direction. Rather than breaking free from shackles, it emphasized following the heart. The appearance of the Ghost Path Soldier transformed this cultivation into a powerful means of mental attack because the cultivator could turn the movement of the heart itself into an external force.

Unity of Heaven and Man and Unity of Heaven and Man Thought had seemed comparatively simple when the four first encountered them. Their immediate use had been to reason through whether a person should conform to or resist the rules of the environment. But that interpretation was too narrow. The limitations affecting a player were not restricted to the written rules of an instance. They also included space, time, life and death, reincarnation, and even the boundary between being inside an instance and being outside it.

An orange grown south of the Huai River remained an orange there, but the same plant grown north of the river became a trifoliate orange. The difference was caused by space. A tadpole eventually became a frog, making the same existence behave differently across time. A spring silkworm could spin silk until its death, creating a limitation imposed by life and death. Flowers bloomed and withered in recurring cycles, showing the restriction of reincarnation. A person could lie within an instance and then step outside the instance where that same prohibition no longer applied. Each was a different limitation, but the player's fundamental choices remained the same: comply or resist.

From that perspective, the real function of Unity of Heaven and Man was Spirit Vision. Before cultivating it, a player's thinking remained trapped within the point in time, place, life, death, reincarnation, and instance occupied by the player. At its highest level, the restriction itself could be stepped outside mentally. The player could look at an entire timeline or space rather than being confined to one point inside it. The people involved in the situation were naturally unable to see the entire structure because they were part of it, while an observer capable of stepping outside those restrictions could perceive the larger arrangement.

A separate observation broadened this deduction. When Chen Ran and Chen Yang activated their Second Realms, they captured a blurry Spirit Body that quickly dissipated, revealing that a Soldier could leave its host instead of remaining confined to the physical body. They then noticed that the True Self Players watching the battle across the River of Time also appeared as Spirit Bodies. This raised the possibility that those observers had also cultivated the Ghost Path Soldier, although their appearance alone could not prove that they all possessed the same system.

The four consequently compared the underlying functions of their respective cultivation systems. The Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm increased the limit of a person's Spirit, the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique could replenish Spirit rapidly, the Dao Heart Demonic Seed enabled possession, and the Ghost Path Soldier appeared to provide more fundamental control over Spirit rather than merely functioning as an unusual mental attack. The Ninth True Self Player's No-Distance, meanwhile, behaved more like an inner world. The remaining question was how the True Self Players could observe events occurring across the Eighteenth Floor without every individual needing to possess an independent projection skill.

A separate system capable of spiritual coverage provided a more plausible explanation. A cultivator using such a system could extend Spirit over a selected region, potentially covering the entire Eighteenth Floor and sensing the events occurring within it. This was the Outer World system, which Chen Ran attributed to Unity of Heaven and Man. The implication was that the highest level of Unity of Heaven and Man could provide area-wide spiritual perception, allowing its user to observe events beyond the immediate location of their physical body. This was related to Spirit Vision but added a more specific explanation for how a True Self Player could monitor a distant region without necessarily entering it in person.

That was why Chen Yang's transformation through Saint's Demonic Fall had increased the gap between him and the other three. His Spirit Vision had already moved beyond theirs. His earlier behavior had therefore been a demonstration of a higher level of Unity of Heaven and Man rather than simply a stronger method of psychological deception.

The order of cultivating the three systems consequently became clearer. The Three Realms of the Spirit Platform formed the foundation because without them the player remained trapped by emotions, common sense, and subjective feelings. Unity of Heaven and Man should come next because it determined the scale at which the player could perceive and plan. Supreme Goodness Is Like Water came after that as a powerful supplementary system for mental attacks.
There was one exception.

If a player obtained the Ghost Path Soldier, Supreme Goodness Is Like Water immediately became far more valuable because the Soldier provided an unusually powerful form of mental offense. That was precisely why Ling Chi had been able to threaten the others despite lacking Chen Yang's Spirit Vision. His Soldier could attack on a level the others were not prepared to defend against. But because Ghost Path Soldier was a secret system that could not be openly taught throughout Hell, most players could not rely on it. For the vast majority, Unity of Heaven and Man remained the more important path after the foundational Three Realms.

This also explained why the Ninth True Self Player had been willing to reveal No-Distance without revealing every other True Self cultivation system. If Ghost Path Soldier were made universally available, then the advantage created by one person's mastery of it would disappear. The same would be true of the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique or any other specialized system. If every top player gained access to every True Self cultivation method, the distinction between the ordinary experts and the True Self Players would shrink into a simple difference in skill. That would destroy the balance of the Eighteenth Floor.
No-Distance itself was an exception because it was a remnant of the earlier war rather than a newly opened cultivation route.

This was why Chen Ran, Qiu Yinong, Lin Xuan, and Jiang Zhe could all reach a point where killing the Seven-Star Players became extremely difficult. Their numerical foundations were too similar and their basic mental cultivation had not created a decisive gap. At that level, Spirit Vision became the real separator. A player who could plan across time while the opponent remained trapped in the present possessed a structural advantage regardless of how close their ordinary mental strength was.
The principle then moved naturally back to the internal struggle.

Chen Ran, Ling Chi, and Zhang Fan had all been trying to solve the Secret Chamber from within it. Chen Yang had already begun treating the Secret Chamber as one event inside a much larger timeline. That difference in perspective explained why he could prepare the Ghost Path Soldier in the past, hide the evidence through timeline correction, and still arrive in the present with the system already cultivated.
The conflict had consequently moved beyond the four-person chamber.

The True Self Players watching from the River of Time began to notice the same danger. Chen Yang's speech about cooperating against the Ninth True Self Player was not merely a proposal to stop killing each other. It was a declaration that the four players had finally reached the point where the internal struggle itself might become less important than the conflict outside it.

The Cold-Faced Youth and the Saint stepped forward on the River of Time while the Omniscient, the Omnipotent, the Little Monk, the Confucian Scholar, and the Ninth True Self Player watched the Eighteenth Floor. Before the confrontation fully developed, the number and identity of the participants began changing. The Black Lotus in Han Fei's consciousness started spinning and released a tremendous mental fluctuation that penetrated the instance, passed through Hell, and reached the Eighteenth Floor. A blurred Spirit Body appeared beside the Cold-Faced Youth and the Saint. Although its strength was negligible compared with that of the Half-Step True Self Players, it seized the Black Lotus when it emerged from the Saint and absorbed it, refining it until its mental power condensed into a youth identical in appearance to Zhang Fan. This was not simply an additional observer: the newly formed figure had acquired a body capable of participating in the confrontation.

Another figure emerged from the space opened by the Death Row Inmate, manifesting as a Soldier with Ling Chi's face. It took its place beside the Cold-Faced Youth, the Saint, and the Zhang Fan-like figure, adding another participant whose existence was connected to Ling Chi's system. The balance changed again when the Little Taoist arrived from the Eternal Land and stood beside the Omniscient and Omnipotent, strengthening the opposing side. A Masked Woman subsequently appeared from downstream of the River of Time and stood beside the Eleventh Half-Step True Self Player. Those two initially remained observers, but they would later step forward and join the group containing the Cold-Faced Youth, the Saint, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi.
The moment the Cold-Faced Youth raised the Pure White Liar Killer, the balance that had existed among the spectators disappeared.
The gun fired, yet nothing happened to the Ninth True Self Player.
Instead, the Pure White Liar Killer in the Cold-Faced Youth's hand vanished.

The effect of Eternal Kingdom had targeted the Ninth True Self Player, yet the weapon carrying the technique had been erased as though the rule itself had turned back onto its owner. Nobody had seen such a phenomenon before.

The strange result immediately triggered an attack from everyone present. Ten No-Distances opened at once, each one different from the ordinary No-Distance used by players in the lower realms. Ten worlds of the heart descended simultaneously, overlapping, collapsing, and rebuilding themselves. Each side carefully controlled the range rather than trying to expand outward, because the objective was not to destroy the surrounding River of Time. They only wanted enough space to trap the opposing mental worlds inside the same battle.

For a moment, the side containing the Cold-Faced Youth, the Saint, Ling Chi, and Zhang Fan began losing ground. The two numerical monsters supporting the opposing side prevented an immediate collapse, but they could not crush the four instantly. That delay was enough for another figure to move.

Supreme Goodness Is Like Water stepped forward and looked toward the sealed Eighteenth Floor. Nobody present knew the complete details of his attack system. He reached out toward the Eighteenth Floor itself.
The sealed space shook.
It was only a momentary tremor, but the Eighteenth Floor appeared to have become slightly smaller.
Something then materialized in Supreme Goodness Is Like Water's hand.
A Liar Killer.

He used Whisperer · Sui Han · Gui Yuan, and the order of the rules immediately took hold. The Cold-Faced Youth, the Saint, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi were forced backward through time to the moment before the Cold-Faced Youth had fired Eternal Kingdom. The Pure White Liar Killer was once again resting at the Cold-Faced Youth's waist.
Supreme Goodness Is Like Water calmly told him that it was not time to return it yet.

The situation was interrupted by another attack. The Saint raised his hand and unleashed Radiant Three-Kills · Heavenly Emperor's Sword. The attack gathered the mental strength of countless players into a single sword. The peerless blade descended toward Supreme Goodness Is Like Water with enough force to make everyone watching instinctively tense.
Supreme Goodness Is Like Water simply withdrew his spirit and disappeared.

The attack was left for the Omniscient to contain with Chains of Rules, while the Little Monk covered the remaining force with Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. The sword and the chains were erased together, leaving the River of Time calm again.
Then the most powerful mental fluctuation of the battle appeared.
The Cold-Faced Youth's body slowly gave birth to another version of himself. The new figure had the same appearance but a noticeably calmer expression, creating a clear contrast between the two.
The spectators were not particularly concerned with the Cold-Faced Youth himself. The real problem was the Pure White Liar Killer at his waist.
That Liar Killer belonged to Chen Ran.
The Ninth True Self Player therefore had no choice. She drew her own Liar Killer, pointed it toward the Cold-Faced Youth, and used Whisperer · Dao Extreme · Wheel of Time.
The Cold-Faced Youth vanished.
Only the Pure White Liar Killer remained floating above the River of Time, yet nobody dared to pick it up.

The weapon still carried Chen Ran's ownership, and the special existence of Future Chen Ran made that ownership abnormal. It then shot downstream along the River of Time and disappeared, only to reappear again when the Ninth True Self Player used Sui Han · Gui Yuan.
The Cold-Faced Youth's mental body returned and slowly took hold of the weapon, and at that moment the balance could no longer be described as four against six.
The Eleventh Half-Step True Self Player and the Masked Woman stepped forward and joined the four.
Eleven people stood against one another.

Then all eleven released their strongest attacks simultaneously. The River of Time filled with separate worlds of the heart, each carrying its own rules, order, and conceptual structure. Rules collided with rules, order with order, and different mental worlds attempted to overwrite one another.
Amid that chaos, the Cold-Faced Youth once again raised the Pure White Liar Killer and pointed it toward the Ninth True Self Player.

Ling Chi had originally arranged the third round around a very simple calculation. He and Zhang Fan would use their newly developed Soldiers to deal with Chen Ran first, and once Chen Ran was removed, they would turn their attention toward Chen Yang. The trap inside the speaking order was supposed to force Chen Ran into an impossible choice: if he spoke, he risked being caught by the ambiguity surrounding Ling Chi's three speeches; if he refused to speak, the four of them could remain trapped until someone else created an opening. Zhang Fan therefore had enough time to continue his epiphany and finish mastering the first layer of the Ghost Path Soldier. From Ling Chi's perspective, this was already a sufficient advantage. Chen Ran might have been extraordinarily strong, but as long as he could neither speak safely nor obtain enough time to recover, the other three could eventually wear him down. The problem appeared only when Chen Ran revealed that his mental system had another layer hidden inside it.

A violent spiritual fluctuation suddenly emerged from Chen Ran's body while Zhang Fan was still attempting to stabilize his newly formed Soldier. Ling Chi and Chen Yang immediately activated their Second Realms, expecting to discover another attack from the outside, but what appeared instead was a figure struggling to emerge from within Chen Ran himself. Its body could not completely detach from Chen Ran's physical form, which initially relieved Ling Chi because it suggested that Chen Ran had not actually mastered the Ghost Path Soldier well enough to create an independent Soldier. That relief lasted only until the figure stretched its arm unnaturally into Zhang Fan's body and pulled something out. The scene changed at once inside their spiritual perception. An arena appeared around Chen Ran, and the figure standing inside it was another Chen Ran wearing enormous boxing gloves while Zhang Fan stood opposite him with a dull expression. The boxer raised his fist, shouted a ridiculous attack name, and struck Zhang Fan hard enough to blow his spirit apart. Zhang Fan, whose eyes had been closed in the real world, immediately opened them, vomited, and felt his Spirit Body wither.

Ling Chi reacted before the others could. His Soldier rushed into the arena to attack the strange Chen Ran, but a referee appeared and tried to stop him, claiming authority over the battlefield. Ling Chi's Soldier killed the referee, and the instant the referee disappeared, the arena and the boxer vanished with him. The attack had already achieved its purpose. Ling Chi's Soldier returned to the actual Secret Chamber and stabbed Chen Ran directly, yet the spear only produced the sound of metal striking steel. Chen Ran's Ego Extreme Realm had already been activated. Even though the Spirit Body inside Chen Ran had not completely become an independent Soldier, the numerical reinforcement provided by the Extreme Realm was enough to make his physical defense extraordinarily difficult to penetrate. Ling Chi immediately realized that Chen Ran had deliberately allowed the attack to appear vulnerable and then switched forms the moment danger approached.

The strange Spirit Body emerged again before Ling Chi could continue his attack, but its form had changed completely. It now wore a sheep's head mask, possessed bronze-colored skin, and casually rolled a piece of dirt from its nose into a tiny ball before flicking it toward Ling Chi's Soldier. Ling Chi wanted to dodge, but he himself restrained the Soldier, allowing the attack to strike. Its appearance immediately changed into the cartoon character Mei Yang Yang, while the other Spirit Body transformed into the Big Bad Wolf. The wolf quickly built a small mechanical toy and sent it toward the sheep. The toy waved goodbye, after which Mei Yang Yang simply disappeared from the Secret Chamber. Ling Chi immediately sensed that his Soldier had not been killed in the ordinary sense. It had been expelled from the current Secret Chamber, then thrown through the second Secret Chamber of the instance, then through the first, continuing outward until Ling Chi used the cicada-shaped technique to pull it back. By the time it returned, Chen Yang was staring at the scene in confusion, Chen Ran wore a faint smile, and Zhang Fan's Spirit Body was already badly weakened.

Ling Chi finally understood the nature of the attack. Chen Ran had developed a crude version of the Ghost Path Soldier, and the mental state supporting it was Supreme Goodness Is Like Water: Joy. Under normal circumstances this Joy could be killed instantly by Ling Chi's own Soldier because Ling Chi's attainment in the actual Soldier technique was far superior. Chen Ran's advantage was not the sophistication of the technique itself. It came from the mental foundation supporting it. Supreme Goodness Is Like Water: Joy had already reached a level capable of fighting Yue Guanshan's Ghost Immortal state, while Zhang Fan's newly created Soldier was built from only one of the ten mental states he had assembled. The difference could therefore be compared to a martial artist wielding an imperfect technique while possessing overwhelming internal energy. A superior move did not automatically defeat a vastly stronger foundation. Ling Chi's Soldier could theoretically destroy Joy in an instant, yet Chen Ran had no reason to let the two clash directly. The moment Joy sensed danger, Chen Ran could shift into the Ego Extreme Realm, allowing the overwhelming statistics of that state to protect him.

The result put Ling Chi in an awkward position. He could keep his Soldier outside his body and force Chen Ran's Joy to remain hidden, allowing Zhang Fan to continue his epiphany without fear of another ambush. The cost was continuous spiritual consumption on Ling Chi's side, while Zhang Fan had already suffered one direct attack from Joy and therefore could not safely withstand another forced breakthrough. Ling Chi also noticed something else. The violent spiritual fluctuation surrounding Chen Ran during the earlier attack had been enormous, suggesting that Joy itself had spent a substantial amount of spirit. Yet Chen Ran showed no obvious weakness afterward. That seemed impossible until Ling Chi remembered that Chen Ran's Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm had three forms: Joy, Half-Step Super-Self, and Ego Extreme Realm. If Joy had exhausted itself, that did not mean Chen Ran's entire system had been exhausted. Another form could remain on standby, with its own Spirit and statistical foundation untouched by what had just happened.

The realization changed Ling Chi's estimate of Chen Ran completely. The Chen Ran who had just displayed an overwhelming mental fluctuation was only one of the three forms. The other two could remain available while Joy spent its resources. That meant Chen Ran possessed something extremely rare inside the Secret Chamber: redundancy. Most players could only fight with the mental strength they currently had. Chen Ran could shift between different forms of the same system, allowing one to consume Spirit while another remained ready. His advantages in skill, statistics, and Military Form all pointed toward the same kind of combat. He did not need the opponent to give him a single perfect opening. He could simply force the battle to continue until one of his separate resources became decisive.

Ling Chi also realized that his earlier trap had therefore failed in a very specific way. He had successfully created a situation where Chen Ran dared not speak, but he had not created a situation where Chen Ran dared not wait. Chen Ran could remain inside the stalemate, recover through his unused forms, and continue attacking Zhang Fan whenever Zhang Fan tried to complete his cultivation. The speaking-order problem had not trapped him after all. It had merely prevented him from taking the most direct action. As long as waiting remained available, Chen Ran could continue grinding away at the other three.

Before Ling Chi could decide how to handle that problem, the atmosphere inside the Secret Chamber changed again. Nothing had been said, yet the spirits of the other three suddenly became extremely quiet. Ling Chi felt the same kind of danger one experiences when realizing a poisonous snake has been watching from nearby grass. He immediately activated his Second Realm. This time, the figure he detected was another Chen Yang standing beside the real one. The duplicate carried a strangely beautiful minimalist sniper rifle, and the three of them had never seen anything resembling it. Chen Yang's duplicate raised the rifle, announced the Seventh Heaven and Earth Sword, and fired a single bullet. The projectile itself looked absurd, possessing eyes, a mouth, and tiny hands, even pulling out a small sword while flying toward Ling Chi, yet the attack was genuine.

Ling Chi reacted immediately by sending a Spirit Body to intercept the projectile and teleporting it away. The bullet shattered the space into which it had been moved and continued its pursuit. It eventually slashed the Spirit Body apart before striking Ling Chi himself, at which point the Deep Abyss Maw emerged from within him and swallowed the projectile. A violent explosion occurred inside the maw, which then expelled smoke. The Secret Chamber became quiet again, but the cost was obvious. Ling Chi's Spirit was weakened, Chen Yang's Spirit was weakened from launching the attack, and Zhang Fan had already been severely weakened by Joy. Chen Ran himself was left staring at the situation, apparently uncertain how Chen Yang had produced such an attack.

The most disturbing detail was that Chen Yang's Spirit was already recovering. His Spiritual Energy had been depleted during the attack, but the absorption speed provided by the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique was so high that the lost Spirit was steadily returning. The other three estimated that Chen Yang would need only about half an hour to return to his previous peak. In exchange for thirty minutes of recovery time, he had nearly crippled Ling Chi with a single strike. If the same exchange happened again, the advantage would accumulate. Ling Chi immediately recognized the real danger. Chen Yang could afford to trade Spirit at a rate that the others could not. Even if they somehow survived the first Heaven and Earth Sword, the second would arrive after another period of recovery, and then a third. The Secret Chamber could turn into a process where Ling Chi was gradually battered into incapacity while Chen Yang repeatedly recovered between attacks.

The only remaining question was how Chen Yang had obtained the Ghost Path Soldier. Ling Chi went back through everything that had happened on the Eighteenth Floor. From the perspective of the True Self Players, Chen Yang's pursuit of the Dao Heart Demonic Seed had always been a distraction. His actual objective was to increase his probability of winning the internal struggle. That meant obtaining another system was the obvious target, but the candidates were limited. Chen Ran's Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm was protected by the future version of Chen Ran. The other three systems did not provide enough reason to risk seizing them, while the Dao Heart Demonic Seed was too heavily guarded by the True Self Players. Chen Yang already knew No-Distance. The only remaining system that would dramatically increase his combat strength was the Ghost Path Soldier.

Ling Chi then reconstructed the exact operation. Chen Yang had used Zhang Fan's Imprint-derived abilities to return to the specific point in history when Ling Chi first comprehended the Ghost Path Soldier. He had used Empathy to obtain the system and then remained there. Because that point existed in the past, he could continue cultivating the system for an enormous period of time before returning to the current moment. In other words, Chen Yang had not merely copied the method and started learning it from the beginning. He had effectively borrowed the same span of historical cultivation time that Ling Chi himself had spent mastering the technique. Since Chen Yang also possessed the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique, the resulting Soldier could then receive an enormous statistical enhancement. The technique and the system amplified each other.

That also explained why Chen Yang had been hiding in the background instead of immediately attacking. He had no need to challenge Ling Chi head-on when he could wait until Ling Chi had already committed his own pieces. Ling Chi had spent his effort creating an arrangement that trapped Chen Ran; Chen Yang had watched that arrangement and used it as cover while waiting for the proper moment to cripple Ling Chi instead. The three other players finally understood the practical effect of the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique. Their thoughts had originally existed within roughly the same range. They could outthink one another in specific moments, but nobody possessed enough distance from the others to simply dominate the entire struggle. Chen Yang's cognitive activity operated at a higher level. He could process and arrange information from a wider conceptual range, allowing him to prepare counters to plans that the others had only just begun constructing. Even if the three joined forces, they might still be unable to catch him.

The next scene moved into the past. Ling Chi was sitting beside an already-cleared instance, attempting to comprehend the Ghost Path Soldier at a deeper level. Yet he suddenly sensed something that did not fit. He had already cut off his Ego, so spontaneous intuition should have been nearly impossible for him. Nevertheless, he had now experienced the same strange sensation twice. When he checked his Liar Killer panel, there was no obvious indication that a skill had attacked him. He therefore considered the possibility that something had actually happened and then been corrected by the rules of time before the consequence could remain in the present.

The story then rewound to twenty seconds before the Secret Chamber. During the first ten seconds, Ling Chi opened his eyes and found Chen Yang standing nearby, smoking calmly against the wall. Chen Yang asked him why he did not use Heavenly Punishment and Earthly Destruction. Ling Chi was startled because he had not known Chen Yang was there, yet when he checked his panel he found that he had somehow acquired Empathy. Before he could act, the Whisperer of Space-Time Reincarnation and the Wheel of Time and Space rang through both their minds. The second ten-second segment unfolded differently. Ling Chi looked toward an empty wall and somehow sensed that somebody was about to appear there. A moment later Zhang Fan materialized. He immediately recognized the danger, but before he could react he was pulled into another space and the same Whisperer announced the correction. Ling Chi had witnessed two events that should never have existed in his history, and then the timeline erased them.

The truth was that Chen Yang and Zhang Fan had arrived in the past independently for the same purpose. Each wanted to use Empathy to seize the Ghost Path Soldier from the moment when Ling Chi first comprehended it. Neither knew that the other had conceived the same plan. Chen Yang, however, had one decisive advantage: because he had already Imprinted Zhang Fan's skills, he could predict that Zhang Fan would use Infinite Replication to send copies of himself into the same point in time. Zhang Fan had made his move without knowing that Chen Yang could follow him there. Chen Yang had therefore arrived second in terms of his own decision-making but first at the destination. Every one of Zhang Fan's replicas found itself blocked by another Chen Yang, with the corresponding skills sealed before the replicas could reach Ling Chi. Chen Yang described this as striking later but arriving first.

There was another purpose behind Chen Yang's intervention. He knew that Chen Ran was the player associated with the true timeline, and the presence of Empathy in the future meant that the past could not have genuinely contained a successful destruction of the skill. Chen Yang therefore intentionally warned Ling Chi about Empathy, hoping that Ling Chi would destroy it. If Empathy were destroyed in the past while continuing to exist in the future, the contradiction would force the Ninth True Self Player to correct the timeline. That correction would erase the evidence that Chen Yang and Zhang Fan had visited the past. Zhang Fan's memory of Chen Yang possessing the Ghost Path Soldier would then disappear as well.

The Ghost Path Soldier itself could remain because it had become part of the result of the internal struggle. The correction was not supposed to decide the winner. The distinction could be understood through the example of a worker repairing wet concrete. If two children stepped into freshly laid concrete and the worker simply smoothed over the footprints, he was only restoring the floor within the scope of his job. He had not chosen which child should win the competition. If he repaired the floor and then dragged the children away to punish them for competing, he had entered the competition himself and changed its result. The Ninth True Self Player's intervention worked the same way. She could smooth away the temporal footprints left by Chen Yang and Zhang Fan, but erasing the Ghost Path Soldier that Chen Yang had obtained through their struggle would amount to deciding the outcome herself.
