Once the temporal contradiction had been corrected, Chen Yang's Soldier returned to the present with an advantage the other three had not yet properly understood. He could prepare moves before Ling Chi had even decided how to respond. Ling Chi had treated his own pre-arranged trap as an advantage, but Chen Yang had already anticipated that approach. The problem was therefore not simply that Ling Chi had failed to predict one counterattack. His entire reasoning remained confined to the amount of information available in the present. He had learned one rule and naturally assumed that any later possibility outside that rule must be wrong. Chen Yang explicitly identified this as the flaw in his thinking: cognition itself was restricting what he was capable of considering.

Zhang Fan's problem was even clearer because his system should have given him the ability to think on a much larger scale. Chen Yang could not understand how someone with an ability close to Lesser Omnipotence could still remain tied so tightly to the present. During his own exploration of the Eighteenth Floor, Chen Yang had searched across the entire range of time and space and had never found an earlier version of Zhang Fan using the Dao Heart Demonic Seed to secure the true timeline. The implication was that Zhang Fan had not even attempted the strategy because he was afraid of being sealed by the True Self Players in advance. His fear had become a cognitive limitation. He was still thinking from the perspective of someone trapped inside the current situation instead of the perspective of someone who could manipulate the past and future as parts of the same board.

Chen Yang then turned his attention to Chen Ran, and his criticism was different again. Chen Ran knew the future version of himself was abnormal, but instead of treating Future Chen Ran as an opponent who might need to be confronted, he was allowing that future existence to become a restraint on his current actions. Chen Yang told him that the future version of Chen Ran could not simply be treated as an inevitable superior self. If the two were genuinely competing over the same position on the timeline, then the current Chen Ran had to be willing to make the future version his enemy. Hiding his danger level would also be counterproductive. The more obvious the possibility of Chen Ran causing a catastrophic result became, the more seriously other people would be forced to treat him. A weapon that everyone knew could explode was harder to approach than one whose existence remained uncertain. Chen Yang therefore urged Chen Ran to make the danger attached to his identity visible rather than attempting to hide it.

After targeting all three weaknesses, Chen Yang finally stated the reason for revealing so much information. He could have killed them, but the internal struggle was taking place under time pressure, and continuing to fight each other only benefited the players who were already controlling the larger situation. From Chen Yang's perspective, the Ninth True Self Player was the more dangerous enemy than the Omniscient and Omnipotent. The latter wanted to kill them but was still constrained by the rules and by the surrounding True Self Players. The Ninth True Self Player was different because she controlled the Fate Layer and therefore controlled the structure of the destiny they were all trapped inside. If the four of them continued killing one another, they would simply become the pieces that fulfilled someone else's predetermined arrangement. Chen Yang's conclusion was that the internal struggle had already served its useful purpose. They had all exposed enough of their systems to understand the relative strengths involved, and continuing to fight inside the Secret Chamber was no longer necessary.

The suggestion immediately created three different reactions. Zhang Fan suspected that Chen Yang was still trying to obtain the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. Ling Chi noticed that Chen Yang's Spirit had secretly recovered by more than half despite the massive expenditure of the previous attack. Chen Ran, meanwhile, focused on the claim that great scholars would naturally debate his existence if his danger coefficient became high enough. Yet beneath those personal doubts, all three recognized that Chen Yang's basic argument was sound. If the four continued attacking one another, three of them would probably die while the fourth would still have to face the True Self Players afterward. Joining forces against the external threat was therefore the more rational choice even though none of the three trusted Chen Yang.

Time arrives at a certain point in the future, and the Eighteenth Floor appears completely different from the place everyone has known. There are no players walking through the streets, no Death Row Inmates, no buildings, and no ordinary signs of life. Everything has become an endless white expanse, yet if the perspective pulls farther away, the structure of the place becomes visible again. In the middle of that white world sits a throne, and upon the throne is a young man who has been left there alone. The description of him as eternity and loneliness is not only atmospheric. His entire existence has effectively become an endless continuation without meaningful change. He sits there, raises the Liar Killer, says a command, fires, and repeats the same process. He has already given birth to an inner demon because he remains at Nine-Star and has not yet reached Ten-Star or the True Self, meaning that he cannot escape the erosion produced by the inner demon. As time continues to pass, that inner demon becomes stronger and increasingly distorts his personality. He knows that he is approaching destruction and can only continue living by consuming Spirit, but the problem is no longer whether he can physically survive. The inner demon has begun attacking the meaning of survival itself. He wants to prove that he is still alive precisely because he no longer understands why he should keep living.

The fact that he repeatedly reviews his own past gives the scene another layer. He does not conclude that everything he did was wrong. His conclusion is much more specific: the result was right, but the process was wrong, and because the process was wrong, the final outcome was also wrong. This is the kind of distinction that matters enormously to someone trapped inside a temporal structure. If the final result alone were incorrect, he would only need to change the final decision. But if the process itself contained the fundamental mistake, then repeating the same decision through the same chain of events would inevitably reproduce the same ending. The inner demon therefore becomes more than an enemy consuming his Spirit. It becomes the mechanism that gives him an opportunity to revisit the entire chain. He understands the principle of “two negatives make a positive” and deliberately waits for the inner demon to reach the point where it can seize his Reason. That may sound self-destructive, but he has already calculated that allowing the inner demon to completely overwhelm him is the condition that permits another choice. He is therefore intentionally allowing himself to approach the point of collapse.

Eventually, the opportunity arrives. A woman appears and asks him whether he regrets what happened. His immediate reaction is hostility because his current state makes him view an unexpected visitor as a threat. He uses his Spirit to seize her and pulls her in front of the throne. The woman is visibly shocked by the amount of power he possesses despite only being Nine-Star. He explains that the people who trapped him here believed that he could do nothing except wait for death, but during the years of his imprisonment he has cultivated the Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm to the Eighth-Turn. That is enough to explain why an ordinary Nine-Star Player would be so dangerous, but the more important point is that the woman notices how heavily the inner demon has already eroded him. His current power cannot be separated from his mental state. Had he not been this deeply consumed, he probably would not have allowed her to enter this layer in the first place or given her enough room to negotiate with him.

She tells him that this layer is called [Future], and that she can give him another opportunity to choose. The young man immediately asks whether the choice is between himself and the other version of himself, and her response—that they are the same person—goes straight to the heart of the temporal problem. Another time traveler then appears, and the person standing before him looks exactly like the young man himself. This creates an obvious opportunity for Possession. The person across from him possesses a human body while the woman who brought him here is only a spiritual body that can be discarded, so from a purely practical perspective the young man would naturally prefer to seize the human version of himself. But his own condition prevents him from doing so. The other version is controlled by someone else, and the more important problem is his inner demon. He already knows exactly how severe it has become, estimating it at roughly eight times that of an ordinary Half-Step True Self Player. If he took that condition outside, he would not simply gain a body and continue his plan. The Eighteenth Floor would turn into a bloodbath, and the resulting situation could trap him inside the [Samsara Layer]. The distinction matters because he is not refusing Possession out of morality or hesitation. He is refusing because he has enough self-knowledge to recognize that his own current state is an uncontrollable weapon.

The conversation then turns toward the timing of the second choice. He asks when the re-selection will happen, and she answers, “The node.” That immediately causes him to examine the Liar Killer in his hand. There is only one. If the node produces a new choice, then his current Liar Killer should disappear. The implication is enormous because the weapon itself becomes evidence of the temporal structure. There are not two independently generated Eternal Kingdom Liar Killers. The object has a single existence that moves through different points in time. The young man across from him understands the same thing, which is why he does not object when the weapon is thrown toward him. Normally, a Liar Killer can only be touched by its owner and would reject anyone else. Yet this version of himself catches it and places it at his waist without being repelled. The only reason this can happen is because the two versions are connected through the same weapon and the temporal arrangement permits the transfer.

The two instructions they exchange are therefore extremely precise. One tells the other to remember to return it, while the other is told to remember to borrow it. Nothing more complicated is required. The existence of the weapon at one point in time establishes the reason it exists at the other point. The woman understands what has just been created and remarks that nobody in Hell understands time loops better than she does. But the young man on the throne suddenly begins to lose control again. His expression changes, his body is consumed by pain, and he forces out the command for them to leave. The two visitors immediately flee. Remaining in front of someone whose inner demon has reached this state would be equivalent to waiting for the entire Future Layer to be destroyed.

After they disappear, the young man finally releases the pressure he has been suppressing. His Spirit tears through the Eighteenth Floor and he begins laughing because he knows that he has obtained another opportunity. He repeatedly reminds himself to be more careful this time. He wants to fight slowly, avoid repeating his earlier mistakes, and deceive everyone before they can plot against him again. The important part is the way he connects his survival to the Liar Killer. He shouts toward Chen Ran and asks whether Chen Ran has noticed the clue his future self has left behind. That clue is the only Liar Killer in Hell. Its importance is not that it is inherently unique as a weapon type, but that its existence at the present point proves something happened in the future that should have been impossible if the original certain-death outcome had remained unchanged. The future version has effectively left physical evidence in the present that another result is possible.

The young man understands the danger of dying before that clue can function. If he dies in the Future Layer, the chain that produces the clue can collapse with him. That is why he desperately repeats that he cannot die yet. His earlier failure was being plotted against before reaching the True Self, but someone has now abused space-time and given him another chance to correct the process. His response is to deliberately slow down. He no longer wants to reveal everything immediately. He wants to watch the other participants fight, learn from their behavior, and use the additional information to construct a more careful route toward the result he wants.

The two people who escaped the Future Layer eventually return to their own timelines, still shaken by the Eighth-Turn Ghost God mental state they have witnessed. One of them asks for the cultivation method of the Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm. The young man who now possesses the Liar Killer refuses to respond and begins leaving. When the woman threatens to change his fate, he simply raises the Liar Killer toward the sky and asks whether she no longer wants her own timeline. The threat works because it contains no need for explanation. If he possesses knowledge of how a timeline can be changed, then threatening to alter hers turns the entire concept of fate against her. She can interfere with his fate, but he can also potentially make her own timeline the object of retaliation. His indifference is precisely what makes the threat effective.

Back inside the Internal Strife Secret Chamber, Chen Ran, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi begin examining Chen Yang's proposed escape route. Their first obstacle is identifying the true-timeline player. Once that person is determined, the remaining three can use the Dao Heart Demonic Seed to remain on the true timeline rather than being sent back into the timelines controlled by the Ninth True Self Player. Obtaining the cultivation method is not considered especially difficult because Zhang Fan would have an obvious reason to cooperate. If giving up the Mind Cultivation Method for the Dao Heart Demonic Seed gives him a chance to remain permanently outside Ninth's control, refusing would be difficult to justify. The difficult part is what happens after the method is obtained.

One possibility is for the three alternate-timeline players to plant a Black Lotus into the consciousness of the true-timeline player. The true-timeline player would then carry the three Dao Heart Demonic Seeds while clearing the Secret Chamber and the instance. Once the process reaches the true timeline, those three Black Lotuses could be used to possess players there. The flaw is that the three people who planted the Black Lotuses must die in order for the true-timeline player to complete the instance. That creates a trust problem that cannot be solved by simply promising not to betray them. Once the three are dead, the survivor has complete control over whether their Black Lotuses remain. If that person changes his mind and destroys the three Black Lotuses afterward, then the sacrifice becomes meaningless. The entire plan depends on one person voluntarily preserving the means by which the other three can escape after they no longer possess the ability to force him to cooperate.

The second possibility is to remove Future Chen Ran's prohibition from the Secret Chamber. The problem immediately extends beyond the four people inside. Future Chen Ran might be willing to remove the seal, but the other True Self Players watching the battle would not permit him to do so freely. Once he attempted to retract the Eternal Kingdom's prohibition, the spectators would have to divide themselves into opposing factions. Chen Ran, Ling Chi, Zhang Fan, and Chen Yang have an obvious reason to cooperate because all four are trapped by the same system. Chen Yang is the person who proposed the plan, and the Chen Yang belonging to the true timeline should naturally support an operation that allows his current version to escape. The other six True Self Players have different interests and therefore become the opposing faction, resulting in the 4v6 division that Chen Yang has already begun to manipulate simply through his Spirit Vision.

The fact that a few sentences from a Five-Star Chen Yang can potentially initiate a conflict among Ten-Star Half-Step True Self Players is itself evidence of how much his Spirit Vision has changed the scale at which he thinks. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi are forced to consider that a battle may already have begun on the River of Time. If such a battle has broken out, then the four-person faction must possess some method of eventually realizing its plan. The chance that matters is the chance for the three alternate-timeline players to remain on the true timeline. Once they cross onto that timeline, the Ninth True Self Player can no longer alter the past to manipulate them in the same way, because on the true timeline the past cannot be changed.

But escaping the created timelines does not mean escaping the True Self Players. Future Chen Ran must lift the prohibition, and the opposing six will obviously monitor him. Even Ultimate Sublimation of Eternal Kingdom does not solve the problem by itself because its abilities are overwhelmingly strong in terms of prohibition but do not give Future Chen Ran the ability to travel through space-time. If the opposing True Self Players teleport him somewhere else, he cannot simply follow them by using Causality Teleportation because he does not possess that effect. He would need to prohibit the entire River of Time or accept that he can no longer meaningfully participate in the conflict.

The problem becomes even worse once Chen Ran's identity as the true-timeline player is considered. If Chen Ran is the true version, then Future Chen Ran exists on the timeline created by Ninth. Ninth controls that timeline and can alter its past. Therefore Future Chen Ran does not possess the same freedom as an independent True Self Player. During an external battle, especially one where Ninth herself belongs to the opposing side, he must be extremely careful about what he does. If he uses a skill that produces an unfavorable result, Ninth can simply alter the history of the timeline around him and change the person who eventually becomes Future Chen Ran. His own existence becomes one of the things she can manipulate.

This is why the possibility of using the Andersen Fairy Tale Squad becomes so important. Once the three alternate-timeline players successfully remain on the true timeline, they will still have to survive the pursuit of the other True Self Players. Their best solution is to possess members of the Andersen Fairy Tale Squad and use An Sheng's Absolute Defense. The problem is that these members are all Nine-Star Superego Players. Possession is not automatically successful. Their Spirit first has to be exhausted to the point where the invading consciousness can take control without being killed in return. That requirement is manageable because Zhang Fan, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi each possess systems capable of producing enormous amounts of pressure. Zhang Fan and Chen Yang have complicated combinations of abilities, while Ling Chi's Jie Mie can directly nullify the skills of the Andersen Squad. Any three of the four should therefore be capable of exhausting an individual member sufficiently.

The entire escape plan seems to converge on the question of Eternal Kingdom. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi realize that Chen Yang has been pointing toward something even more basic: can one Eternal Kingdom prohibit another Eternal Kingdom? Chen Ran's current Eternal Kingdom has not undergone Ultimate Sublimation, meaning that using it would impose its effects across a large region rather than simply functioning as a precise countermeasure. If the Secret Chamber itself was created by a skill and is adjacent to the Eighteenth Floor, then activating Eternal Kingdom could potentially affect the surrounding Eighteenth Floor as well. Therefore even if Chen Ran had the theoretical ability to remove Future Chen Ran's prohibition, he could not freely use that option without risking damage to the larger structure.

That is why Chen Yang turns their attention toward time itself. Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom is the “One” among the ten True Self Skills. There should only be one. The weapon at Chen Ran's waist is that Eternal Kingdom, and it exists on the true timeline. Yet Future Chen Ran also has an Eternal Kingdom. Chen Ran has already tried to think through this contradiction himself and failed. The fact that his Extreme Realm cannot solve it is meaningful. There is an Internal Conflict Factor involved because the subjective perceptions of the people participating in the temporal structure are inconsistent with objective reality. Chen Ran can construct deductions from the information available to him, but if several observers each possess a different relationship to the same object in time, their perspectives can produce conclusions that contradict one another even while every individual statement remains internally coherent.

The Young Man on the Throne has effectively left this problem for Chen Ran to discover. The existence of the second Eternal Kingdom is the clue. Chen Yang, however, has already seen the same contradiction and solved it from the perspective of a broader temporal structure. His reasoning begins with the fact that the Chen Ran created by Ninth does not have Eternal Kingdom. The second axiom is that Eternal Kingdom is unique. There is only one. The weapon at Chen Ran's waist is therefore the only Eternal Kingdom that can genuinely exist on the true timeline. Yet Future Chen Ran possesses one. If both facts are correct, then the simplest explanation is also the only one that does not require a second copy to exist: the Eternal Kingdom carried by Future Chen Ran is the same Liar Killer currently carried by Chen Ran.

The temporal exchange seen in the Future Layer provides the missing precedent. The young man sitting on the throne had already realized that there was only one Liar Killer. When the node arrived, the weapon in his possession would disappear if a new choice replaced his current state. He therefore handed the Liar Killer to another version of himself and explicitly established the relationship as borrowing and returning. The same principle applies here. Future Chen Ran does not possess another Eternal Kingdom created from scratch. The future Chen Ran on the true timeline eventually lends the Liar Killer to the Future Chen Ran belonging to the timeline created by Ninth. Ninth and Future Chen Ran therefore travel into the future, encounter the later version of Chen Ran, and borrow his Liar Killer.

This immediately creates the connection to the certain-death future. For the future version of Chen Ran to lend Eternal Kingdom to Future Chen Ran, there must be a reason. The most obvious reason is that the future Chen Ran of the true timeline has already reached a state in which the ending prepared for him by the Omniscient and Omnipotent is effectively certain death. Chen Yang connects this to Mo Xi's line. If the Omniscient and Omnipotent possess a trump card capable of producing Chen Ran's certain death, then using that trump card immediately would normally make sense if they wanted to secure the result. The only reason it would become expendable is if evidence from the future shows that the supposedly certain ending can eventually be deciphered.

That is exactly what the borrowed Eternal Kingdom provides. The existence of the Liar Killer in the present proves that the future version of Chen Ran must eventually have lent it to Future Chen Ran. The weapon becomes the physical clue that a different future is possible. Once that clue exists on the true timeline, the Omniscient and Omnipotent can infer that their certain-death arrangement will eventually be broken. Mo Xi therefore loses much of its value as a trump card. Instead of being an unavoidable final move, it becomes something they can afford to expend in the current instance because the future already contains the evidence that it will not remain decisive forever.

Three parties consequently benefit from the same temporal exchange. The future Chen Ran belonging to the true timeline receives another opportunity to escape his certain-death ending. Future Chen Ran receives Eternal Kingdom and can use it to construct the Absolute Defense on the River of Time. Ninth retains control over Future Chen Ran because the future version still exists on her created timeline. None of these benefits require two independent Eternal Kingdoms. One weapon is simply being used by different versions at different points along its temporal path.

The contradiction appears when Chen Ran asks what happens after that future has been changed. If the certain-death future is successfully avoided, then the future Chen Ran who was supposed to die in that future should cease to exist in the original form. If he no longer exists, then there should be nobody there to lend the Liar Killer to Future Chen Ran. If nobody lends the weapon, then Future Chen Ran cannot possess Eternal Kingdom, meaning the future cannot be corrected in the way that allowed the Liar Killer to be lent in the first place. The cause seems to disappear as soon as the effect occurs.

The answer is the closed loop itself. The future Chen Ran will lend the Liar Killer precisely because he is the future Chen Ran. The existence of the later event is already part of the history that leads to the present weapon. When the true timeline progresses forward, Chen Ran eventually reaches the future. At that future point, the Liar Killer at his waist is the same weapon that existed in the present. He lends it to the Future Chen Ran who traveled there, and that Future Chen Ran then carries the weapon back to an earlier point. From the perspective of the present, the weapon simply appears to coexist with another version of itself, but from the perspective of the River of Time there is only one continuous object.

That also answers the question of why the past cannot be changed. Future Chen Ran confirms the present by carrying the weapon backward from the future. Once the weapon has reached the past, its existence is already part of the history through which the future eventually occurs. Chen Ran does not need to create a second Eternal Kingdom. His future self is already the person who will eventually lend the same weapon. The temporal loop sustains itself because the present is already part of the future's history.

Chen Ran then raises the only apparent escape route: what if his future self refuses to lend it? Chen Yang points out that Ninth does not actually need to force him directly. Her timeline was created from the true timeline, and Future Chen Ran's existence depends upon that relationship. If Chen Ran becomes strong and deliberately ignores Future Chen Ran, then the Future Chen Ran created by Ninth risks disappearing because the history that produced him has diverged. Ninth would therefore have to alter Future Chen Ran's past to make his development correspond to Chen Ran's path again. This changes the relationship between the two sides. When Chen Ran is weak, he is the passive party while Ninth is the active party who determines how the timeline is arranged. When Chen Ran becomes strong enough, he becomes the active party because his choices force Ninth to react in order to preserve the Future Chen Ran she relies upon.

The question of whether to lend Eternal Kingdom therefore becomes secondary. Regardless of which choice Chen Ran makes, the future must eventually find a way to rationalize itself around that choice. If he refuses to lend Eternal Kingdom, Future Chen Ran loses the Absolute Defense. Ninth and Chen Yang might then have to construct another Absolute Defense using different True Self Players, or they might abandon the construction and hide instead. Without the protection of that Absolute Defense, however, the future Chen Ran's survival becomes far less secure. The pressure of that future ensures that Chen Ran will eventually lend the weapon. There is no independent future in which the future version simply refuses and then continues normally, because the refusal itself would create a future in which the necessary Absolute Defense never appears and Chen Ran eventually dies.

This is why the true node is not the meeting with Future Chen Ran and not the decision to lend Eternal Kingdom. Those events are already structurally locked into the temporal loop. The variable that actually matters is how long Chen Ran allows his Eternal Kingdom to remain in the hands of Future Chen Ran. The moment he recalls the weapon is the moment the Absolute Defense protecting the three people on the River of Time collapses. That is the point where Chen Ran actually possesses freedom to influence the structure instead of merely being one of the pieces required to make it function.

The absurdity of Chen Ran's situation becomes apparent even to Zhang Fan and Ling Chi. The Omniscient and Omnipotent have prepared a certain-death instance specifically around him. Ninth has manipulated his future and eventually takes his Liar Killer into another point in time. Unity of Heaven and Man has blocked his route toward the Eternal Land. Yet these are only the problems that have already been successfully deduced. Chen Ran himself gives no indication that he intends to complain about any of this. He lights another cigarette, takes a long drag, and shows Chen Yang a smile as though he is simply asking what the next problem is.

Chen Yang then returns to the Secret Chamber itself. If he had never proposed joining forces, he asks, what would the four people have done? The answer is that they would have remained trapped. Nobody currently dares to speak, and without another method of changing the situation, the four would simply consume their resources until all of them died. The rules look simple because one death is theoretically enough to determine the winner, but the presence of Ling Chi's Soldier destroys the normal progression of the game. Once the Soldier becomes involved, the safest choice for everyone is to stop speaking. As long as the four remain locked in that state, the game cannot reach the final judgment. The four eventually exhaust themselves instead of producing a winner.

Chen Ran realizes that this is the real death trap. The game has a fatal factor built into the process of the infighting just as human beings have a fixed limitation in the form of lifespan. Players can struggle against one another, but if the struggle inevitably activates a mechanism that forces all four into a state of mutual stagnation, then fighting itself becomes the cause of death. That mechanism is Ling Chi's Soldier. Chen Ran's Extreme Realm makes him particularly vulnerable to this kind of design because his normal method is to start by reconstructing the rules. He grants Spirit Vision to the other three, they understand the structure more deeply, and Ling Chi eventually reveals the Soldier. Once the Soldier appears, the result of the earlier deductions naturally leads to nobody daring to speak.

This means their earlier struggle was already part of the calculation made by the Omniscient and Omnipotent. Their attempts to fight over momentum and luck, the efforts to determine who belonged to the true timeline, the pressure placed upon Future Chen Ran, Chen Ran's Extreme Realm, and Ling Chi's decision to externalize the Soldier all fit into a single chain. None of them had realized that the very strengths they were using to escape the situation were also being used to drive them deeper into the trap.
There is one exception, being Chen Yang.

The three stare at him because the obvious question is why he was not calculated in exactly the same way. His Soldier raises two fingers in a peace sign and explains the reason: the Omniscient and Omnipotent cannot spy on his past, cannot spy on his future, and cannot change him. Even after he created the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique, they still cannot properly know what he is thinking, reflect his thoughts, or predict his actions. This is why Ninth sent him into the Secret Chamber. She could not simply construct his future in the same way she had constructed the others.

Chen Yang's next deduction follows directly from that immunity. He has already spoken about a large number of secrets and is still sitting here alive. If Ninth possessed complete control over the situation, the act of revealing those secrets should itself have allowed her to erase him or correct the timeline around him. She has not done so. Therefore, the Secret Chamber in which all four are now standing must be located on the true timeline. On the true timeline, the past cannot be changed in the same manner as the alternate timelines created by Ninth. Chen Yang calls this Causality and Rule Spirit Vision because the important distinction is not merely that he can see farther. He can identify how the causal rules governing the different timelines restrict the actions of the people within them.

He then turns the observation into the deeper principle behind the entire Secret Chamber. The most important conclusion is not that Future Chen Ran can potentially release the prohibition or that one Eternal Kingdom can interact with another. The important fact is that whenever these four people appear inside this particular Secret Chamber, the natural outcome is that all four are worn down to death. Their talents are precisely what make that outcome inevitable. The better Chen Ran understands the rules, the more effectively he exposes the Soldier. The more effectively Ling Chi uses the Soldier, the less willing everyone becomes to speak. Zhang Fan's complicated system makes him capable of using enormous numbers of skills, but when the game reaches the speaking deadlock, those skills cannot be freely deployed. Chen Yang's existence is the only major variable the original arrangement cannot properly calculate.
He then introduces the theory that a king does not meet another king.

The principle is straightforward. A king can meet a marquis, an earl, or a viscount because there is a clear difference in authority. One side possesses enough superiority that the confrontation does not necessarily result in mutual destruction. But if two kings of equal level meet directly, neither can simply overwhelm the other. If both are genuinely capable of carrying out their respective plans, then the confrontation itself creates a situation in which both can die. The theory is therefore not merely saying that powerful people avoid one another. It is describing a structural consequence of equal authority.

That becomes important when applied to the River of Time. If there is already a battle between two groups of True Self Players, then the existence of the battle itself indicates that one of the two sides believes its plan can be realized. Otherwise there would be no reason for equally powerful existences to expose themselves to mutual destruction. If one side has the confidence to execute its plan, then the four people inside the Secret Chamber can regard themselves as the passive party. They do not necessarily need to force an opening themselves. They can wait for the active side to make the move that changes the conditions around them.

There is an immediate practical problem. Nobody dares to speak, which means the only person among the four who can currently activate skills without saying anything is Zhang Fan. His passive ability [Mind Follows Will] allows him to operate his skills directly through thought. If the prohibition on the Secret Chamber is eventually removed and Zhang Fan is therefore the only one capable of acting immediately, he could potentially escape while the other three remain trapped. The other three obviously cannot accept such a result. The issue is not even that Zhang Fan is stronger. It is that he would possess an asymmetrical ability to take advantage of the exact opening they are all waiting for.

Chen Yang therefore turns this structural inequality against him. His Soldier asks whether they should kill Zhang Fan now, or kill Zhang Fan now. The wording is deliberately shameless because Zhang Fan has very few options. Chen Yang wants the cultivation method for the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. If Zhang Fan refuses, he can be killed inside the Secret Chamber. If he agrees, he has a way to preserve his consciousness through the Black Lotus arrangement and potentially escape Ninth's control. Zhang Fan therefore receives an offer that is technically a choice but functionally an extortion.

His situation is even worse because Chen Ran had already damaged his Spirit and Zhang Fan has not fully mastered the Ghost Path Soldier. He cannot use No-Distance, cannot use his own Soldier as a mouthpiece, and therefore cannot even freely explain what he intends to do. The result is an intentionally ridiculous image of Zhang Fan looking around anxiously while the other three pretend not to notice because everyone knows exactly what he wants to say. Eventually he can only make a helpless gesture, effectively surrendering to Chen Yang's demand.

The pressure then shifts to Ling Chi. Chen Yang openly tells him what would happen if Zhang Fan escaped without him. Zhang Fan could allow Chen Yang to Imprint his skills, and Chen Yang could then use those abilities to send Ling Chi directly in front of several Superego Players from the Underworld. Ling Chi would be subjected to mental attacks and would likely die. Chen Yang strengthens the threat by revealing that he previously encountered Yanluo while conquering the Eighteenth Floor, and Yanluo addressed him as “Lord.” The obvious implication is that the members of the Underworld listen to Chen Yang. This makes the threat much more than a generic statement that Chen Yang knows powerful people. He is telling Ling Chi that there is an entire structure outside the Secret Chamber that he can use to eliminate him.

The threat is especially strange because Chen Yang has already acquired the Ghost Path Soldier. Ling Chi's greatest unique advantage has therefore been reduced. Chen Ran was the only one of the four who originally lacked that system, while Chen Yang has now obtained it through his temporal manipulation. That should mean that Ling Chi's value to Chen Yang has sharply decreased. From a purely strategic perspective, there is no obvious reason for Chen Yang to announce that he intends to preserve Ling Chi. In fact, if Chen Yang were simply trying to maximize his own odds, allowing Zhang Fan to escape and then eliminating Ling Chi would be a perfectly reasonable route.

Chen Yang has already shown that his stated objective can be a decoy. He spent the earlier conflict behaving as though obtaining the Dao Heart Demonic Seed and remaining on the true timeline were the central purpose of his actions, while the actual objective turned out to be the Ghost Path Soldier. Now he openly demands Zhang Fan's cultivation method and threatens Ling Chi with the Underworld, yet he simultaneously argues that the four should cooperate. His actions are not contradictory because all three things can serve a larger plan, but the other players still lack enough information to determine what that larger plan is.

Chen Ran, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi therefore had found themselves in the strange position of having to depend upon a person who has repeatedly demonstrated that he is willing to manipulate them while also being the only person who has remained outside the predictive structure imposed by the Omniscient, Omnipotent, and Ninth. Every attempt to fight him directly risks falling into another one of his preparations, while refusing to cooperate leaves them trapped inside a Secret Chamber whose rules naturally grind all four of them toward death.

Zhang Fan considered the situation and concluded that handing over the cultivation method for the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] might actually be the safest choice available to him. If Chen Yang was telling the truth about the possibility of escaping the Secret Chamber, then cooperating would allow Zhang Fan to preserve his position until the restrictions were lifted, while refusing would only encourage the other two to eliminate him before he could escape. Even if Chen Yang was lying and the blockade could not be lifted, the four of them would eventually exhaust their Spirits and die inside the Secret Chamber anyway, meaning that withholding the cultivation method would accomplish nothing. Zhang Fan therefore extended his consciousness toward the other three, allowing strands of mental energy resembling fine hairs to spread from his body and enter their consciousnesses. Chen Yang and Ling Chi accepted the connection, and the strands immediately transformed into Zhang Fan's likenesses within their minds, transmitting the cultivation method of the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] directly to them. When the same strands reached Chen Ran, however, they were instantly annihilated before they could invade his consciousness, indicating that Chen Ran had deliberately rejected the transmission rather than simply failing to receive it.

The three looked toward Chen Ran, who continued smoking with his chin raised at an exaggerated angle, showing no intention of explaining himself. Chen Yang was particularly confused because learning the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] should have provided Chen Ran with several methods of protecting himself against the Ninth True Self Player. Since Ninth had created numerous alternate timelines, Chen Ran could potentially use the technique to possess players existing on those timelines and establish a presence within the very structure that Ninth controlled. With Future Chen Ran already operating on one of those timelines, he would also have a powerful ally who could help him exploit the connection between the alternate timelines and the true timeline. Even if Chen Ran encountered a life-or-death crisis in the future, possession would provide him with another means of preserving his existence by transferring his consciousness into someone else's body. From Chen Yang's perspective, refusing such a versatile technique made little sense, especially when Chen Ran had already been placed in a position where his survival depended upon understanding the same rules that governed the other True Self Players.

Chen Ran eventually raised one finger, reminding the others of his status as [One], and the three immediately understood the distinction that had prevented him from accepting the technique. The [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] could allow Chen Ran to possess another person, but the body he occupied would not automatically possess the Liar Killer known as Eternal Kingdom. His identity as [One] was inseparable from that weapon, so learning the technique too early could force him into a situation where preserving his consciousness came at the cost of losing control over the ability that defined his place among the True Self Players. The danger extended beyond the immediate loss of Eternal Kingdom because Ninth would have a reason to manipulate Chen Ran's possession from the beginning. If Chen Ran learned the technique, Ninth could force him to possess another player and then trap his Main Body on one of the layers of the Eighteenth Floor, ensuring that the Liar Killer held by his Main Body remained available for Future Chen Ran to borrow. Through that arrangement, Ninth could effectively maintain control over two True Self-level Liar Killers rather than allowing Chen Ran to use Eternal Kingdom independently against her.

The reasoning resembled Liu Bei borrowing Jingzhou, because an arrangement that initially appeared to provide an advantage could eventually become the means through which the other party controlled the situation. Chen Ran might gain the ability to invade Ninth's alternate timelines and survive through possession, but those benefits would also give Ninth an opportunity to determine where his Main Body remained and who could access Eternal Kingdom. The same principle could be seen in the comparison with Wu Zetian, whose decision to declare herself emperor caused the forces that had supported her to collapse, leaving her dependent upon another arrangement to rebuild her external political influence. In both cases, a seemingly small decision changed the relationships on which a person's existing power depended, and the resulting consequences could not simply be reversed after the decision had been made. Chen Ran therefore could not evaluate the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] solely according to its immediate benefits, because learning it too early could make Ninth his direct enemy and force him into a situation where he lost the very advantage that made him difficult to control. His refusal was consequently a calculated decision to preserve the existing structure of his power rather than an unwillingness to acquire another system.

Chen Yang and Ling Chi quickly entered a state of sudden enlightenment as they began cultivating the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed], and approximately ten minutes later, both had completed the initial process despite the complexity of the technique. Their rapid progress was consistent with their status as True Self Players, whose cultivation and understanding had already reached a level where the basic principles of another system could be absorbed far more quickly than they could by ordinary players. Ling Chi then looked toward Chen Ran and raised the question of whether he intended to cultivate the [Ghost Path Soldier], since all three of them now possessed knowledge of that system. Chen Ran shook his head again, leaving the others unable to understand why he would reject another technique that could potentially improve his chances of survival. His refusal to learn the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] could at least be explained by the relationship between [One] and Eternal Kingdom, but declining the [Ghost Path Soldier] created a different problem because the immediate disadvantage was much harder to identify. Chen Ran nevertheless offered no explanation, and the Secret Chamber returned to silence while the other three continued calculating their positions.

Ling Chi eventually recognized that Chen Ran's behavior reflected his position as the central figure in the struggle between the True Self Players. Chen Ran had more reason than anyone else to be cautious about acquiring another system, because even a small change to his abilities could alter the way Ninth manipulated his future or the way the other True Self Players attempted to control him. However, Ling Chi did not extend the same interpretation to Chen Yang, whom he considered much more dangerous precisely because his motives were not confined to the survival of his current self. Chen Yang had already demonstrated that he could manipulate the other players into helping him achieve an objective different from the one they believed he was pursuing, and Ling Chi was certain that if the three of them managed to escape the Secret Chamber, Chen Yang would attempt to eliminate both him and Zhang Fan. The possibility that all three could return to the true timeline did not mean that they would benefit from allowing one another to survive, because the best outcome for each of them was for their own existence on another timeline to escape while the other two died.

Their temporary cooperation therefore did not eliminate the fundamental conflict between them. Every additional user of the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] represented another opponent capable of possessing someone, devouring a consciousness, and expanding their influence across different timelines, so none of the three could regard the others as permanent allies. Chen Yang had reasons to kill Zhang Fan and Ling Chi, but Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had equally strong reasons to eliminate Chen Yang and one another before their competitors could become more powerful. The difficulty was that each player possessed a different method of escaping the Secret Chamber, meaning that they could not simply attack simultaneously without considering what would happen if one of them survived the confrontation. Ling Chi could not teleport himself out, while Chen Yang needed to use Imprint before he could reproduce another player's skill and apply it to the escape. Zhang Fan, by contrast, possessed the greatest immediate advantage because [Mind Follows Will] allowed him to activate skills directly through thought, making him the person most likely to escape first once the restrictions disappeared.

Ling Chi consequently began considering how he could avoid being abandoned after Zhang Fan escaped, especially because Chen Yang's earlier threat to send him into the Underworld had already exposed the danger of remaining behind without a means of defending himself. He had intended to plant a [Black Lotus] inside Zhang Fan's consciousness together with Chen Yang, thereby ensuring that Zhang Fan could not escape the conflict simply by teleporting to another time or space. However, the plan had to account for the possibility that Chen Yang would cripple Zhang Fan's consciousness first and then abandon Ling Chi once Zhang Fan could no longer resist. If that happened, Ling Chi would be left alone with Chen Ran, who was already established on the true timeline and would not need to escape with anyone else. The rules of the Secret Chamber would eventually reduce the remaining participants to two, at which point the speaking order would become decisive: Ling Chi would be required to judge Chen Ran before Chen Ran judged him, but Chen Ran had not told a Lie throughout the confrontation, making Ling Chi's judgment certain to fail and leaving him with no means of surviving the final stage.

Ling Chi therefore needed the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] as protection against being abandoned. If he possessed the technique alongside the [Ghost Path Soldier], he could weaken Chen Ran through mental attacks and then use the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] to possess him, giving Ling Chi another way to preserve himself even if Chen Yang refused to take him along during the escape. This possibility changed the calculation entirely because Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom meant that abandoning Ling Chi would also carry the risk of losing the entire Secret Chamber. If Ling Chi could force Chen Ran into a situation where he would certainly die, Chen Ran would have every reason to activate Eternal Kingdom rather than accept the result, and Chen Yang could not safely assume that his own escape would remain unaffected. The [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] would thus give Ling Chi the leverage required to make Chen Yang take him seriously as a necessary participant rather than treating him as an expendable ally whose usefulness ended once Zhang Fan had been disabled.

At that moment, Chen Yang turned toward Zhang Fan, and his [Soldier] appeared as he prepared to attack, evidently intending to cripple Zhang Fan's consciousness before the restrictions could be lifted. The purpose was straightforward: if Chen Yang and Ling Chi could first overwhelm Zhang Fan through their [Soldier]s, they could then plant the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] inside him while his Spirit was too exhausted to destroy the Black Lotuses. Once Zhang Fan had been weakened sufficiently, the two could use possession, cooperation, or the threat of possession to prevent him from escaping and preserve their advantage after the blockade disappeared. Chen Yang expected Ling Chi to participate because the two had a shared interest in preventing Zhang Fan from escaping with his extensive collection of skills, but as he prepared to act, he suddenly noticed Ling Chi's [Soldier] watching him and immediately understood that Ling Chi was prepared to ambush him if he proceeded without meeting his demand.

Chen Yang stopped and asked what Ling Chi intended to do, and Ling Chi's [Soldier] answered that he wanted the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique]. The demand was not an attempt to improve Ling Chi's cultivation for its own sake, because he had recognized that Chen Yang's plan depended upon Ling Chi cooperating in the attack against Zhang Fan while receiving no guarantee that Chen Yang would protect him afterward. If Zhang Fan's consciousness were crippled, he might lose the ability to launch mental attacks, allowing Chen Yang to cooperate with Chen Ran to eliminate Ling Chi once Zhang Fan was no longer a threat. By demanding the technique before participating, Ling Chi forced Chen Yang to provide him with an independent means of recovering his Spirit and defending himself against the possibility of being abandoned. The exchange would leave Ling Chi less dependent upon Chen Yang's goodwill and would make it far more dangerous for Chen Yang to attempt to eliminate him after escaping the Secret Chamber.

Chen Yang's earlier threat to use Imprint and send Ling Chi into the Underworld had also been designed to create suspicion between Ling Chi and Zhang Fan. If Zhang Fan chose to ignore Ling Chi and escape independently, Chen Yang could obtain Zhang Fan's skills through Imprint and use them to send Ling Chi to the Underworld, where several Superego Players could attack him mentally until he died. The threat made Ling Chi appear to be a burden whose survival depended entirely upon Zhang Fan's willingness to cooperate, encouraging Zhang Fan to prioritize his own escape rather than protect a competitor. Yet the same threat also revealed why Ling Chi needed to secure the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] before helping Chen Yang attack Zhang Fan, because otherwise he would be left with no way to prevent Chen Yang from using the exact arrangement he had described. Ling Chi was therefore forcing Chen Yang to choose between granting him the means to survive independently and accepting the possibility that Zhang Fan would escape before they could cripple his consciousness.

Chen Yang now faced two viable but costly choices. He could concentrate on eliminating Ling Chi and allow Zhang Fan to escape, preserving the immediate opportunity to remove one opponent while sacrificing the possibility of catching Zhang Fan again, since Zhang Fan's diverse collection of devoured skills would make tracking and restraining him across different times and spaces extraordinarily difficult. Alternatively, Chen Yang could give Ling Chi the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique], allowing the two of them to attack Zhang Fan together, cripple his consciousness, and plant their [Black Lotuses] before the escape conditions changed. With Zhang Fan's Spirit sufficiently depleted, he would have much greater difficulty destroying the two Black Lotuses, and even if he later escaped or concealed himself in another time or space, the two users of the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] would still have a means of tracking him through the connection established by the technique. The second choice would secure the immediate escape of all three players, but it would also preserve the rivalry between them and force Chen Yang to deal with Zhang Fan later rather than allowing him to eliminate both competitors immediately. His decision therefore depended upon which danger he considered more urgent: losing Zhang Fan permanently by allowing him to escape now, or strengthening Ling Chi through the cultivation method and accepting another round of internal strife after the three had left the Secret Chamber.

Chen Yang did not hesitate to act once Zhang Fan's position had been determined. He immediately used his consciousness to transmit the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] to Ling Chi, giving him the same means of absorbing Points that Chen Yang possessed. This was not simply an exchange of cultivation methods between two temporary allies. Ling Chi needed to recover his Spirit before the seal of the Secret Chamber was lifted, because the coming struggle would leave no time for him to recover naturally, while Chen Yang needed Ling Chi to possess enough strength to help suppress Zhang Fan. The moment Ling Chi received the technique, he began cultivating it and absorbed Points until his mental state returned to its peak. Zhang Fan immediately understood what the exchange meant for him. If he allowed the other two to escape together, they would first cripple his consciousness and then use the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] to plant Black Lotuses inside him. By the time the actual struggle began, he would have neither the mental strength to resist them nor the opportunity to eliminate them separately.

Chen Yang and Ling Chi therefore did not immediately proceed to the next stage. They first used their [Soldier]s to launch mental attacks against Zhang Fan, concentrating their attacks on his consciousness until he was left barely capable of keeping himself awake. Once his resistance had been sufficiently weakened, the two used the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed] to invade his consciousness and plant a Black Lotus within his No-Distance. The distinction between this and their earlier mental probing was important. Previously, Zhang Fan had been able to remove their influence by destroying the Black Lotus before it could establish itself, but his current condition made that response much more difficult. If he attempted to eliminate both Black Lotuses while his Spirit was already close to exhaustion, he would have to expose himself to the subsequent attacks from Chen Yang and Ling Chi. If he did not eliminate them, the two could gradually consume his consciousness and eventually take possession of him. Either way, Zhang Fan had been placed under pressure before the actual struggle had even resumed.

Nevertheless, Chen Yang and Ling Chi could not assume that Zhang Fan had already lost. They remembered that his system included a substitute-death ability, and the timing of its possible activation made it particularly dangerous. Once the restrictions on skills were lifted, Zhang Fan might be able to use that ability to substitute another object for himself or otherwise escape the consequences of his current condition. If the effect restored his mental state to its peak, the damage inflicted by Chen Yang and Ling Chi would no longer be enough to keep him under control. They therefore had to watch carefully for any attempt by Zhang Fan to commit suicide or activate his substitute-death mechanism, because allowing him to recover at the critical moment could immediately reverse the advantage they had worked to establish. Their preparation was consequently not complete merely because Zhang Fan had been weakened and infected with two Black Lotuses; they still had to survive until the restrictions disappeared and then prevent him from using whatever remained of his system to escape their control.

The three continued waiting for the outcome of the conflict on the River of Time, where the theory that a king does not meet another king was supposed to determine whether anyone could escape the existing arrangement. None of them could yet know whether the larger structure would permit them to leave the Ninth Timeline or whether the conflict would end with them trapped inside the Secret Chamber. What they could establish was that the person who appeared to be losing did not necessarily have the weakest position. Zhang Fan had performed poorly during the confrontation, repeatedly finding himself on the defensive and allowing Chen Yang and Ling Chi to dictate the immediate course of events. However, he remained the only person among the four who could activate skills through thought alone without speaking a skill command. As soon as the restrictions were lifted, this would give him an advantage that Chen Yang and Ling Chi could not automatically overcome. The difference between possessing a powerful skill and being able to activate it at the necessary moment was becoming more important than the difference between their apparent levels of strength.

Chen Ran understood this distinction even though his own position was also unfavorable. He possessed [Eternal Kingdom], but the restrictions surrounding the Secret Chamber meant that using it recklessly could kill everyone rather than secure his victory. He could not simply attack Zhang Fan while the other two were preparing to escape, because any immediate escalation might force him to use Eternal Kingdom without knowing whether the consequences would favor him. From the perspective of the other three, Chen Ran had become almost irrelevant to the immediate struggle. He had not taken control of the preparations, nor had he directly helped Chen Yang or Ling Chi cripple Zhang Fan. The only thing preventing the others from treating him as an ordinary spectator was the possibility that he might activate Eternal Kingdom if he were pushed too far. They therefore had little incentive to involve him in their decisions, but they also could not safely ignore him. Chen Ran's apparent passivity concealed a more complicated position: he could not determine the outcome through ordinary means, yet his decision could still destroy the framework in which everyone else's plans depended upon succeeding.

Chen Ran suddenly began laughing, eventually laughing so hard that he had to hold his stomach before returning to his chair and apologetically lowering his head. The reaction made little sense to the others, who believed that his situation was worse than Zhang Fan's because he possessed only Eternal Kingdom while the other three had demonstrated more varied systems. They interpreted his laughter as an expression of helplessness or mockery directed at his own predicament, assuming that he was simply acknowledging that he had become an insignificant participant in a struggle whose result would be determined by the other True Self Players. However, the reaction would later acquire a different significance when Zhang Fan reconstructed the connection between Chen Yang's theories and Chen Ran's decision to use Eternal Kingdom. Chen Ran had already heard that the active party was the person willing to act without fear, while the passive party was the one who allowed the opponent's possible actions to determine his own choices. His laughter occurred before the seal was lifted and before Zhang Fan attempted to force his hand. It therefore marked a point at which Chen Ran had begun considering whether his apparent lack of options was itself the product of his own hesitation.

The timing of the next event made Zhang Fan's response decisive. In a dilapidated temple in the western part of a city, a young beggar had once shared half of a piece of moldy cornbread with an old beggar who was close to starving. The young beggar had learned from another beggar, Scarhead, that extreme hunger could drive people toward wickedness, but Scarhead had ultimately been beaten to death after trying to seize food from others. The young beggar consequently developed his own interpretation of what it meant to oppose wickedness. If depravity came from hunger, then benevolence should lead toward being able to eat one's fill. Yet sharing half of his food with the old beggar had not solved his own hunger, so he asked when people like them would finally have enough to eat and what meaning their lives possessed if they remained trapped in the same condition. The old beggar answered that as long as they remained alive, there would still be hope and the possibility that they would eventually eat their fill.

This memory was important because it established the principle Zhang Fan used to justify continuing the struggle even when his immediate prospects looked hopeless. His past as a beggar had taught him to regard survival not as evidence that victory was guaranteed, but as the minimum condition required for another opportunity to appear. The fact that he had reached the level of a True Self Player despite that background also explained why the others could not safely assume that his current disadvantage would determine the final outcome. Zhang Fan was accustomed to surviving situations in which the available resources were insufficient, and his system allowed him to exploit opportunities that the other players could not use in the same way. When the restrictions on the Liar Killer panels disappeared, he immediately reached for his weapon and returned to the contest. The memory of the old beggar's words became the basis of his decision: even if he was now facing three opponents, remaining alive was enough to preserve the possibility of turning the situation around.

The disappearance of the restrictions was itself the result of the development on the River of Time. Future Chen Ran had returned the Liar Killer that had been lent to him, removing the condition that had kept the Secret Chamber sealed and the four players' skills prohibited. Zhang Fan immediately recognized that this was the opportunity he had been waiting for. Rather than attempting to escape through a slow exchange of attacks, he used [Mind Follows Will] to launch a lethal attack against Chen Ran at the moment the restrictions were released. His immediate objective was to force Chen Ran into activating Eternal Kingdom. The arrangement of the battlefield made this far more dangerous than an ordinary direct attack, because a trap had been established beneath Chen Ran's chair through a Whisperer Secret Chamber. The moment the trap was triggered, arrows, evil spirits, and blades rushed toward Chen Ran from every direction. The interval between activation and impact was so short that even the other True Self Players had almost no time to react, and the attack was designed to leave Chen Ran with no practical alternative if he wanted to survive.

Chen Ran nevertheless responded immediately. His Extreme Realm gave him the reaction speed needed to act before the trap could kill him, and he drew his Liar Killer and activated [Whisperer: Eternal Kingdom] without hesitation. The arrows, evil spirits, and blades disappeared before reaching him, and the structure of the Secret Chamber began to dissolve into darkness. Ling Chi was horrified by the speed of Chen Ran's response because he understood that Zhang Fan had not simply attempted to kill Chen Ran. He had deliberately created a situation in which Chen Ran would be compelled to use his ultimate skill, regardless of whether Chen Ran believed that doing so was the correct strategic decision. The trap exploited the difference between knowing that a skill was dangerous and being willing to accept that danger when the alternative was immediate death. Zhang Fan expected Chen Ran to hesitate because Eternal Kingdom might destroy the Eighteenth Floor and kill the people caught within it. Instead, Chen Ran acted as though he had already accepted that possibility, which was precisely the response that made Zhang Fan's plan possible while also introducing the risk that Zhang Fan himself had failed to account for.

Zhang Fan's intended escape depended on the assumption that the Secret Chamber occupied a wild space adjacent to the Eighteenth Floor rather than an ordinary instance space. Under that interpretation, activating Eternal Kingdom would collapse the Eighteenth Floor while leaving the second Secret Chamber of the instance outside the skill's effective range. Chen Ran, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi would then be trapped within the area affected by Eternal Kingdom, leaving them vulnerable to the subsequent attacks of the Omniscient and Omnipotent once their skills were prohibited. Zhang Fan, however, would already have teleported himself into the second Secret Chamber and would not suffer the same consequences. His plan therefore transformed Chen Ran's strongest skill into a means of separating the four players and eliminating three of them simultaneously. It was not enough for Zhang Fan merely to escape the original Secret Chamber; he needed to place himself in a location where the destructive effect would not reach him while allowing the other three to remain exposed.

The second part of his plan depended on the Black Lotus already planted inside Han Fei's consciousness by the Zhang Fan from the true timeline. Zhang Fan believed that once the Eternal Kingdom eliminated Chen Ran and the others, the Zhang Fan who had escaped to the second Secret Chamber could use the existing Black Lotus as a route through which the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land could escape by taking possession of another body. The latter possessed the more powerful version of the [Dao Heart Demonic Seed], so the Black Lotus he had established would not be comparable to the two weaker Black Lotuses that Chen Yang and Ling Chi had planted in Zhang Fan's own consciousness. Even if the two of them attempted to take possession of him after the transfer, their Black Lotuses would be unable to withstand the overwhelming difference in strength. Once the Zhang Fan from the true timeline obtained a suitable host, he could use [Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation] to escape the restrictions that had kept him sealed, while the resulting possession could also eliminate other players within the instance. His intended victory was therefore not simply a one-against-three confrontation. It was an attempt to use the four-way struggle to provide the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land with another route back into the world.

The scale of that plan explains why Zhang Fan was willing to sacrifice his immediate safety and why the other three had underestimated the danger of allowing him to reach the second Secret Chamber. His current condition was disastrous, but the Black Lotus inside Han Fei represented an independent resource established by a much stronger version of himself. If the transfer succeeded, the exhaustion inflicted by Chen Yang and Ling Chi would cease to be decisive because the consciousness taking over the new host would not depend entirely on the weakened Zhang Fan in the Secret Chamber. He had also accounted for the causal connection between Jiang Zhe and his Main Body, reasoning that he could use the skills gained through possession to escape and kill the Main Body, leaving the other players without the means to leave the instance. The plan appeared to create a situation in which every possible response from Chen Ran benefited him: if Chen Ran used Eternal Kingdom, the Eighteenth Floor would collapse; if Chen Ran refused to act, Chen Yang could provide a resurrection effect that would keep them alive temporarily, giving Zhang Fan enough time to execute the possession. Either result was supposed to eliminate the three opponents while opening an alternative route for the Zhang Fan trapped in the Eternal Land.

The struggle on the River of Time developed alongside this attempted escape. Future Chen Ran no longer possessed the Liar Killer at his waist, confirming that the restriction responsible for the Secret Chamber's seal had been removed. When Zhang Fan withdrew from the River of Time and disappeared, the other True Self Players did not simply restore the previous arrangement and drag him back into the conflict. They understood that the conditions governing the larger confrontation were different from the conditions of the immediate struggle inside the Secret Chamber. If one player from the Ninth Timeline escaped, that would already satisfy the objective of the corresponding group on the River of Time, regardless of which person managed to get out. Consequently, the others accepted Zhang Fan's departure and concentrated their attacks on the First True Self Player, buying time for him to reach the second Secret Chamber. Their intervention demonstrated that the struggle inside the Secret Chamber was connected to a larger contest whose participants could evaluate victory according to different conditions. The escape of one person could satisfy one side's immediate objective even though that person's continued existence might create another problem for the players who controlled the true timeline.

Zhang Fan arrived in the second Secret Chamber and immediately found Han Fei lying on the ground. He believed that the most difficult part of his plan had succeeded because the Black Lotus established in Han Fei's consciousness was still present and appeared ready to emerge. The Black Lotuses planted by Chen Yang and Ling Chi had already begun consuming his Spirit, but he did not regard their attacks as decisive because the Black Lotus belonging to the Zhang Fan from the true timeline was vastly stronger. He expected the stronger Black Lotus to overwhelm the two weaker ones and allow the possession to proceed. As long as the Zhang Fan from the true timeline could take over the appropriate host, the damage suffered by the version who had escaped from the Secret Chamber would cease to matter. He therefore reached toward the Black Lotus, convinced that he was about to secure a victory that would allow the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land to escape and remove Chen Ran, his most dangerous opponent, from the equation.

The skill command that interrupted him completely overturned that expectation. When the light returned, Zhang Fan found Chen Ran, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi standing in front of him, despite having believed that Eternal Kingdom would leave them trapped within the collapsing Eighteenth Floor. He immediately attempted to use [Mind Follows Will], but the skill did not respond. The Black Lotus began emerging from Han Fei's body, and Zhang Fan reached toward it, believing that the three opponents were unable to intervene in time. Chen Ran's reaction speed should have allowed him to move, but Chen Ran remained still, while Chen Yang and Ling Chi also appeared unable to stop the possession directly. Zhang Fan interpreted their stillness as confirmation that he had finally obtained the necessary opening. Before he could complete the transfer, however, eleven Worlds of the Heart descended and immobilized everyone in the Secret Chamber. Eleven enormous hands reached through the connection to the River of Time and crushed the Black Lotus that had emerged from Han Fei. The intervention did not merely interrupt Zhang Fan's possession; it destroyed the object on which his entire escape plan depended, leaving no remaining route through which the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land could take over the host.

Zhang Fan collapsed because his mental state had already been pushed to its limit and the destruction of the Black Lotus invalidated the outcome he had spent the entire confrontation trying to secure. The contradiction finally became clear to him. If Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom had truly affected a wild space adjacent to the Eighteenth Floor, then Chen Ran, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi should have been subjected to the collapse of the Eighteenth Floor rather than appearing together in the second Secret Chamber. Eternal Kingdom possessed Dispel and prohibition effects, but it could not reset the positions of players or items or simply erase the boundary separating one instance from another. The fact that the three had survived and that Zhang Fan's skills were now prohibited demonstrated that the Secret Chamber had not been located in the wild space he had assumed. Chen Yang had transferred the internal-strife Secret Chamber into the second Secret Chamber of the instance while clearing the Eighteenth Floor, meaning that Eternal Kingdom had only affected the instance itself. The three had never been exposed to the collapse of the Eighteenth Floor, and Zhang Fan's attempt to place himself outside the skill's range had been based on a false understanding of the battlefield.

The failure was not merely the result of Zhang Fan overlooking a technical restriction. His plan depended on Chen Ran choosing the response that Zhang Fan considered psychologically and strategically unlikely, yet Chen Ran had used Eternal Kingdom without hesitation. Zhang Fan had calculated that Chen Ran would be more likely to refrain from acting because he feared destroying the Eighteenth Floor and dying together with the others. If Chen Ran refused to activate Eternal Kingdom, Chen Yang could provide a temporary resurrection effect, allowing the three to survive the trap long enough for Zhang Fan to use the time difference created by the Whisperer Secret Chamber. Meanwhile, the Zhang Fan from the true timeline would possess Han Fei and Jiang Zhe, then use the causal relationship between Jiang Zhe and his Main Body to eliminate the Main Body as well. Once this was accomplished, Chen Yang would be the only person among the three who could potentially use Jiang Zhe's skills to escape, leaving Chen Ran and Ling Chi trapped and eventually exhausted. Zhang Fan therefore treated Chen Ran's reluctance to use Eternal Kingdom as the central assumption supporting his victory.

Instead, Chen Ran selected the response that Zhang Fan had considered to have a probability of less than twenty percent. The reason was connected directly to the theories Chen Yang had explained earlier. The principle that a king does not meet another king meant that a confrontation between equally powerful people should not be interpreted as a situation in which both sides could act freely without exposing themselves to mutual destruction. If one side had already initiated such a confrontation, it suggested that the side initiating the conflict believed its objective could be achieved. Chen Yang's theory of active and passive behavior added the necessary decision rule: a player who allowed fear of the opponent to determine his actions became passive, while a player willing to act according to his own judgment could seize the initiative. Chen Ran had previously appeared to be laughing at his own predicament, but Zhang Fan now realized that the laughter might have marked the moment when Chen Ran connected the two principles and understood what Chen Yang was communicating. Chen Yang had not needed to tell his brother explicitly to activate Eternal Kingdom, because the argument itself supplied the reason for doing so. Chen Ran had chosen the dangerous option precisely because he no longer regarded the danger as a sufficient reason to remain passive.

The intervention of the eleven Worlds of the Heart added another layer to the result. The players on the River of Time did not merely prevent the four people in the Secret Chamber from moving; they deliberately destroyed the Black Lotus that would have allowed the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land to escape through possession. Zhang Fan had treated the Black Lotus as a resource that would inevitably favor him because of the difference between his Nine-Star version and the weaker Black Lotuses planted by Chen Yang and Ling Chi. However, he had not accounted for the interests of the True Self Players who could interfere with the process. The same group that had permitted him to escape the River of Time did not necessarily intend to allow the possession to succeed or the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land to return to the true timeline. The distinction between allowing someone to escape from one conflict and allowing that person to obtain the outcome he desired from another was decisive.
