Zhang Fan had mistaken the assistance given to one stage of his plan for permission to complete the entire plan, even though the players controlling the larger structure had their own reasons to intervene once the Black Lotus began to threaten their preferred arrangement.

As Zhang Fan's consciousness weakened, he reconstructed the connection between Chen Yang's earlier reasoning and the outcome. The theory of kings not meeting had implied that Chen Ran could act without allowing the apparent danger to control his response, while the distinction between active and passive behavior had explained why Chen Yang was willing to leave the decision to him. The two theories had not been unrelated observations about the behavior of powerful people. Together, they meant that the only way to escape the position Zhang Fan had constructed for Chen Ran was to reject the assumption that Chen Ran would prioritize avoiding danger over taking action. Chen Ran had understood that the Secret Chamber's restrictions and the larger conflict on the River of Time prevented Zhang Fan from controlling every part of the result. If he used Eternal Kingdom, the actual consequences would depend on the boundaries of the instance and the actions of the True Self Players, rather than on Zhang Fan's preferred interpretation of the situation. Zhang Fan could not force Chen Ran to accept his own understanding of the battlefield simply because that understanding appeared reasonable.

Zhang Fan also recognized that Chen Yang had been the reason Chen Ran could act with such confidence. Chen Yang had deliberately allowed Zhang Fan to believe that his plan could succeed, while the ideas he presented earlier had given Chen Ran a basis for identifying the intended response. The apparent choice between using Eternal Kingdom and doing nothing had been designed to trap Chen Ran, but the trap depended on Chen Ran treating the two options as Zhang Fan had framed them. Once Chen Ran understood the active and passive principle, he no longer had to choose between the consequences Zhang Fan expected. He could act first and allow the other participants to determine how the larger system would respond. Zhang Fan had therefore lost not because he lacked a sufficiently complicated plan, but because his plan had been built around a prediction of another True Self Player's behavior that did not account for the possibility that the player had already reconstructed the underlying reasoning.

Chen Yang then turned toward Ling Chi and asked whether he intended to continue resisting. Ling Chi understood that the position had changed beyond the point where he could reasonably expect to reverse the result. Zhang Fan was unconscious, his own skills were prohibited by Eternal Kingdom, and Chen Ran and Chen Yang were both in a position to prevent him from taking possession of Zhang Fan. If Ling Chi continued attacking them with mental techniques, the two brothers could simply wear him down. Chen Yang would eventually obtain Zhang Fan's remaining skills through Imprinting, while Ling Chi would be sent into an independent space in the Underworld and subjected to mental attacks from several Superego Players. The combination of these disadvantages left Ling Chi without a practical method of escaping the arrangement. He could continue fighting, but doing so would not change the fundamental conditions that had already determined his position. He therefore concluded that remaining alive would only prolong a struggle in which he had lost the means to protect his own interests.

Ling Chi nevertheless had another reason to reject Chen Ran's possible attempt to cooperate with him against Chen Yang. Once Chen Ran activated Eternal Kingdom and the two of them did not disappear, Ling Chi could infer that he would not be allowed to remain on the true timeline. The same skill that had removed the trap also represented a direct threat to his system, because Eternal Kingdom could prohibit the skills of a selected target while leaving other participants able to use theirs. Ling Chi's system depended on his ability to apply different mental states and combat techniques, so the complete prohibition of his skills would leave him at an extreme disadvantage. Chen Yang, meanwhile, possessed both the Ghost Path Soldier and the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique, giving him enough strength and flexibility to defeat Ling Chi in a direct mental confrontation. Ling Chi therefore understood that even if he avoided dying immediately, he would still face a situation in which Chen Ran and Chen Yang could eventually eliminate him. His suicide was not simply an admission that his current plan had failed; it also denied Chen Ran the opportunity to use him as an ally against Chen Yang.

Chen Ran attempted to stop Ling Chi before he pulled the trigger, but Ling Chi deliberately ended the exchange by declaring that he had lied. Chen Ran recognized the statement and responded that Ling Chi had lied, yet Ling Chi immediately shot himself in the temple. The action left Chen Ran without the ally he had hoped to use against his brother, forcing him to confront Chen Yang alone. The suicide also served Ling Chi's own calculation: if he could not remain on the true timeline, then removing himself from the struggle was preferable to allowing Chen Yang to dictate the terms of his defeat. His final decision made the relationship between the three players even more unequal. Zhang Fan had been rendered unconscious, Ling Chi was dead, and Chen Ran now faced the only remaining opponent capable of exploiting the destruction of the original arrangement. Chen Yang, who had repeatedly manipulated the other players while concealing his true priorities, could now redirect the struggle toward the conflict he had intended to establish between the two brothers.

Chen Yang did not immediately attack Chen Ran. Instead, he asked whether Chen Ran understood why Zhang Fan, Ling Chi, and himself had not disappeared after Eternal Kingdom was activated. The first part of the answer concerned the skill's actual function. Eternal Kingdom could Dispel and prohibit, but it did not reset the positions of players or items. The second part concerned the intervention of the True Self Players on the River of Time. Apart from Zhang Fan and Ling Chi on the true timeline, the other ten Half-Step True Self Mind Cultivation Players did not want either of those two to remain on the true timeline. Zhang Fan's ability to devour skills and continue expanding his system made him a threat that could not safely be allowed to develop without restraint, while Ling Chi's ability to extinguish skills would undermine the mechanisms through which the powerful players controlled and observed the larger structure. If Zhang Fan remained free to absorb more systems, the danger would continue increasing; if Ling Chi remained on the true timeline, the others would have to consider whether their own skills could be neutralized before they could be used.

This was why Chen Yang had described the role of a great scholar who would defend the scriptures for him. He had arranged the immediate situation so that the True Self Players could obtain an outcome that already served their interests, allowing their own preferences to determine the action they would take. Once Zhang Fan's Black Lotus began to threaten the possibility that the Zhang Fan sealed in the Eternal Land could escape, the ten players had reason to intervene, and their combined action destroyed it. The same intervention prevented Eternal Kingdom from producing the result Zhang Fan expected, because the players on the River of Time were not obligated to allow the disappearance of Chen Ran, Chen Yang, and Ling Chi merely because that outcome was part of Zhang Fan's plan. The skill's actual range and the interests of the True Self Players together determined the result. Chen Yang had therefore relied on a combination of technical understanding and political calculation, ensuring that the players who possessed the power to alter the outcome would act according to priorities he had already anticipated.

The larger arrangement was a transaction between two factions. The players associated with the River of Time accepted the possibility that Chen Ran might die inside the instance, while the Omniscient and Omnipotent accepted the possibility that Chen Yang might remain on the true timeline. Neither side could dictate every part of the result without exposing itself to the other's interference, and the creation of the instance reflected that mutual limitation. Chen Yang, however, occupied a different position from the True Self Players who had already established their own systems and interests. He was a product of the Ninth True Self Player's creation of other timelines, and he did not possess the same attachment to the existing arrangement or the same need to preserve a particular position within it. If he lost, he would lose a life that the larger structure already treated as expendable. The other True Self Players, by contrast, had much more to lose if their systems, established positions, or control over the River of Time were compromised. Their greater power therefore came with constraints that Chen Yang could exploit. He could take risks that they could not accept, then use the outcomes of those risks to influence their actions.

Chen Yang's method was closely connected to his cultivation of [Unity of Heaven and Man Mind Cultivation]. In Hell, the concept of Heaven had effectively become the True Self Players who controlled the fundamental structure of the world. Their interests determined which arrangements could persist and which threats would be removed. Acting in accordance with Heaven therefore meant acting in accordance with the interests of those players, while the principle that justice was legitimacy described the way their preferred outcomes became the effective rules of the system. Chen Yang did not need to force the True Self Players to obey him directly. He needed to construct a situation in which their own understanding of what must be protected led them to make the decisions he wanted. Zhang Fan was precisely the sort of individual they would not willingly allow to grow without limit, because his ability to devour skills could eventually undermine their systems. Ling Chi posed the opposite but equally serious threat, because his ability to destroy skills could prevent the Omniscient from using skills to observe the timeline, the Omnipotent from applying their abilities without restraint, and the Unity of Heaven and Man from maintaining the blockade of the Eighteenth Floor. Chen Yang used these established interests to make the True Self Players act as the Heaven that justified the outcome he had prepared.

He then explained why Ling Chi had preferred to die rather than cooperate with Chen Ran. After seeing that the three of them remained in the instance, Ling Chi understood that the larger arrangement did not permit him to remain on the true timeline. He also knew that Chen Yang's combination of Ghost Path Soldier and the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique made him particularly difficult to defeat through mental attacks. If Ling Chi remained alive and tried to fight Chen Yang directly, he would eventually be forced into a confrontation in which his skills had already been restricted and the other side possessed the advantage. More importantly, Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom represented the principle of One, and after its ultimate sublimation it could prohibit a selected person or item. If Chen Ran chose to prohibit Ling Chi's skills while leaving Chen Yang's skills unaffected, Ling Chi would be unable to employ the combat techniques on which his system depended. He lacked the kinds of time, space, or resurrection abilities that might allow him to bypass the prohibition. For Ling Chi, allowing Chen Ran to survive would therefore preserve a threat that he could not reliably counter, even if Chen Yang also remained dangerous. His suicide was intended to remove the possibility of joining Chen Ran against Chen Yang, thereby increasing the likelihood that the brothers would eliminate one another.

Chen Yang finally returned to the question he had raised after Ling Chi's death. He told Chen Ran that he was different from the other participants because he was his brother, then asked whether Chen Ran believed he would kill him. Chen Ran had already seen Chen Yang manipulate the other True Self Players, misdirect Zhang Fan, exploit Ling Chi's circumstances, and arrange the confrontation so that the larger forces would respond according to their own interests. He therefore could not simply assume that brotherhood would prevent Chen Yang from attacking him, especially after Chen Yang had deliberately removed both of their remaining opponents and left the two of them alone. Chen Yang reinforced the pressure by recalling the advice Chen Ran had received from Di Wu Zhi Yi through Qiu Yinong's memories: in a dog-eat-dog environment such as Hell, a player should not trust others or develop an emotional identification with them. By invoking that principle while demanding an answer about their relationship, Chen Yang forced Chen Ran to evaluate whether the bond between them was strong enough to override everything he had learned about survival and deception. Chen Ran retreated as Chen Yang advanced, unable to settle the contradiction between the possibility that his brother genuinely cared about him and the evidence that Chen Yang had arranged the entire confrontation to leave him with no safe alternative. Chen Yang stopped only after determining that Chen Ran still had no answer, then stated that he would provide the answer himself as his [Soldier] appeared before them.

Chen Yang's Soldier did not turn its weapon toward Chen Ran. Instead, it aimed at Zhang Fan, who was still lying on the ground, and fired [Radiant Three-Kills · Heaven and Earth One Sword]. The attack immediately produced two screams from within Zhang Fan's body, one belonging to Zhang Fan himself and the other to Ling Chi, before Zhang Fan slowly stood up and mocked the two of them for attempting to deceive him through a trick of hiding in plain sight. This revealed that Chen Yang had already successfully subjected Zhang Fan to Possession through the Black Lotus planted in his consciousness. Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had apparently attempted to exploit the confusion surrounding the possession to recover their mental strength and reverse the situation, but Chen Yang had anticipated their attempt and used his Soldier to attack Zhang Fan before they could complete their plan. The two had been depending on the possibility of destroying Chen Yang's Black Lotus and using the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] to restore their depleted Spirits, because doing so would have given them another opportunity to attack Chen Yang or help Chen Ran escape his control. By acting first, Chen Yang eliminated that possibility and ensured that Zhang Fan could no longer independently resist the possession, leaving Chen Ran with neither the skills nor the mental entities necessary to counter him inside the Secret Chamber.

Chen Yang then explained why he had deliberately arranged the situation this way. Eternal Kingdom had already sealed the entire Secret Chamber, and although Chen Ran could still use its underlying authority, the restrictions prevented the other players from freely deploying their skills to escape or reverse the outcome. If Zhang Fan and Ling Chi had been allowed to destroy the Black Lotus and restore their mental strength, Chen Ran might have had a chance to use them as allies and turn the situation around. Chen Yang therefore intended to eliminate every source of assistance before proceeding to possess Chen Ran himself. Zhang Fan had already lost control of his own consciousness, while Ling Chi had been reduced to a voice inside the same body, meaning that neither could provide the independent resistance necessary to prevent Chen Yang from completing his plan. The remaining objective was to seize Chen Ran's body and obtain Eternal Kingdom, a skill that could be carried into the true timeline without introducing another copy of [Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation]. Zhang Fan's skill was unsuitable for this purpose because one version of [Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation] already existed on the true timeline, and the other True Self Players would not permit a second version to remain there. Eternal Kingdom presented a different opportunity, since Chen Yang could obtain its authority through Possession and thereby gain a system that the other players might tolerate on the true timeline even though they would not accept Zhang Fan's ability to devour and accumulate skills indefinitely.

Chen Yang consequently ordered Chen Ran to answer whether he believed his older brother would kill him, advancing while Chen Ran retreated. He then invoked the three states Chen Ran had cultivated, identifying them as the Half-Step Superego State of Mind, the Ghost Path Soldier technique associated with Supreme Goodness is Like Water, and the Ego Extreme Realm. Chen Yang's [Radiant Three-Kills] possessed three corresponding attacks, allowing him to target the foundations of Chen Ran's existing systems rather than relying on a single overwhelming mental assault. As Chen Yang's Soldier raised its sniper rifle, Chen Ran noticed that its mental energy was recovering at an abnormal rate even after the first attack, making it clear that Chen Yang could continue launching attacks without suffering the depletion that should have followed such powerful techniques. The first sword, [Heaven and Earth One Sword], represented Only Self, meaning the cultivation of one's own strength. Its bullet entered Chen Ran's body and appeared within No-Distance, where the corresponding Chen Ran summoned [Wait a Moment] and fired repeatedly, attempting to stop the attack before it reached him. The shots were nevertheless chopped apart by the incoming sword, and the Chen Ran inside No-Distance was subsequently hacked into pieces, demonstrating that the first attack could overwhelm even the defensive mechanisms Chen Ran had cultivated for his own survival.

The second sword, [Heavenly Emperor One Sword], represented Only Emperor, meaning the acquisition of status and the power that came from standing at the very top. Within Chen Ran's No-Distance, the attack manifested as a towering figure standing upon a mountain peak, with countless particles converging into a precious sword at his command. Each particle represented a player using a different Mental Attack, and their combined power formed a single sword light that struck Chen Ran's consciousness. The Chen Ran inside No-Distance appeared in a Shamate-style youth's appearance, humming casually until he perceived the immense difference between his own combat strength and the sword approaching him. He estimated that his own strength amounted to roughly one thousand points, whereas the sword's strength reached at least one million, and immediately attempted to solicit support from the viewers of his livestream by asking them to send gifts that would increase his combat power. The absurdity of this behavior did not lessen the significance of the attack, because even Chen Ran's attempt to acquire additional strength through an external source was useless when the sword light could destroy him before the assistance arrived. The sword's approach dismembered the Shamate-style Chen Ran and eventually reduced even his remaining mouth to fragments, showing that a sufficiently overwhelming difference in power could render an opponent's defensive tricks and attempts at obtaining assistance completely meaningless.

The third sword, [Heaven's Will One Sword], represented Only Multitude, meaning that Heaven's Will and the principle of justice as legitimacy had become the decisive source of authority. Unlike the previous two manifestations, the Chen Ran inside No-Distance was filled with mental energy and had advanced close to the Superego State of Mind, allowing him to transform into a giant thousands of feet tall and attempt to crush the enemy with an enormous stomp. The figure holding the Heavenly Emperor Sword nevertheless remained expressionless and simply slashed once, causing the gigantic Chen Ran to collapse as though he had been made of paper. The three swords therefore represented more than three unrelated offensive abilities, because together they described the structure of Chen Yang's own life: grassroots experience and personal cultivation developed his abilities, advancement through the official system granted him increasingly powerful positions, and those abilities and positions ultimately allowed him to pursue his ambitions by aligning himself with the authority that determined legitimacy. This also explained why his [Unity of Heaven and Man] attainment was so unusually high. His cultivation was not restricted to increasing his own strength through individual effort, because he had understood how personal ability, institutional power, and the interests of those controlling the wider system could reinforce one another. Through the three swords, he could turn these different forms of authority into direct mental attacks, and the resulting combination destroyed Chen Ran's three states almost simultaneously.

Chen Ran's mental energy immediately withered after the three attacks, leaving him pale, vomiting bile, and struggling to remain upright. Before he could recover, he noticed that Chen Yang's mental energy had begun spreading toward him like thin vines, entering his consciousness and forming a Black Lotus. The situation made the danger of Possession unmistakable, because Chen Yang was no longer merely attacking Chen Ran's mental states from the outside; he was establishing a foothold inside Chen Ran's consciousness and replacing his identity from within. Qiu Yinong, Lin Xuan, Jiang Zhe, Nan Sheng, and Chen Nuo recognized that Chen Ran was in immediate danger and prepared to launch Mental Attacks against Chen Yang, but Chen Yang's Soldier transformed into a towering demon and released a roar that shook everyone present. The force of the roar overwhelmed not only those who had intended to intervene but also the surrounding players who had not planned to participate, leaving them limp and unconscious before they could complete their attacks. This prevented Chen Ran from receiving outside assistance and demonstrated the difference between Chen Yang's present strength and the condition of the other players, whose mental energy had already been depleted by the struggle. With the other participants incapacitated, the Black Lotus continued transforming Chen Ran's consciousness into Chen Yang's likeness, allowing Chen Yang to seize his weakened opponent directly and demand an answer to the same question: whether he would kill his own younger brother.

Chen Ran could barely resist the hand holding him, yet he still raised his middle finger at Chen Yang instead of providing the answer he wanted. Chen Yang interpreted this reaction as another attempt to avoid confronting the contradiction in Chen Ran's own beliefs. If Chen Ran truly believed that nobody could be trusted and that no identification with another person was permissible, then relying on Chen Yang at the most dangerous moment should have been impossible, particularly when Chen Yang had already threatened to kill him and possessed the strength to carry out that threat. Nevertheless, Chen Ran had used Eternal Kingdom without hesitation after receiving Chen Yang's hint, accepting the possibility that his brother was helping him despite having repeatedly been taught by Hell that survival required absolute distrust. Chen Yang argued that Chen Ran's decision to refuse the [Ghost Path Soldier] and [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] had likewise depended upon the assumption that Chen Yang would teach him those techniques later inside No-Distance. Chen Ran had apparently believed that his brother would continue to provide him with the means to survive, even while presenting himself to the other True Self Players as someone who refused to trust anyone. Chen Yang therefore accused him of maintaining a contradiction between his stated survival theory and his actual behavior, because the very decision that had saved him from Zhang Fan's trap demonstrated that he still possessed trust in another person.

Chen Yang then forced the contradiction into a direct question by pointing out that the two possible outcomes would each determine whether Chen Ran's belief had been correct. If Chen Yang killed him, then the belief that nobody could be trusted would be vindicated, but if Chen Yang spared him, then Chen Ran would have to acknowledge that his belief was not universally correct. The difficulty was that Chen Ran had acted on the possibility of being spared even while claiming to believe that he would be killed, meaning that his actual choice had already contradicted the rigid principle he professed to follow. Chen Yang's accusation was not simply that Chen Ran had been foolish to trust his brother, because he was deliberately testing whether Chen Ran's understanding of human nature had become completely subordinated to Hell's survival logic. Chen Ran's willingness to activate Eternal Kingdom had exposed a remaining part of his original self that still believed his brother would not abandon him, and Chen Yang intended to force that part into the open. He tightened his grip as though he could crush Chen Ran's consciousness at any moment and demanded that Chen Ran decide whether his belief was correct or wrong, leaving him with no opportunity to hide behind another joke or evade the question through silence.

Chen Ran remained silent, refusing to provide the answer Chen Yang wanted, and the stalemate continued until Chen Yang finally released him and allowed him to fall onto the ground. Rather than immediately continuing the attack, Chen Yang produced a cigarette and a chair, sat down, and mocked Chen Ran for sitting on the floor as though he were a helpless child who belonged to nobody. When Chen Ran complained that he could not get up and demanded help, Chen Yang continued portraying himself as the older brother who had merely wanted to discipline his younger sibling. He described himself as the cherished legitimate eldest son of the family, the person entrusted with authority by their grandparents and relatives, and the gold-medal henchman who was expected to carry out their wishes. The exaggerated description was intended to reassert the ordinary relationship between the brothers after Chen Yang had just subjected Chen Ran to an overwhelming display of violence, suggesting that he regarded the confrontation as a form of discipline rather than an actual attempt to kill him. However, the sniper rifle still rested between Chen Yang's knees, making it impossible to interpret the exchange as a complete return to safety. When Chen Ran asked him to put the weapon away, Chen Yang admitted that he had originally intended to execute Chen Ran if he answered even one word incorrectly, but had simply forgotten to remove the rifle after changing his mind about continuing the questioning. The casual admission did not make his earlier threat harmless, because it confirmed that the possibility of killing Chen Ran had been genuine and that Chen Yang could still decide to resume the attack if his brother's response displeased him.

Chen Yang then criticized Chen Ran's habit of relying on the idea that deterrence fundamentally meant mutual destruction, explaining that an academic would express the same principle as the game-theoretical relationship in which a loss for both sides could be preferable to allowing one side to win at the expense of the other. Chen Ran objected to his brother's tendency to present ordinary observations as if they were profound academic discoveries, but Chen Yang dismissed the objection by comparing it to their childhood disagreements. When Chen Ran was young, Chen Yang would warn him about an approaching puddle and tell him not to step into it, only for Chen Ran to step into it anyway and later admit that the puddle had been there. Chen Yang claimed that his advice had repeatedly been correct, but that Chen Ran disliked acknowledging its value because he did not want to demonstrate obedience in front of his older brother. He further argued that Chen Ran simultaneously wanted recognition from him and wanted to prove himself by challenging him, creating the familiar contradiction of a younger sibling who needed his older brother's approval but resisted accepting the guidance through which that approval might be earned. Chen Ran considered this interpretation another example of Chen Yang pretending to understand everything, yet he did not seriously disprove the underlying point. The exchange allowed Chen Yang to move the conversation away from the immediate threat of Possession and return to the question of whether Chen Ran had genuinely believed in Hell's survival logic or had merely adopted it as a defense against the possibility of trusting another person.

Chen Yang returned to the earlier events inside the Internal Strife Secret Chamber and argued that he had deliberately refrained from defeating the others immediately, despite possessing enough power to kill them at the beginning. He had pretended to be evenly matched with the other three because he wanted to observe their reactions and test whether their behavior remained consistent with their professed beliefs. Chen Ran's response had been particularly revealing because he used Eternal Kingdom without hesitation after Chen Yang supplied the necessary hint, showing that deep down he still believed his brother would help him rather than immediately exploit his vulnerability. Chen Yang therefore concluded that Chen Ran had not been completely consumed by the survival theory taught to him by Di Wu Zhi Yi, even if Hell's repeated lessons in distrust had made him believe that the principle was correct. His decision not to kill Chen Ran followed from that conclusion, because Chen Ran's behavior demonstrated that he still possessed the capacity to recognize another person and maintain a bond of trust despite the apparent logic of the environment. Chen Yang argued that Chen Ran still believed himself to be a good person beneath the accumulated effects of Hell, and he warned him that there was still time to return to the right path before he became like his future self. The single Liar Killer that Future Chen Ran had provided was therefore not only a clue intended to help Chen Ran escape the arrangement, but also a clue that Chen Yang could use to draw his younger brother back toward a decision that preserved his original nature.

The meaning of this test becomes clearer when viewed through the structure of the Reincarnation Layer. Chen Ran had previously interpreted the influence of the Superego as a source of distortion, assuming that the pressure it exerted on his thinking made him less capable of reaching an objective conclusion. Yet the events inside the Secret Chamber suggested that the problem was not simply the Superego's influence, because Mind Cultivation itself could be responsible for producing the rigid survival logic that prevented people from trusting one another. Mind Cultivation undeniably increased a player's strength, but its development also reinforced the belief that every person represented a potential threat and that cooperation was merely another opportunity for betrayal. Ling Chi's outcome on the true timeline illustrated the consequence of this principle: even a person who pursued peace could become trapped in a cycle of distrust and violence when his own cultivation prevented him from relying on others. If every player attempted to reach the desired outcome alone, then no one could escape the arrangement through trust, because each person would regard cooperation as a liability and eventually turn against those who might have helped them. Breaking this pattern therefore required a player to recognize that the survival theory was not an absolute truth, allowing the Superego to influence them toward finding like-minded companions rather than treating every relationship as a means of exploitation.

This was the purpose of the Reincarnation Layer, which had been constructed through Supreme Perfect Enlightenment's Mind Cultivation and existed within the player's own heart. The layer did not need to imprison someone inside an ordinary physical space, because its function was to force the person to repeat the same fundamental mistake whenever they attempted to overcome their circumstances. No matter how many times such a player repeated their life, the result would remain failure if their underlying understanding of human relationships never changed. Chen Yang had therefore designed the apparent struggle inside the Secret Chamber as a test of Chen Ran's heart, deliberately allowing the other players to appear dangerous enough that Chen Ran would have to choose between preserving himself through absolute distrust and accepting that his brother might still be someone he could rely upon. The test was effective precisely because Chen Ran had accumulated so much evidence supporting Hell's survival theory that his decision could not be explained as simple ignorance. He knew that betrayal was possible, understood the danger of the other True Self Players, and had experienced the consequences of trusting people in a world where deception was fundamental to survival. Yet when the decisive moment arrived, he still acted according to his underlying identification with Chen Yang, showing that the survival theory had never completely replaced his original values.

The previous Chen Ran, who believed that Hell's survival theory was the only rational way to live, was consequently the person who lost the test, because his own rigid understanding of the world had prevented him from recognizing what his behavior actually revealed. The success of the test allowed the Reincarnation Layer inside his heart to be Deciphered, and what emerged was the true Chen Ran who had existed before death, a person still possessing flesh-and-blood emotions, a sense of righteousness, and the capacity to form meaningful relationships with others. The distinction between the two was not that the new Chen Ran had suddenly become unaware of danger or incapable of acting strategically, but that he no longer needed to subordinate every decision to the assumption that nobody could be trusted. The idealist had initially been a materialist in the sense that the facts of Hell had forced him to accept the survival theory as the only workable description of reality, yet the questioning of his heart reversed that process and compelled him to confront the values he had tried to suppress. His victory therefore depended on recognizing that the logic of survival could be useful in understanding threats without being sufficient to determine how every relationship should be treated. By refusing to answer Chen Yang's question with a simplistic declaration and allowing his actual behavior to expose the contradiction, Chen Ran reached the point where the Reincarnation Layer could no longer compel him to repeat the same cycle of distrust.

The change was immediately reflected in the River of Time, where the Liar Killer at Future Chen Ran's waist flashed. The eleven Half-Step True Self Mind-Cultivation Players watching the confrontation recognized the significance of the change, because the Liar Killer's disappearance and subsequent reappearance indicated that it no longer belonged to the previous Future Chen Ran but to a newly established version of his future. Since Chen Ran had already Deciphered the Reincarnation Layer, the previous arrangement had lost the condition that had justified continued interference, and the True Self Players had no reason to prolong the struggle. Supreme Goodness is Like Water nodded to the others before disappearing, while Jie Mie took one final look at the Liar Killer and realized that he had been deceived, responding with an inward sigh before withdrawing. The masked woman then remarked that the young man had walked out of the dream of the jianghu and began moving downstream along the River of Time. Their departure showed that the change in Chen Ran's state had altered the larger timeline enough to make the immediate confrontation unnecessary, allowing the other True Self Players to stop fighting and accept the new outcome.

Chen Ran gradually recovered enough to open his eyes and found Chen Yang still present inside No-Distance, where the two brothers continued talking instead of immediately leaving the instance. Chen Yang snapped his fingers, causing his mental body to fade slightly while the Spirit overflowing from him helped Chen Ran's mental body recover. Chen Ran asked whether Chen Yang intended to remain there, then suggested that he might as well eliminate Yue Guanshan while leaving, but Chen Yang dismissed the suggestion as wishful thinking. The reason was not that Yue Guanshan could be ignored, but that the entire instance formed part of an agreement between the True Self Players, who had allowed the Secret Chamber to be created under an arrangement in which each faction accepted a different possible outcome. The Trio on the River of Time had accepted the possibility that Chen Ran might die inside the instance, while the Omniscient and Omnipotent had accepted the possibility that Chen Yang would remain on the true timeline. If Chen Yang immediately killed Yue Guanshan, he would overturn the Omniscient and Omnipotent's side of the arrangement by destroying the meaning of the instance, and they would respond by overturning the other side's arrangement as well. Under those circumstances, neither brother would escape, because the larger conflict would no longer be constrained by the transaction that had allowed the Secret Chamber to function in the first place. Chen Yang consequently warned Chen Ran that Yue Guanshan was a much more formidable opponent than he appeared, as his cultivation through Supreme Perfect Enlightenment had given him a solid foundation and he had survived an Ego Loss Tribulation that would have killed most people whose cultivation was interfered with during the process.

Chen Yang further explained that although Chen Ran and Chen Yang could rely on their systems to elevate their mental strength beyond Yue Guanshan's, this did not automatically make them superior in a battle of wits. Yue Guanshan was a Ghost Immortal who had survived the Ego Loss Tribulation and forcibly completed the Loss of Self, demonstrating that his accumulated foundation was exceptionally profound despite his apparent lack of luck. Chen Yang believed that Yue Guanshan would probably not lose to him in a contest of pure intelligence, and that defeating Chen Ran would be more than sufficient for someone with Yue Guanshan's capabilities. Chen Ran accepted the warning because the survival of a person through a heavily interfered Ego Loss Tribulation implied that their cultivation was not easily overturned through ordinary manipulation. The conversation then turned to Chen Ran's habit of expressing strategic principles through phrases such as the essence of deterrence being mutual destruction, which Chen Yang criticized as the sort of language that immediately revealed a lack of academic knowledge to anyone familiar with game theory. Chen Ran countered that the Academic School was excessively arrogant and that Folk Thought and Folk Philosophy had their own merits, especially because their concepts could be understood by teammates without requiring specialized terminology. Chen Yang responded that his earlier use of the principles that a king does not meet another king and that the active party differs from the passive party had also been expressed in ordinary language, yet Chen Ran had not necessarily understood their full implications. Chen Ran fell silent, because the events inside the Secret Chamber had demonstrated that he had grasped the practical outcome of those principles without necessarily understanding the cultivation theory underlying them.

Chen Yang then returned to their childhood relationship and asked whether Chen Ran remembered the time he had lied to him, reminding him that he had once said he could forgive his younger brother for lying about many things but would never tolerate a second occurrence. The question created tension because Chen Yang was not asking about an ordinary childhood incident; he was testing whether Chen Ran understood that being accepted as his brother did not mean that every action could be disregarded simply because the final result appeared satisfactory. Chen Ran demanded to know what Chen Yang intended to ask, but the latter eventually smiled and explained that he was merely curious. As his younger brother, Chen Ran was theoretically someone whose final outcome should matter more than the precise route he had taken to reach it, and since he had now returned to the right path by Deciphering the Reincarnation Layer, Chen Yang should have been able to leave the matter alone. Nevertheless, he could not suppress his curiosity about the moment immediately before he had been about to crush Chen Ran: whether Chen Ran had possessed enough strength to kill him instantly or whether the person standing before him had actually been Chen Ran's Soldier rather than his true consciousness. This question followed directly from Chen Ran's behavior in the Secret Chamber, because his refusal to learn the two cultivation methods seemed inconsistent with how quickly he had understood the underlying principles of the struggle. Chen Ran nevertheless denied having any knowledge of the Ghost Path Soldier and mocked Chen Yang for assuming that he did.

Chen Yang then explained why the possibility remained plausible. The principle that a king does not meet another king had a specific term within the Academic School, the Law of Increasing Entropy, while the distinction between the active and passive parties referred to the principle that Double-Loss was Greater than Single-Win. Both theories formed core components of the Mind Cultivation Method for the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique]. Ordinarily, deducing that technique required an extremely high attainment in [Unity of Heaven and Man], because its underlying method depended on understanding how those different strategic principles operated within a person's consciousness. However, if someone could deduce the Law of Increasing Entropy and the Double-Loss principle from the seemingly ordinary statements Chen Yang had made during the Secret Chamber struggle, the barrier to reconstructing the cultivation method would be greatly reduced. Chen Ran had already demonstrated his ability to analyze the practical significance of those principles, and if he had independently reconstructed the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] during the earlier confrontation, he could then have combined its mental activation effect with the insights gained from [Ghost Path Soldier: Supreme Goodness is Like Water, Joy] to deduce the Ghost Path Soldier cultivation method as well. With the Nine-Turn Ghost God Realm, the Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique, and Ghost Path Soldier all available, Chen Ran would have possessed three True Self systems, making it entirely plausible that he could have killed Chen Yang instantly during their confrontation.

Chen Ran interpreted the explanation as an elaborate attempt by Chen Yang to provide him with the two cultivation methods without openly admitting that he wanted to help him. The supposed question about whether Chen Ran had already acquired the techniques therefore became another example of Chen Yang constructing a complicated academic explanation to preserve his image as a knowledgeable master, when he could simply have offered the techniques directly. Chen Yang admitted that maintaining that image mattered to him, then asked Chen Ran whether he wanted the Mind Cultivation Methods for the [Three Corpses God-Transformation Technique] and [Ghost Path Soldier] passed to him immediately, provided that Chen Ran would cultivate them before challenging him to another fight. Chen Ran asked why Chen Yang had not offered them in the Secret Chamber, explaining that all three participants knew he belonged to the true timeline and might have interfered with him if he had acquired the techniques openly. Chen Yang challenged him to accept the offer now, and Chen Ran eagerly agreed because he believed that once his Spirit had recovered, he could use the new systems to beat his brother. Chen Yang then deliberately displayed his sniper rifle and remarked that the bullets were big and round, immediately causing Chen Ran to retract his request and insist that he no longer wanted the techniques. Even when Chen Yang repeatedly offered to pass them over, Chen Ran refused and swore that he did not want them, showing that he understood the threat of being used as the target of Chen Yang's next experiment.

Before Chen Yang could leave, Chen Ran asked whether Zhang Fan and Ling Chi might have been actors whom Chen Yang had arranged to participate in the Secret Chamber. Chen Ran's suspicion originated from the transaction governing the entire instance. The Trio had allowed the Omniscient and Omnipotent to create an opportunity to kill Chen Ran, while the Omniscient and Omnipotent had accepted the possibility that Chen Yang would remain on the true timeline. The Secret Chamber had been created to make the outcome dependent on the abilities of the participants rather than allowing either faction to dictate it completely. If Chen Ran's survival depended on whether he could kill Yue Guanshan, then Chen Yang's ability to remain on the true timeline should likewise have depended on whether he could overcome his opponents, who were Zhang Fan, Ling Chi, and Chen Ran. Their starting strengths had appeared roughly equal when they entered the Internal Strife Secret Chamber, but Chen Yang had eventually gained an advantage by using Zhang Fan's skills to learn Ghost Path Soldier. This created a contradiction that Chen Ran could not ignore, because Zhang Fan possessed [Dust Ruins Spirit Transformation] and should theoretically have been capable of traveling to different points along the River of Time to steal the same systems before Chen Yang could acquire them. If Zhang Fan had genuinely wanted Ghost Path Soldier, waiting until the internal conflict was almost over would have been an irrational strategy when he had the temporal abilities necessary to obtain it in advance.

Chen Yang attempted to explain this discrepancy by pointing out that Ling Chi's enlightenment of Ghost Path Soldier was a fixed point in time. He had traveled directly to that point and left countless clones in the surrounding timeline, preventing Zhang Fan from stealing the system whenever he approached the moment of enlightenment. Furthermore, the Ninth Restoration Time could restore the relevant timeline and remove Zhang Fan's memory of repeatedly attempting to obtain the technique, meaning that Zhang Fan would be blocked infinitely without retaining the knowledge necessary to change his approach. Chen Ran nevertheless identified a flaw in this explanation: if Chen Yang could prevent Zhang Fan from stealing Ghost Path Soldier during and after Ling Chi's enlightenment, then Zhang Fan could simply travel to a point before that enlightenment occurred and wait for the opportunity to acquire the system before Chen Yang established his interception. The existence of a fixed point did not explain why Zhang Fan could never reach a time outside the range of Chen Yang's preparations, nor did it explain why someone possessing such a powerful temporal ability would continue allowing his opponent to dictate the conditions under which the technique could be acquired. Chen Yang could only respond that Zhang Ran's failure to do so was something that would have to be explained by Zhang Fan himself, leaving the contradiction unresolved.

Chen Ran concluded that Zhang Fan must already have stolen Ghost Path Soldier and that Chen Yang should theoretically have been unable to obtain it independently, yet the result of the Secret Chamber was precisely the opposite. The simplest explanation was that Zhang Fan had acted throughout the confrontation, pretending not to possess the technique while allowing Chen Yang's schemes to proceed as though Chen Yang had gained a decisive advantage through his own preparations. Zhang Fan's apparent inability to respond would then have been part of a Plan B rather than evidence that he had truly been cornered. This plan would have required Zhang Fan and Chen Yang to know one another before entering the Secret Chamber and to exchange their respective cultivation systems in advance. Zhang Fan could plant a Black Lotus in Chen Yang's consciousness, while Chen Yang would arrange to bring that Black Lotus onto the true timeline through the outcome of the instance. Under such an arrangement, Zhang Fan would not need to defeat Chen Yang openly inside the chamber, because Chen Yang's successful escape would also provide a route through which Zhang Fan's influence could enter the true timeline. Zhang Fan could therefore permit Chen Yang to appear to possess the Ghost Path Soldier while retaining an alternative means of survival that did not depend on winning the immediate struggle. Chen Ran's accusation was that the supposed victory Chen Yang had achieved against Zhang Fan had been staged to conceal an agreement that already existed between them.

Chen Ran then applied the same reasoning to Ling Chi, whose behavior during the final moments of the Secret Chamber had been unusually difficult to explain. He acknowledged that he did not know Ling Chi's earlier history well enough to make claims about his motives, but he had observed the entirety of Ling Chi's actions during the confrontation and found the final decision inconsistent with the level of strategic understanding he had demonstrated beforehand. For most of the struggle, Ling Chi had acted carefully, making use of his system and recognizing the weaknesses of the other players, yet near the end he had allowed Zhang Fan to escape first and then chose suicide rather than continuing to pursue the most advantageous outcome. Chen Ran argued that the internal-strife Secret Chamber was a Wild Space created by players, meaning that its existence and rules directly affected Ling Chi. Once Future Chen Ran lifted the blockade, Ling Chi should have been capable of destroying the chamber with his own system. If Zhang Fan were eliminated first, Chen Yang's skills would no longer be able to determine the chamber's outcome, and Ling Chi would become the person whose ability was needed to destroy the remaining structure. This would place the initiative in Ling Chi's hands and allow him to demand that Black Lotuses be planted in Chen Ran's and Chen Yang's consciousnesses, leaving him with a method of threatening both opponents instead of relying on either one's goodwill.

Ling Chi therefore had no obvious reason to accept the plan that allowed Zhang Fan to escape before the final confrontation, because eliminating Zhang Fan first would have preserved Ling Chi's unique leverage and prevented the other two from coordinating their survival. His sudden decision to commit suicide was especially suspicious when considered alongside his knowledge that the chamber itself could be destroyed through his system. If he had genuinely wanted to survive independently, he could have used that advantage to seize control of the endgame rather than allowing the arrangement to collapse into a duel between the Chen brothers. Chen Ran consequently suspected that Ling Chi had also been acting according to a prior agreement with Chen Yang. The intended result would be that Chen Yang could carry both Zhang Fan's and Ling Chi's Black Lotuses onto the true timeline while presenting the events inside the Secret Chamber as though he had defeated two independent opponents. Chen Yang's apparent success would then conceal a larger operation in which he was not merely escaping the timeline controlled by the Ninth True Self Player, but also smuggling the two other True Self Players' influence into the true timeline under an arrangement that the remaining True Self Players might not recognize until it was too late.

Chen Yang responded with irritation, accusing Chen Ran of developing the habit of inventing crimes whenever he wanted to obtain benefits. Chen Ran replied that his deductions gave him a righteous cause to request compensation, because Chen Yang's apparent schemes had already provided enough evidence for him to suspect that the promised escape and the possession of the other players were connected to a larger agreement. Chen Yang eventually asked what Chen Ran actually wanted, allowing the discussion to move away from the accusation and toward the conditions under which the two brothers would cooperate after leaving the instance. Chen Ran first requested that Chen Yang resolve the Mental Seal imposed on Qiu Yinong by the Underworld, explaining that Qiu Yinong had been marked when she previously suffered from Loss of Self and that the seal could create problems later if Chen Yang began reorganizing the Underworld. Chen Yang agreed to help remove the problem after he had finished organizing the Underworld, confirming that he expected to possess a member of the Andersen Squad first and then use that position to carry out his plans. Chen Ran next requested detailed information about Shen Yuwei, Mei Zhixu, and Yu Xiangwan, including their lives before and after entering Hell and the complete details of their respective skills, and Chen Yang accepted this request without hesitation. Chen Ran then announced that he had one final question, prompting Chen Yang to glare at him suspiciously before Chen Ran asked who the person behind Lin Xuan was.

Chen Yang answered without hesitation that the person behind Lin Xuan was Lin Ou. Before Chen Ran could continue questioning him, Chen Yang sensed three extremely strong mental fluctuations and his expression changed from alarm to recognition, which meant that the immediate problem had shifted from the question of Lin Xuan's identity to the people approaching them. He told Chen Ran that the conversation had to end because their real opponents had arrived, then withdrew from Chen Ran's No-Distance. In the outside space, Chen Yang opened his eyes while occupying Zhang Fan's body, with Chu Yun still collapsed nearby, and immediately ordered both of them to get up because the group outside was no longer something they could ignore while continuing to discuss their plans. Zhang Fan lit a cigarette and walked over to Chen Yang, remarking that he had already warned him the plan was unreliable and that they had nevertheless been discovered. This reaction showed that Zhang Fan had understood the possibility of interception in advance, even if he had accepted the plan because it offered a chance to escape the Ninth True Self Player's control. Chu Yun, after getting up and stretching the body he had just occupied, said that he had encountered no resistance when possessing this person and asked whether the host was one of Chen Yang's fanatical believers. Chen Yang rejected that explanation and said that the host was repaying a debt of gratitude, which distinguished deliberate cooperation from obedience produced by fanaticism. The three then stood together, smoking and looking toward one point in the distance, because each could sense three powerful spirits waiting outside the instance with the patience of predators waiting for their prey; Chen Yang's hope that An Sheng would not be among them also showed that he considered An Sheng a particularly dangerous possibility within the approaching group.

Their Liar Killer panels then showed that the time limit on Chen Ran's Eternal Kingdom ban had expired, and the three exchanged glances before immediately disappearing from the Secret Chamber and reappearing in an unnamed space. The timing mattered because they acted as soon as the displayed restriction ended rather than remaining in the chamber to test whether their freedom had been restored in practice. Three figures were already waiting for them. The first was a boy who looked about eleven or twelve years old, despite emitting mental fluctuations at the Superego level, and he announced that the Whisperer Alliance Leader had ordered the arrest of Chen Yang, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi as cross-realm smugglers, while offering to spare their lives if they surrendered. His voice made the three dizzy and gave them the sensation that they were about to fall into an illusion, showing that he was not merely a messenger delivering an order but a combatant whose speech itself exerted a mental effect. The second figure was a noble-looking youth in a long robe, carrying a folding fan and dressed in a manner associated with the Ming Dynasty; his sharp eyebrows, bright eyes, and imposing bearing were matched by another set of Superego-level mental fluctuations. He issued a parallel declaration on behalf of the Liar Killer Alliance Leader, saying that he had come to apprehend them and that resistance would be answered with lethal force. 

The presence of one representative from each alliance established that the pursuit was coordinated at the highest level of both organizations rather than being a unilateral operation by one side. The third figure, standing between the two youths, then turned around and revealed a face identical to An Sheng's, while the mental pressure coming from him exceeded that of either person at his sides. This was a Nine-Star An Sheng. Zhang Fan's later complaint about a Five-Star Chen Yang facing three Superego Players does not contradict An Sheng's Nine-Star rank, because Star level and state-of-mind attainment describe different aspects of cultivation; the danger lay in having to face two Superego-level enforcers and an even stronger Nine-Star opponent at the same time. The lineup was therefore not merely a formal arrest party, but a force assembled to stop the three from using their skills to escape or establish themselves on the true timeline.

Zhang Fan responded by raising his middle finger, because the scale of the lineup exposed how little protection the arrangement had actually given them. The transaction had allowed Chen Yang a chance to remain on the true timeline, but it had not given Zhang Fan and Ling Chi permission to do the same, so the three of them had violated the agreed boundary by attempting to stay together. The arrival of the two alliance representatives was therefore consistent with the punishment that should follow the breach, but a Nine-Star An Sheng was more than they had expected. His complaint about a Five-Star Chen Yang being made to face three Superego Players reflected that mismatch, while An Sheng's Nine-Star rank meant the most formidable of the three was not simply another opponent at the same tier. Chen Yang's chance to remain was consequently not a safe exemption from the conflict, because it still depended on surviving the opposition created by the plan itself. An Sheng appeared to understand the question raised by their expressions and explained that he had received a strong premonition that the three would try to possess his teammates, which was why he had come in person. Their usual method could have been to use their skills to take control of the available hosts while keeping An Sheng occupied, allowing them to exploit the gap between the person fighting them and the body they needed in order to establish themselves on the true timeline. That approach was no longer reliable, however, because the trio could sense that the skills possessed by the boy and the Ming-dynasty youth were probably selected specifically to counter their own abilities.

If the two accompanying figures could neutralize the possession or skill-based maneuvers on which Chen Yang, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi depended, then the trio could not simply concentrate on restraining An Sheng and assume that the rest of the plan would work. The fact that An Sheng had brought both figures was itself evidence that he had prepared for their likely response rather than relying on his own strength alone; otherwise, the three opponents would not have needed this particular combination of abilities to stop the trio. With all six people facing one another, An Sheng threw away his cigarette and declared that their path was closed, directly naming Ling Chi, Chen Yang, and Zhang Fan. He then released his World of the Heart, which descended over the entire group and enclosed everyone present within it. This action turned the confrontation from an arrest order and a standoff into an immediate contest over the battlefield itself: instead of attacking one person first or allowing the trio time to negotiate, An Sheng imposed his own world on all of them at once. 

The scene does not establish the result of that clash, but it does establish that the trio's attempt to enter and remain on the true timeline had drawn a response from the two alliances and from An Sheng personally, and that their opponents had arranged their abilities to obstruct the very methods the trio would most naturally use to escape. After Chen Yang left Chen Ran's No-Distance, another person appeared there and asked why Chen Ran had not killed him. Chen Ran answered by explaining that the principle called 'Lose-Lose is greater than a Single-Win' could be reduced to a particular kind of resentment: when someone sees another person gaining more, he would rather lose as well than allow the other person to profit. The questioner was judging the decision through that mindset and therefore could not see any benefit in allowing Chen Yang, Zhang Fan, and Ling Chi to remain on the true timeline.

Chen Ran's response was not that their continued existence was harmless, but that a decision had to be assessed according to what it made possible as well as what it allowed an opponent to gain; refusing an outcome solely because another side might benefit could sacrifice a much larger opportunity. The opportunity depended on An Sheng's obsession with war. Because he wanted to break the blockade imposed by Unity of Heaven and Man, the three True Self Players remaining on the true timeline could become important if that blockade were ever removed. Chen Ran reasoned that, once the restriction was broken, people with the potential of Chen Yang, Ling Chi, and Zhang Fan could advance to Half-Step True Self rather than remaining limited by their current positions. Their roles would also allow their systems and followers to develop in parallel: Chen Yang would organize the Underworld, Ling Chi would organize the Death Row Inmates, and Zhang Fan would plant the Dao Heart Demonic Seed. Adding an increasingly restless An Sheng to those three developments would create a situation in which the Eighteenth Floor could be destabilized and the conflict could expand into a war against the two Alliances. The significance of that war would not be limited to the survival of the Underworld, the Death Row Inmates, or Zhang Fan's influence; for the True Self Players, it could become a struggle over the momentum and destiny of the Ultimate Battle itself. The other person gradually understood the implication and articulated it as a question: once the four had developed enough strength, their conflict could disrupt the Eighteenth Floor and lead to war against the two Alliances, while the True Self Players would be using that war to compete over the direction of the Ultimate Battle. Chen Ran confirmed the deduction, but he also distinguished the motives of the different parties involved.

From Chen Yang's, Ling Chi's, and Zhang Fan's perspective, refusing to take a risk would leave them as pawns controlled by the Ninth True Self Player, so staying on the true timeline was a gamble against that control. The Trio on the River of Time also had a reason to allow the arrangement, because they needed forces capable of testing the foundations of the two Alliances. The Omniscient and Omnipotent, however, had a different incentive: the Underworld, the Death Row Inmates, and the Dao Heart Demonic Seed associated with Nine-Star Zhang Fan were all dangerous precisely because they could remain concealed in the shadows, protected by the stone-pillar rules or by common sense. From their perspective, it would be preferable for these threats to unite and reveal themselves voluntarily, allowing the two Alliances to eliminate them together rather than having to find and confront each one separately.

An Sheng remained the uncontrolled variable in this arrangement, so none of the parties could assume that the outcome would follow the structure they had predicted. Chen Ran gave the possibility of learning other systems and killing Chen Yang as an example: if he acquired enough power to kill his brother in a counterattack, then the plans built around Chen Yang's continued existence would collapse immediately. That possibility mattered because the competing sides were not operating from a complete view of the future; each was making decisions using the portion of the structure it could perceive, while the actions of the other participants could alter the conditions on which its calculations depended. The fact that several factions could temporarily benefit from the same arrangement did not mean that their interests were identical or that their predictions would remain correct.

Their incentives overlapped only while the relevant players, systems, and constraints remained in place, so any change to those variables could reverse the expected result. When the other person asked about his next plans, Chen Ran did not answer and instead exited No-Distance. The physical consequence of the earlier struggle became apparent at once: his legs gave way and he collapsed onto the floor, forcing him to switch states quickly. He attempted to change into the Half-Step Super-Self state, but his head struck the floor hard enough that he immediately switched back to the Ego Extreme Realm. His mental strength had been crippled across all three states by Chen Yang, so the fact that he had survived the confrontation and continued reasoning about the larger conflict did not mean that he had recovered enough to move normally or use his systems without consequences. He then examined his teammates and finally focused on Han Fei, whose Black Lotus had been crushed by the True Self Players on the River of Time; Chen Ran therefore judged that Han Fei should now be free of Zhang Fan's influence, which removed a significant reason to avoid bringing him closer to the team. Chen Ran already had a good impression of Han Fei and considered inviting him to join the team after the instance ended, but he recognized that Han Fei's skills overlapped with Eternal Kingdom.

That overlap was not simply a reason to reject him, because Eternal Kingdom would become harder for Chen Ran to use freely once he reached Seven-Star: at that level it could break through the boundary of an instance, making its activation consequential beyond the immediate battlefield. Chen Ran would therefore have reason to avoid using the skill casually even when it would otherwise be useful. Han Fei's skills, combined with Jiang Zhe's, could produce a weaker version of Eternal Kingdom, giving the team another way to obtain a similar effect without requiring Chen Ran to activate his own ability every time. The timing made the recruitment particularly useful: just as Chen Ran expected his own skill to become too dangerous to employ without careful consideration, the combination of Han Fei's and Jiang Zhe's abilities offered a substitute that could preserve some of its function while reducing the need to expose Eternal Kingdom.
